records.l: RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, opening
records.s: This unit concerns automatic commit message generation and the RACE (Retrieval-Augmented Commit mEssage generation) model proposed to improve it. RACE retrieves a semantically similar code diff and its commit message, then uses an exemplar guider to help a neural model generate informative and readable commit messages while reducing the impact of irrelevant retrieved information. Evaluated on the MCMD dataset across Java, C#, C++, Python, and JavaScript, RACE outperforms 11 state-of-the-art approaches on BLEU, Meteor, Rouge-L, and CIDEr. RACE also improves four existing neural models, including NMTGen, CommitBERT, CodeT5-small, and CodeT5-base.

records.l: commit message generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, opening
records.s: Commit message generation is presented as an important task because developers often lack the time, motivation, or experience to write concise and informative messages. Existing rule-based, information-retrieval, and Seq2Seq approaches have limitations, while RACE improves generation performance and readability.

records.l: commit message, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, opening

records.l: RACE, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, opening
records.s: RACE is a model that retrieves a similar code diff paired with a commit message and uses that commit message as an exemplar for neural commit message generation. Its exemplar guider learns the semantic similarity between the retrieved and current code diffs and uses the exemplar accordingly. Experiments show that RACE outperforms existing approaches and improves several Seq2Seq models.

The framework is applied to NMTGen, CommitBERT, CodeT5-small, and CodeT5-base, substantially improving their performance.

records.l: RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: The unit reviews code intelligence methods for software engineering, focusing on commit message generation from code diffs. It describes information retrieval methods such as ChangeDoc and NNGen, neural-based approaches such as NMTGen, CommitGen, CoDiSum, PtrGNCMsg, and CommitBERT, and hybrid methods including ATOM and CoRec. The unit explains that ATOM and CoRec combine retrieval with neural generation but do not fully exploit retrieved results. It presents exemplar-based commit message generation as an approach that trains a model to use retrieved similar commits to improve generation.

records.l: code intelligence, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: Code intelligence uses machine learning, especially deep learning-based methods, to understand source code. It has produced promising results in tasks including code summarization, code search, and commit message generation.

records.l: commit message generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work

records.l: information retrieval, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: Information retrieval techniques have been applied to commit message generation by finding similar code diffs and reusing their commit messages. ChangeDoc uses syntax or semantic similarity, while NNGen retrieves candidates using cosine similarity between bag-of-words vectors and selects among them using BLEU scores.

records.l: neural network-based approaches, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: Neural-based approaches learn code-diff semantics and translate code diffs into commit messages. They include Seq2Seq models, models incorporating code structure and semantics, pointer-generator networks for out-of-vocabulary words, and Transformer-based decoders.

records.l: CommitBERT, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: CommitBERT uses CodeBERT to learn semantic representations of code diffs and employs a Transformer-based decoder to generate commit messages.

records.l: CodeBERT, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work

records.l: retrieval-augmented generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: Introducing retrieved relevant results into the training process has been found useful in many generation tasks. In commit message generation, hybrid approaches combine retrieval with neural generation, although the reviewed methods do not fully exploit retrieved results.

records.l: ATOM, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: ATOM ensembles a neural-based model and an information retrieval technique through hybrid ranking. It encodes AST paths with BiLSTM, generates commit messages with a decoder, retrieves messages using TF-IDF and cosine similarity, and prioritizes generated and retrieved messages with a hybrid ranking module. It does not learn to refine the retrieved or generated results.

records.l: CoRec, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: CoRec uses retrieval only during inference. It retrieves the most similar training code diff with a trained encoder, combines probability distributions from decoders processing the input and retrieved diffs, and generates the final message step by step. It is not trained to utilize information from retrieval results.

records.l: exemplar-based commit message generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: The approach in this unit treats a retrieved similar commit as an exemplar. It trains the model to leverage the exemplar to enhance commit message generation.

records.l: code diff, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: Code diffs are used as the input for commit message generation and are represented through syntax, semantics, bag-of-words vectors, TF-IDF vectors, AST paths, or learned semantic representations. Retrieval-based methods compare code diffs to find similar examples.

records.l: commit message, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Related Work
records.s: Commit messages are generated from code diffs or reused from similar commits. Retrieval-based methods can reuse messages that are usually readable and understandable.

records.l: RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: RACE is a two-module approach for generating understandable and concise commit messages from code diffs. Its retrieval module uses a trained code diff encoder and cosine similarity to find a semantically similar code diff and paired commit message from a large parallel training corpus. Its generation module encodes the input code diff, retrieved code diff, and retrieved commit message, then uses an exemplar guider to weight their representations before a Transformer-based decoder generates the commit message. The encoder is trained with an encoder-decoder neural network on about 0.9 million code diff and commit message pairs.

records.l: RACE, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: RACE consists of a retrieval module and a generation module. It retrieves a semantically similar code diff and commit message, then uses the retrieved commit message to guide commit message generation.

records.l: retrieval module, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: The retrieval module trains a code diff encoder with a commit message generator, maps code diffs into a high-dimensional semantic space, and retrieves the most similar code diff and paired commit message from a large parallel training corpus. It uses the second-ranked result for code diffs in the training dataset because the first-ranked result is the code diff itself.

records.l: generation module, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: The generation module uses three Transformer-based encoders, an exemplar guider, and a decoder. It combines representations of the input code diff and retrieved information to generate a commit message.

records.l: code diff, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: A code diff is encoded into contextual representations and a pooled semantic vector. Its semantic similarity to another code diff is used for retrieval and for guiding generation.

records.l: commit message, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: A commit message is paired with a code diff in the training corpus and can be retrieved as an exemplar. The generation module produces a commit message token by token using cross-entropy training.

records.l: large parallel training corpus, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: The large parallel training corpus contains paired code diffs and commit messages. The retrieval module searches this corpus for the most semantically similar code diff and its paired commit message.

records.l: commit message generation dataset, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: The commit message generation dataset contains about 0.9 million code diff and commit message pairs. It is used to train the encoder-decoder neural network.

records.l: neural network-based approaches, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: The encoder-decoder neural network is trained on the commit message generation dataset to learn code diff semantics and generate commit messages. Cross-entropy is used as its loss function and AdamW is used for optimization.

records.l: code diff encoder, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: The code diff encoder is trained with a commit message generator to learn semantic representations of code diffs. Its output is mean-pooled into semantic vectors used for cosine-similarity retrieval.

records.l: Transformer, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: Transformer-based encoders are used to capture long-range dependencies and contextual information in code diffs. Their layers include multi-head self-attention, relative position embeddings, feed-forward networks, and add-and-norm operations.

records.l: decoder, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: The Transformer-based decoder generates commit messages step by step from the combined input encoding. It uses masked self-attention, cross-attention, feed-forward networks, and a final MLP with softmax to produce token probabilities.

records.l: exemplar guider, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: The exemplar guider learns a semantic similarity value between the input code diff and the retrieved code diff. It uses this value to weight the input code diff and retrieved commit message representations before decoding.

records.l: retrieved similar commit message, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: The retrieved commit message is treated as an exemplar for generation. Because it may inaccurately describe the input code diff, the exemplar guider controls how much of its information is used.

records.l: cosine similarity, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: Cosine similarity measures the similarity between pooled semantic vectors produced by the code diff encoder. The retrieval module uses it to rank candidate code diffs in the large parallel training corpus.

records.l: semantic similarity, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Proposed Approach / Retrieval module .. Generation module
records.s: Semantic similarity between code diffs is represented through encoder outputs and their mean-pooled vectors. The generation module also learns a similarity value between the input and retrieved code diffs with a sigmoid-based exemplar guider.

records.l: RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: This unit describes the experimental setup for evaluating RACE on the MCMD commit-message generation dataset. MCMD contains 450,000 sampled commits for each of Java, C#, C++, Python, and JavaScript, with further filtering for multi-file and unparsable files. Code diffs are converted into token-level change actions, and CodeT5-base initializes the encoders and decoder. Generated commit messages are evaluated with BLEU, Meteor, Rouge-L, and Cider, using multiple neural, information-retrieval, hybrid, and pre-trained baselines.

records.l: MCMD, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: MCMD is a large-scale dataset containing commits from the top-100 starred GitHub repositories for Java, C#, C++, Python, and JavaScript. It retains 450,000 randomly sampled commits per programming language after filtering redundant and noisy messages, and the study further filters out multi-file commits and files that cannot be parsed.

records.l: commits, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: The commits in MCMD contain code diffs, commit messages, repository names, timestamps, and other information. The study excludes commits involving multiple files or files that cannot be parsed.

records.l: code diff, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: The code diff is originally represented at the line level in MCMD. The study converts it into a sequence of token-level change actions and limits its maximum length to 200.

records.l: commit message, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: Commit messages are used as the generated output and are limited to a maximum length of 50. Their quality is evaluated with BLEU, Meteor, Rouge-L, and Cider.

records.l: token-level change actions, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: Token-level change actions represent code changes using keep, insert, delete, and replace operations. Each action contains a span of tokens, and replace is extended into replace_old and replace_new to distinguish old and new token spans; difflib is used to extract the action sequence.

records.l: CodeT5-base, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: CodeT5-base supplies the encoder weights used to initialize the code diff encoders and the decoder used in the model. Its original vocabulary is expanded with nine special tokens for the token-level change actions, producing a vocabulary size of 32,109.

records.l: BLEU, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: BLEU is one of the four metrics used to evaluate generated commit messages. The study reports B-Norm, a BLEU variant selected because it correlates most with human perception according to Tao et al. (2021).

records.l: Meteor, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: Meteor is used to evaluate the quality of generated commit messages.

records.l: Rouge-L, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: Rouge-L is used to evaluate the quality of generated commit messages.

records.l: Cider, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: Cider is used to evaluate the quality of generated commit messages.

records.l: B-Norm, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: B-Norm is the BLEU result reported in the study. It is selected from BLEU variants because it correlates most closely with human perception according to Tao et al. (2021).

records.l: RACE, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: RACE is compared with end-to-end neural, information-retrieval, hybrid, and pre-trained models on the commit message generation task. The experiments are run three times with random seeds 0, 1, and 2, and the reported results use the mean value.

records.l: CommitBERT, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: CommitBERT is included as one of the pre-trained baselines and is fine-tuned on the MCMD commit message generation dataset.

records.l: CodeT5-small, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Setup / Dataset .. Evaluation metrics / Baselines
records.s: CodeT5-small is included as a pre-trained baseline and is fine-tuned on MCMD. It is described as a source code pre-trained model used for comparison.

records.l: RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: This unit evaluates RACE against 11 baseline approaches for commit-message generation across Java, C#, C++, Python, and JavaScript using BLEU, Meteor, Rouge-L, and Cider. RACE achieves the best results across all five programming languages and all four metrics, while its exemplar guider improves performance over an ablated version. Experiments show that performance remains generally stable when retrieving between 1 and 9 relevant commits. Applying the framework improves four existing Seq2Seq models, with reported gains ranging from 7% to 73%.

records.l: RACE, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: RACE outperforms all evaluated approaches on Java, C#, C++, Python, and JavaScript across BLEU, Meteor, Rouge-L, and Cider. Its exemplar guider improves results over RACE without the guider, and the framework also improves NMTGen, CommitBERT, CodeT5-small, and CodeT5-base.

records.l: baseline approaches, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: The baseline approaches include two IR-based approaches, four end-to-end neural models, two hybrid approaches, and three pre-trained-based approaches. RACE performs best among them across all five programming languages and four evaluation metrics.

records.l: information retrieval, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: IR-based approaches generally outperform end-to-end neural models on average, indicating that retrieved similar results provide important information for commit-message generation. NNGen and Lucene are the two IR-based approaches evaluated.

records.l: neural network-based approaches, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: End-to-end neural models generally perform worse than IR-based approaches on average across the four metrics. The evaluated models are CommitGen, CoDiSum, NMTGen, and PtrGNCMsg.

records.l: pre-trained-based approaches, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: Pre-trained-based approaches outperform the other baseline categories on average across the four metrics. CodeT5-base performs best among the evaluated pre-trained-based approaches before applying RACE.

records.l: NNGen, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: NNGen generally outperforms Lucene and the end-to-end neural models in the reported comparisons. Its retrieved message in the example is semantically similar but incorrectly includes the extra information "Revert."

records.l: Lucene, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: Lucene is an IR-based baseline that generally performs below NNGen. Its retrieved message in the example also contains the relevant meaning "Filter out unavailable databases" but incorrectly includes "Revert."

records.l: NMTGen, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: NMTGen is an end-to-end neural baseline and one of the models enhanced by the RACE framework. RACE improves its BLEU performance by more than 20% on every programming language and boosts its average BLEU, Meteor, Rouge-L, and Cider results by 43%, 49%, 33%, and 61%, respectively.

records.l: CommitBERT, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: CommitBERT is a pre-trained baseline that is also adapted to the RACE framework. Its average improvements from the framework are 11% in BLEU, 9% in Meteor, 11% in Rouge-L, and 12% in Cider.

records.l: CodeT5-small, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: CodeT5-small is a pre-trained baseline that performs below CodeT5-base among the pre-trained approaches. When enhanced with RACE, it receives average gains of 15% in BLEU, 14% in Meteor, 11% in Rouge-L, and 26% in Cider.

records.l: CodeT5-base, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: CodeT5-base performs best among the pre-trained baselines on average before RACE is applied. The RACE framework improves its average BLEU, Meteor, Rouge-L, and Cider results by 16%, 10%, 8%, and 32%, respectively.

records.l: Java, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: On Java, RACE obtains 25.66 BLEU, 15.46 Meteor, 32.02 Rouge-L, and 1.76 Cider, exceeding the evaluated baselines on all four metrics.

records.l: C#, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: On C#, RACE obtains 26.33 BLEU, 16.37 Meteor, 31.31 Rouge-L, and 1.84 Cider, exceeding the evaluated baselines on all four metrics.

records.l: C++, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: On C++, RACE obtains 19.13 BLEU, 12.55 Meteor, 24.52 Rouge-L, and 1.14 Cider, exceeding the evaluated baselines on all four metrics.

records.l: Python, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: On Python, RACE obtains 21.79 BLEU, 14.68 Meteor, 28.35 Rouge-L, and 1.40 Cider, exceeding the evaluated baselines on all four metrics.

records.l: JavaScript, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: On JavaScript, RACE obtains 25.55 BLEU, 16.31 Meteor, 31.79 Rouge-L, and 1.84 Cider, exceeding the evaluated baselines on all four metrics.

records.l: BLEU, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: BLEU is one of the four metrics used to evaluate commit-message generation. RACE achieves the highest BLEU score among the compared approaches for each of the five programming languages, and its framework improves the average BLEU scores of the four adapted models.

records.l: retrieved similar commit, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: RACE treats a retrieved similar commit message as an exemplar rather than directly using it as the final output. The exemplar guides the neural model toward the correct message while avoiding extra or incorrect information in the retrieved result.

records.l: code diff, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: The code diff is used to retrieve relevant commits through cosine similarity between semantic vectors. It is also encoded together with similar code diffs and similar commit messages in the generation module.

records.l: commit message generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Experimental Results / How does RACE perform compared with .. 5.4
records.s: The experiments concern commit-message generation from code diffs. They show that retrieved information can improve generation and that RACE can enhance existing Seq2Seq models, with reported improvements ranging from 7% to 73%.

records.l: RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, 5.5
records.s: The human evaluation assesses the semantic similarity of commit messages generated by RACE, NNGen, NMTGen, CommitBERT, and CoRec. Four volunteers with excellent English ability and more than three years of software development experience scored 250 code diff–commit message pairs from 50 randomly selected test-set code diffs. They rated each pair on Informativeness, Conciseness, and Expressiveness using scores from 0 to 4. RACE outperformed the four baselines on all three aspects, with high evaluator agreement and statistically significant improvements according to Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

records.l: human evaluation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, 5.5
records.s: Human evaluation measures the semantic similarity of commit messages generated by RACE and four baselines: NNGen, NMTGen, CommitBERT, and CoRec. It uses ratings from four volunteers across Informativeness, Conciseness, and Expressiveness.

records.l: RACE, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, 5.5
records.s: RACE generates commit messages that score higher than NNGen, NMTGen, CommitBERT, and CoRec in Informativeness, Conciseness, and Expressiveness. Its improvements over the other approaches are statistically significant according to Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

records.s: Generated commit messages from RACE, NNGen, NMTGen, CommitBERT, and CoRec are evaluated for semantic similarity to their code diffs. The messages receive scores from 0 to 4 for Informativeness, Conciseness, and Expressiveness.

records.s: Four volunteers with excellent English ability and more than three years of software development experience evaluate every code diff–commit message pair. Their scores are averaged to produce the final score for each pair.

records.s: Informativeness measures the amount of important information about the code diff reflected in a commit message. RACE performs better than the other approaches on this aspect.

records.l: Conciseness, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, 5.5
records.s: Conciseness measures the extent of extraneous information included in a commit message. RACE performs better than the other approaches on this aspect.

records.l: Expressiveness, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, 5.5
records.s: Expressiveness measures grammaticality and fluency. RACE performs better than the other approaches on this aspect.

records.l: semantic similarity, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, 5.5
records.s: Semantic similarity is the target of the human evaluation of generated commit messages. The evaluation indicates that RACE produces messages with more comprehensive semantics than the four baselines.

records.l: Krippendorff’s alpha, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, 5.5
records.s: Krippendorff’s alpha is calculated to verify agreement among the volunteers. Its value is 0.90, indicating a high degree of agreement and reliable scores.

records.l: Kendall’s Tau, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, 5.5
records.s: Kendall’s Tau is calculated pairwise among the four volunteers to assess agreement. The pairwise values range from 0.73 to 0.95, indicating high agreement.

records.l: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, 5.5
records.s: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests are used to confirm the superiority of RACE in the human evaluation. The improvements of RACE over the other approaches are statistically significant, with all p-values below 0.05 at the 95% confidence level.

records.l: RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Conclusion .. Limitations
records.s: The paper proposes a retrieval-augmented neural commit message generation method that uses a retrieved similar commit message as an exemplar to guide generation. Experiments show that the method outperforms recent baselines and significantly improves four neural network models. The study is limited by its evaluation on five programming languages, dependence on a code base, approximately 35 hours of training time, and truncation of code diffs longer than 512 tokens.

records.l: retrieval-augmented neural commit message generation method, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Conclusion .. Limitations
records.s: The method retrieves a similar commit message and uses it as an exemplar to guide a neural network in generating an accurate and readable commit message. It outperforms recent baselines and significantly boosts the performance of four neural network models.

records.l: commit message, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Conclusion .. Limitations
records.s: The commit message is generated to be accurate and readable, with a retrieved similar commit message serving as an exemplar.

records.l: retrieved similar commit message, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Conclusion .. Limitations
records.s: The retrieved similar commit message is used as an exemplar to guide the neural network model during commit message generation.

records.l: neural network-based approaches, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Conclusion .. Limitations
records.s: Four neural network models receive significant performance improvements from the proposed framework.

records.l: programming languages, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Conclusion .. Limitations
records.s: The experiments cover five programming languages. The paper notes that models perform differently across programming languages and that further experiments are needed to confirm the framework's generality.

records.l: code base, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Conclusion .. Limitations
records.s: The method requires a code base from which it retrieves the most similar example. This requirement is identified as a limitation inherited from information-retrieval-based techniques.

records.l: training time, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Conclusion .. Limitations
records.s: The model takes about 35 hours to train because it retrieves similar diffs and encodes them in addition to modeling the input code diffs.

records.l: code diff, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation, Conclusion .. Limitations
records.s: The model retrieves and encodes similar code diffs. Diffs longer than 512 tokens are truncated, which can cause information loss because longer diffs may contain more complex semantics or behaviors.

records.l: The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: This is a sequence of diary records from June through August 1661, centred on Samuel Pepys’s naval, household, family, financial, and social life. Early in June, Pepys works with Sir W. Pen and the Navy Office to inspect and prepare ships at Woolwich and Deptford for an impending voyage. My Lord prepares to go to Algier and Lisbone, entrusting Pepys with preparation work; meanwhile the Office faces an acute lack of money and collapsing credit, with suppliers demanding personal security. Pepys reports these difficulties to the Duke of York, obtains funds and ammunition, and arranges cloth and other provisions for my Lord before seeing him sail from Deptford. Alongside official business, Pepys pursues prospects connected with the Wardrobe, where my Lord suggests he may become Mr. Townsend’s deputy and promises his father first refusal of Mr. Young’s place. He improves his house, oversees painted stairs, buys household goods, begins singing lessons, and frequently visits churches, theatres, taverns, family, and acquaintances. His wife is intermittently unwell, while Pepys takes pleasure in his cleaner home, music, plays including “Bartholomew Fayre,” “The Siege of Rhodes,” and “Claracilla,” and social outings. In July, the death of uncle Robert draws Pepys to Brampton. With his father, he arranges the burial, reads the will, sorts papers, and discovers a less secure and more disordered estate than expected. Copyhold documents are missing, Tom Trice files a caveat for his mother, and Pepys consults relatives, tenants, Sir Robert Bernard, Mr. Moore, Roger Pepys, and others. A later agreement asks Pepys’s aunt to leave the house for £10, but wider claims remain for the law, leaving him worried that debts and disputes will diminish the inheritance. August continues these family and legal concerns while Pepys returns to London work, Privy Seal affairs, and negotiations to add Sir R. Ford’s house to the Office for £200 yearly. He considers Tom’s marriage, worries over his father’s finances and Balty, and notes deaths and mourning in the family. Public and naval anxieties persist: the Office’s bills sell at losses, money is scarce, and strange fatal fevers make the season sickly. Pepys also follows Lord Hinchingbroke’s illness and Lord Sandwich’s fever at Alicante, both of whom improve. The period ends with Pepys conscious of debt, pleasure-seeking, Court disorder, and clerical conduct.

records.l: Sir W. Batten, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Sir W. Batten is a Navy Office official, husband of Lady Batten, associated with a house and a baboon brought from Guiny by Captain Holmes. After travelling from Chatham, he socializes closely with Pepys at dinners, church, and his house, then joins Pepys and Sir W. Pen in reporting the Navy’s lack of money to the Duke of York.

records.l: Sir W. Pen, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Sir W. Pen is a Navy Office official who inspects ships at Woolwich and Deptford and gives readiness orders. He joins Pepys and Sir W. Batten in reporting Navy finances to the Duke of York, while also sharing outings: travel, wrestling at Moorefields, bowling, theatre-going, and visits to the Dolphin.

records.l: Lord Sandwich, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Lord Sandwich is a lord, the diarist’s patron or superior, and Master of Trinity House, with responsibility for Wardrobe business. Before leaving, he places great confidence in the diarist: Mr. Townsend is to explain the Wardrobe administration, and the diarist is to become Townsend’s deputy if Townsend dies. He also proposes that the diarist and Mr. Moore manage the business if necessary, promises the diarist first refusal of Mr. Young’s place if vacant, and entrusts him with a major preparation during his absence. Preparing for a voyage to Algier to settle business and order the fleet, followed by a return to Lisbone with three ships, he obtains ammunition, requires £300 in cloth for presents among the Turks in Barbary, receives the cloth, travels to Deptford, boards a Dutch yacht, and sails after taking leave of the King and friends. While at sea, he falls sick ashore at Alicante, alarming the diarist because of his health and family. Reports say his pain and fever ease; he later writes that he has recovered, remains at Alicante, and expects to proceed toward Portugal, while concern remains over £5,000 intended for his departure.

records.l: Mr. Townsend, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Mr. Townsend holds and administers the Wardrobe under my Lord, ordered to reveal the mystery only to the diarist; he makes the diarist deputy should he die during my Lord's absence.

records.l: Mr. Moore, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Mr. Moore is a legal adviser and Privy Seal colleague of Samuel Pepys. He advises on the Pepys family will, explaining that its legatee-witnesses do not invalidate it, then reviews it further with Pepys. He also handles Seal-day business, reads bills for Lord Roberts, gives Pepys Hooker’s Ecclesiastical Polity, and socializes with him.

records.l: Mr. Creed, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Mr. Creed is ordered £300 for cloth, reports Lord Sandwich’s recovery, then receives a £10,000 voyage imprest and helps seek ammunition for my Lord’s ships.

records.l: the diarist's father, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The diarist’s father is a central family and business figure, assisting Samuel Pepys with the cloth business and helping choose scarlet, purple, and black cloth and linen. When a letter reports that Robert is seriously ill and needs help with his business, he prepares to go to him and considers advice about a proposed land purchase. After Robert’s death, he and the diarist work at Brampton through Robert’s will, property, and papers, trying to put the estate in order: letting the crop, arranging for Stankes to manage the business, and discussing the will with the Trices and others. He remains alone at Brampton after the diarist returns to London, while there is concern that he may profit from his London house rather than leave it to Tom. Later he is found well, travels between Brampton and London, and joins the diarist in dealings with Thomas Trice, Dr. Williams, and Mrs. Whately’s household, including examination and proof of the uncle’s will and discussion of a possible marriage for Tom. He notices the diarist drinking, an unfamiliar sight to him. In family matters, he helps confront Pall and agrees she should go into the country with the diarist’s mother. His finances appear precarious: £45 is owed to him, about £45 is owed by him, and this is said to be all his money due in the world.

records.l: Lord Hinchingbroke, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Lord Hinchingbroke, Lady Sandwich’s son, becomes gravely ill and is feared to have smallpox, then steadily improves until sitting up and walking about his chamber.

records.l: Tom, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Tom, the diarist’s brother and executor, is responsible for their father’s trade. In August 1661 he visits the diarist, hosts family and ladies at dinner, and becomes the subject of marriage discussions, including women of property and the daughters of a broker and Mr. Evans.

records.l: Lord Crew, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Lord Crew, accompanied by his lady, hosts the narrator warmly, temporarily resides with Sir H. Wright, and advocates naval service as honorable as land war.

records.l: the Wardrobe, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The Wardrobe was the subject of my Lord’s instructions to the diarist concerning its management during his absence. My Lord proposed joining the diarist and Mr. Moore in its business if Mr. Townsend died, and promised the diarist first refusal of Mr. Young’s place for his father if it became vacant. The diarist visits the Wardrobe, where he dines with my Lady and is kindly treated. He later brings his wife there to dine, and she is received with considerable attention.

records.l: Whitehall, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Whitehall is a place repeatedly visited by the diarist and speaker: they seek my Lord, meet Dean Fuller and the Duke of York, and see the Portuguese Embassador take leave of the King. Pepys waits for Lord Roberts at the Privy Seal, then goes with him to his chamber over the gate.

records.l: the Navy Office, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The Navy Office is an office that occupies a house under an agreed arrangement. In June–August 1661, the diarist repeatedly attends it for official business while it considers nearby lodgings. Facing a sad lack of money that prevents its men from serving further, it agrees to write to the Duke of York. It also secures Sir R. Ford’s house for its quarters at £200 per year.

records.l: the voyage, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The voyage receives imprest funding for my Lord and Mr. Creed, while the diarist and others inspect ships and prepare them to depart.

records.l: the Wardrobe business, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_a mystery [the whole mystery of the Wardrobe] The diarist is promised an important role in the Wardrobe administration: my Lord intends to make him deputy to Mr. Townsend. Townsend is to explain the administration's whole mystery to him.

records.l: ships, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: On June 1, the diarist, Sir W. Pen, and Mr. Gauden went from ship to ship at Woolwich and Deptford to give orders and assess their readiness to go forth. The diarist and Mr. Creed later sought ammunition at the Tower for my Lord’s ships.

records.l: Lieutenant Lambert, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_a captain [newly appointed] Lieutenant Lambert has been made Captain of the Norwich. He takes the diarist by water to Greenwich, explains various matters concerning ships, and later accompanies him to Mr. Holland's house.

records.l: Lady Sandwich, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Lady Sandwich is a mother of Lord Hinchingbroke, Sidney, Oliver, John, and a newborn daughter, associated with the Wardrobe and Pepys’s home. Pepys first finds her household merry and well after returning to London. Later, she consults him over Lord Hinchingbroke’s illness and, fearing smallpox, sends her other three sons to his house before fetching them to dine with her. She is also mourning her brother, Mr. Saml. Crew, troubled by toothache, and managing poor housekeeping after my Lord’s departure.

records.l: the Theatre, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The Theatre is a house and performance venue. It presents Bartholomew Faire, admired as well acted though excessively profane and abusive, and Claracilla, also well acted. Once thronged, it becomes unusually empty after the Opera begins, ending with the diarist’s first viewing of Claracilla.

records.l: Bartholomew Faire, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Bartholomew Faire, a theatrical play, is performed at the Theatre; the diarist attends with Lady Batten, Mrs. Rebecca Allen, Mrs. Thompson, and others, praising its acting while finding it profane and abusive.

records.l: uncle Wight, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Uncle Wight, the narrator's uncle, advises on a Brampton purchase and has daily long fits of stupefaction. After merriment at the Mitre and offense over Brampton, he dines with the narrator and learns of uncle Robert's death.

records.l: uncle Robert, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Uncle Robert, the diarist’s uncle, suffers serious dizziness and episodic stupidity and speechlessness while his business needs the diarist’s father’s attention. He offers adjoining land for purchase. He dies on the 5th; the diarist goes to Brampton for the funeral and affairs, finding a reasonably supportive will but disappointing estate and papers.

records.l: uncle Robert's estate, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Uncle Robert's estate proved worth far less than expected; missing copyhold-land surrenders created legal difficulty, leading the family to seek Mr. Philips's advice.

records.l: the narrator's wife, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The narrator’s wife, Elizabeth Pepys, is Samuel Pepys’s spouse, active in household, family, and social life. She appears first dressed in a black silk gown laced with black gimp lace, looking very pretty as she walks with him to the Wardrobe and stays with my Lady. Her sore belly becomes serious enough for Dr. Williams to attend her. She travels with Pepys to Whitehall, helps with visits, reports the theft of their silver tankard, and gives him his linen for safekeeping. She visits and travels with relatives and acquaintances, including a Walthamstow visit, trips to Uncle Fenner’s and Aunt Wight’s, the Opera, and the Wardrobe; she also goes with Mr. Hater during his wife’s labour and is expected back from Brampton. Lady Batten and her daughter treat her coldly. Most urgently, she tearfully pleads for help for her brother Balty.

records.l: fleet, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Fleet is put in order at Algier, then follows the narrator's lord after his three-ship return to Lisbone, meeting him there.

records.l: my Lord Chancellor, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: My Lord Chancellor begins by directing preparations during the narrator's lord's absence, while facing political opposition from Duke of Buckingham and Lord Bristol.

records.l: Edward Montagu, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: gives_orders_concerning great preparation [during the narrator's lord's absence] Edward Montagu is to give the narrator orders concerning the great preparation during the narrator's lord's absence.

records.l: great preparation, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_a preparation [for the fleet] The great preparation is to be overseen by the narrator during the narrator's lord's absence, under orders from my Lord Chancellor and Edward Montagu.

records.l: Huntingdon, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Pepys travels to Huntingdon but finds that the judges have not arrived. He drinks there with Thomas Trice and Mr. Phillips before returning to Brampton.

records.l: the narrator's house, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Pepys’s house, cleaned after dirt and finished, becomes very clean and neat, greatly pleasing Pepys and pleasing his father on Midsummer-day.

records.l: Sir George Carteret, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Sir George Carteret is an office member who attends a meeting, helps approve a letter to the Duke of York on financial difficulties, and hosts invited officers for dinner at Deptford, without inviting Pepys.

records.l: Duke of York, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The Duke of York receives reports that the office lacks money, supplies, and credit, and meets the speaker and Sir Williams at Whitehall to identify why ships were not sent out. Troubled by the Navy’s financial crisis, he orders a report on the ships and travels on the King’s yacht.

records.l: money, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The office lacks money, and its men are not able to serve it more without some money.

records.l: the office's credit, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_brought_low a low level [so that suppliers require personal security] The office's credit has fallen so low that no one will sell it anything without personal security from those involved.

records.l: Samuel Pepys, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Samuel Pepys is a person and diarist whose records follow his work, family obligations, finances, household, health, and recreations. He serves in command as an office official at the Navy Office, handling business, letters, naval financial difficulties, sealing matters, and reports to the Duke of York alongside Sir W. Batten and Sir W. Pen. Early on, he arranges cloth for my Lord, accompanies him to Deptford, and later writes to him at sea. He recovers from a severe cold, improves his home with painted stairs, buys a chest of drawers and an Indian gown, keeps linen in his custody, and studies singing with Theodore Goodgroome. A central concern becomes his uncle’s estate: he examines the will, debts, property, surrenders, and papers, seeks advice from relatives and associates, helps prove the will, and fears the proceeds will be less than expected despite an anticipated £200 a year in land. Family anxieties include his parents’ discontent, concern that Tom Pepys may mishandle their father’s trade, arrangements for Pall and Jane, and efforts to protect Lady Sandwich’s younger sons during Lord Hinchingbroke’s illness and possible smallpox. Throughout, he borrows £40 from Sir William Batten, conducts household and legal accounts, and visits friends and family. He frequently attends the Theatre, Opera, plays, and social gatherings, eventually acknowledging that excessive spending and pleasure, especially playgoing, distract him from business and resolving to change. The records end with this self-criticism amid continuing family, household, and office responsibilities.

records.l: the cloth, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The cloth, valued at £300 for presents to the Turks in Barbary, is bought for my Lord: two pieces each of scarlet, purple, and black cloth, plus £50 in linen. Mr. Shaw offers the money, my Lord orders Mr. Creed to advance it through Alderman Backwell, and the diarist struggles to send it before it is lately sent to sea.

records.l: King Charles II, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: King Charles II travels by barge to adjourn Parliament amid pressure over Presbytery and dependence on the Lord Chancellor for policy and service; he later attends Sir William Davenant's Opera and excels at stag hunting.

records.l: garden stairs, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_finished finished [by the painters] The stairs are being painted by the diarist's workmen. The work is finished by the 20th and pleases the diarist greatly.

records.l: Dutch yacht, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_a yacht [Dutch] The Dutch yacht is boarded by my Lord and the narrator at Deptford. It waits while W. Howe brings my Lord's things, then sails from Erith after dinner.

records.l: the painters, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: paint the stairs The painters work on the diarist's stairs. Their progress causes the diarist some vexation because of delays, but they finish the work by the 20th, to his great content.

records.l: Brampton, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Brampton is the Pepys family estate, central to managing uncle Robert’s affairs after his death. Samuel Pepys travels there to join his father, remain through the burial and following week, sort papers, inspect lands, handle disputes and relatives, and arrange his aunt’s departure for £10. His father continues settling estate matters there before the mother arrives, while Samuel returns after visits to Yelling and Graveley and ultimately rides toward London.

records.l: a Margate Hoy, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_a vessel [from Margate] A Margate Hoy is hired to carry the cloth and related goods. The diarist sends the things aboard it late at night, hoping they will reach the Downs by the following night.

records.l: the cloth shipment, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The cloth shipment is delayed when the purser does not come and the Duke of York has departed, then is sent by a Margate Hoy to the Downs.

records.l: the diarist's illness, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The diarist's illness is a painful cold caused by playing in the water. He stays home, keeps warm, breaks wind, and gains relief; by the 19th he reports that he is very well again.

records.l: the painters' work, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: finishes the stairs [to the diarist's great content] The painters' work on the stairs is delayed and troubles the diarist for much of the 18th and 19th. It is completed on the 20th, leaving him greatly content.

records.l: aunt (uncle Robert's widow), The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The narrator found his aunt in bed in a condition he described as extremely dirty and unpleasant. He was repeatedly troubled by what he called her ugly and disagreeable humours during the week at Brampton.

records.l: Mr. Norbury, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: has_wife Mr. Norbury's wife Mr. Norbury discussed his wife's house and land at Brampton with the narrator over dinner.

records.l: Mr. Norbury's house and land at Brampton, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Mr. Norbury's wife's house and land at Brampton is too expensive for the narrator to buy, from learning of it onward.

records.l: Mrs. Frances Butler, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Mrs. Frances Butler, Monsieur L'Impertinent’s sister, is seen by Pepys at Graye’s Inn Walks as his greatest beauty.

records.l: Pall, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Pall, the diarist’s maidservant, is associated with Kate Joyce at a child’s christening, causes the diarist great trouble, is reprimanded for her conduct and high spirit, and is sent to stay with the diarist’s parents in the country.

records.l: Pepys's wife's illness, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: has_condition dangerous [as Elizabeth Pepys thinks] Pepys’s wife was unwell, and her sore belly was described as having become dangerous as she thought. Dr. Williams came to see her.

records.l: the Navy Office, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The Navy Office is a quiet workplace where Samuel Pepys returns to official business, takes pleasure in authority, and considers Tangier matters and adding Sir R. Ford’s house. With clerks at Tom Whitton’s burial, officials report severe financial losses to the Duke of York. Lack of money leaves the house addition uncertain because of division and rent-guarantee difficulties.

records.l: Sir Williams both, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Sir Williams both went by coach with the narrator, the narrator’s wife, and Mrs. Margarett Pen to Walthamstow on August 1.

records.l: the letter from the diarist's aunt, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The diarist's aunt writes that Robert is seriously unwell with dizziness and needs help with his business, prompting the diarist's father to plan visiting him.

records.l: Aunt Fenner, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: An aunt known for hypocritical tricks writes that Robert needs the father's help, nears death, and dies.

records.l: land, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_the_subject_of the land-purchase plan [intended acquisition] The diarist is considering buying land that would yield £50 per year. He proposes paying £600 immediately and £150 annually for the remainder.

records.l: the land-purchase plan, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: A proposed land purchase: the diarist has his father offer £600 immediately and £150 annually until completion, aiming for £50 annual income while appearing able to save more than his actual £500.

records.l: ships, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Ships' departure is delayed as contrary wind prevents them leaving the river while being made ready.

records.l: our old club, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Old club members meet the writer at the Bell at the Maypole, talking and drinking with much pleasure.

records.l: Mr. Chetwind, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Mr. Chetwind, formerly consumptive, becomes fat and sallow through habitual tobacco chewing and praises Hooker’s Ecclesiastical Polity as the best book and the only one that made him a Christian.

records.l: the Bell at the Maypole in the Strand, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The Bell at the Maypole in the Strand was the place where the writer met Mr. Chetwind, Gregory, Hartlibb, and Mr. Kipps for drinking and conversation.

records.l: Hooker's Ecclesiastical Polity, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: A book praised by Mr. Chetwind as the best and the only one that made him a Christian, prompting its purchase.

records.l: trade of briefs, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: A weekly Sunday trade of briefs becomes a constant practice until the writer and others resolve to give it no more.

records.l: Portuguese Embassador, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Portuguese Embassador comes to White Hall, takes leave of the King, and arranges the Queen’s overseas departure.

records.l: Queen, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The Portuguese Embassador was going to end all with the Queen and send her over. The speaker hoped to make up his expenses by helping prepare things to send with the next fleet to the Queen.

records.l: order to report on the ships, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: requests an account of the cause of the failure to send out the ships An order had been sent to the speaker and Sir Williams the previous day to give the Duke of York an account of where the fault lay in the ships not being sent out.

records.l: failure to send out the ships, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_caused_by wind against the ships [the stated sole cause] The failure to send out the ships was attributed solely to the wind being against them, which prevented them from leaving the river.

records.l: Portuguese ambassador's departure and arrangements for the Queen, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: concerns Queen [the ambassador is ending matters with her and sending her overseas] The Portuguese Embassador came to take leave of the King and was going to end all with the Queen and send her over.

records.l: fleet, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: carries_items_to Queen [the next fleet] The speaker hoped to recover his recent expenses during the summer by helping get things ready to send with the next fleet to the Queen.

records.l: Roger Pepys, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Roger Pepys, a sober man who succeeded Talbot Pepys as Recorder of Cambridge in 1660, welcomes Pepys from Cambridge to Impington, discusses difficulties over an uncle's will, and fears Parliament's profane young men may obstruct serious proposals and cause renewed war.

records.l: London, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: London is the place Pepys returns to on the 22nd after travel, finding his household and family well. There he resumes household, social, theatrical, official, office, and Privy Seal duties, visits major sites, and continues investigating his uncle’s estate.

records.l: the Opera, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The Opera, associated with Sir William Davenant, presents the second part of The Siege of Rhodes and The Witts. It began in late June 1661; on July 2, a delayed performance featured magnificent scenery and generally good acting despite falling dust from a broken board.

records.l: The Siege of Rhodes, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: The second part of "The Siege of Rhodes" was acted at Sir William Davenant's Opera on July 2nd. The Eunuch performed so poorly that he was hissed off the stage.

records.l: Claracilla, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_a play "Claracilla" was performed at the Theatre on July 4th. The diarist saw it for the first time and thought it well acted.

records.l: uncle Robert's corpse, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Uncle Robert’s corpse, placed in a coffin on joint-stools in the hall at Brampton, begins to smell and is moved to the yard overnight under watch before burial in church. His will, papers, and estate become central business: money, debts, Sturtlow, and an uncertain inheritance for Samuel Pepys and others.

records.l: the will, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Uncle Robert’s will is read and reviewed by the narrator, his father, relatives, Dr. John Pepys, Sir Robert Bernard, and Mr. Moore. It gives the narrator little at present, with more after his father’s death, but provides for the family and other kindred. Mr. Moore judges it sufficient despite three witnesses being legatees. Roger Pepys offers guidance and agrees to read the Captain’s will with Pepys’s uncles, while trouble over interpretation and execution is expected.

records.l: burial of uncle Robert, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: includes funeral sermon [preached by Mr. Turners] Uncle Robert was buried at the church on Sunday after the family prepared ribbons and gloves. Mr. Taylor conducted the burial, and Mr. Turners preached a funeral sermon praising the deceased's widely known honesty.

records.l: Tom Trice, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: puts_in caveat against the estate [on behalf of his mother] Tom Trice put in a caveat on behalf of his mother, who had received nothing from uncle Robert's will. This development troubled the narrator and his father.

records.l: caveat against the estate, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_on_behalf_of Tom Trice's mother A caveat was entered against the family in behalf of Tom Trice's mother, who was excluded from uncle Robert's will for reasons expressed there. The caveat added to the family's uncertainty about the inheritance.

records.l: uncle Robert's papers, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: are_in confusion [not well sorted] The narrator's father examined uncle Robert's papers while the narrator worked through them during the week. The papers were badly disorganized, making them difficult to understand and causing the narrator considerable distress.

records.l: copyhold land, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Uncle Robert’s copyhold land lacks required surrenders, so it passes to the heir at law instead of intended beneficiaries.

records.l: Cambridge, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Cambridge is a place containing Christ College, King's College chapel, Magdalen, and the University of Cambridge. It is repeatedly a narrator's destination: after preparing to ride there, he arrives, visits colleges, the Rose tavern and university friends, attends Assizes at Castle Hill, dines and drinks, notices university tensions, then rides onward.

records.l: Impington, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: After leaving Cambridge, the narrator rode to Impington. There he found his elderly uncle Talbot Pepys.

records.l: Talbot Pepys, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Talbot Pepys, the narrator’s old uncle and sixth son of John Pepys, was born in 1583, educated at Trinity Hall, became a barrister and Cambridge official, and died of plague aged eighty-three.

records.l: Pepys family estate, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Pepys family estate comprises land, crops, copyhold interests, London houses, money, debts, and surrenders. About £500 is found; a house carries a £400 fine and £46 rent. Pepys expects legal claims and debts to reduce £200-yearly land inheritance.

records.l: Walthamstow, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: is_a place Walthamstow was the destination of the August 1 coach journey, where the narrator and the others visited Mrs. Browne.

records.l: Samuel Pepys's uncle Thomas, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Dr. Thos. Pepys dined with the narrator on August 2 after the narrator had spent the morning at the office.

records.l: Parliament, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Parliament begins in disorder, with a delayed expected adjournment and a dispute between its Houses over searches, pamphlets, and seditious books. It faces City of London pressure over the Church settlement, while young men oppose serious men’s measures, raising fears of spoiled affairs and renewed war.

records.l: will litigation, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Pepys family will dispute remains unresolved: Samuel Pepys, his father, the Trices, Mr. Greene, and others negotiate his aunt leaving the house for £10, while debts, inheritance, and other estate matters proceed to law.

records.l: Mrs. Margarett Pen, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: comes_from Ireland Mrs. Margarett Pen accompanied the narrator and the others to Walthamstow. It was the first time the narrator had seen her since she came from Ireland.

records.l: Mrs. Browne, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Mrs. Browne was visited at Walthamstow by the narrator and the others. The narrator gave her six silver spoons for her boy, and the party ate a venison pasty and were merry.

records.l: the allegation about Lady Batten, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: concerns Lady Batten [alleging that she was such a man's whore] The allegation was that Lady Batten had been a man’s whore. The narrator believed the story was true, but an attempt to reconcile the matter failed.

records.l: the visit to Walthamstow, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: takes_place_at Walthamstow [by coach] The visit to Walthamstow took place on August 1, with Sir Williams both, the narrator, the narrator’s wife, and Mrs. Margarett Pen traveling by coach to see Mrs. Browne. The party ate a hot venison pasty, were merry, and returned home at night.

records.l: the journey to Cambridge, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: ends_at Cambridge [on horseback] The narrator prepared for a journey to Cambridge on horseback after Tom came to him on August 2.

records.l: Quakers, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: continue Quaker movement [in Cambridge and elsewhere] Pepys observes that the Quakers continue to be present in Baldwick and elsewhere, and that they seem to be increasing rather than diminishing.

records.l: the Privy Seal, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: has_clerks clerks [treated severely by Lord Roberts] The Privy Seal business is delayed because Lord Roberts does not appear during the morning or afternoon of the 8th. On the 9th, Lord Roberts arrives after four o'clock, questions Pepys about his deputation, and then allows the bills to be read and the business to conclude successfully.

records.l: Lord Privy Seal, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Lord Roberts, the Lord Privy Seal, misses the 8th, delaying Privy Seal business and worrying Pepys over clerks; on the 9th he questions Pepys’s deputation, accepts it, and completes the business.

records.l: Pepys family business, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Pepys examines his uncle's will, Privy Seal business, and Graveley property obligations while traveling through Brampton, Yelling, and Graveley and consulting relatives and associates.

records.l: Privy Seal business, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: requires_authorization_from Lord Roberts [as Lord Privy Seal] Pepys is required to attend Lord Roberts at the Seal because it is his month of duty. After delays on the 8th, he and Mr. Moore complete the reading of the bills on the 9th; Mons. Eschar is also waiting there for a warrant for £5,000 for the Earl of Sandwich's preparation for Portugal.

records.l: Parliamentary conflict, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
records.s: Roger Pepys describes conflict in Parliament between young men who opposed measures and serious men who advanced them. He also reports that the young men were exceptionally profane and might cause renewed war.

records.l: Quaker movement, The Diary of Samuel Pepys
