records.s: When the Spanish came in sight of Yucatan in 1517, they were surprised by its well-built stone monuments, large cities, roads, causeways, boats, and civilized inhabitants. They compared the monuments favorably with the best structures of Spain and other parts of Europe.

records.l: Maya civilization, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, The population of the country, about 250,000 souls all told, are mostly Indians
records.s: Maya civilization is described as having reached a high degree of development, demonstrated by its cities, architecture, art, sciences, language, and writing. Much of its knowledge remains unknown because its books are hidden or unavailable and its surviving works have been damaged by time and human conflict.

records.l: Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The narrator describes his investigations at Chichen-Itza and Uxmal, defending his conclusions as the result of careful analysis and comparing Maya customs with those of Old World peoples. He reports that Uxmal preserves evidence of Nahualt phallic worship, while Chichen-Itza is associated with the Itzaes, the Cans, and worship of the mastodon's head, the sun, and fire. He discusses the decline and transformation of the ancient Maya religious system, the survival of Maya language, and the dispersal of the name Maya across the Old and New Worlds. He also explains that Mayab means a tammy or sieve, probably referring to Yucatan's absorbent stony soil.

records.l: the narrator, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The narrator explains that his conclusions about the monuments resulted from careful and patient analysis and comparison rather than imagination. He describes abandoning a statue at Chichen-Itza after his men were disarmed, then continuing his research at Uxmal through photography and surveys.

records.l: Mayas, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The Mayas are described as having possessed funeral customs resembling those of some Old World nations. Their language and some customs survived invasions, wars, and Spanish efforts to suppress their traditions.

records.l: Nahualts, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The Nahualts are described as invaders from the west who introduced phallic worship and symbols of the reciprocal forces of nature. According to the narrator, they destroyed Chichen and established their capital at Uxmal, where they altered building ornaments to display their religious symbols.

records.l: Itzaes, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The Itzaes are identified as the holy and learned people associated with Chichen-Itza. Some Itzaes reportedly fled Nahualt invasions and later lived in the islands of Lake Peten and in inaccessible mountain valleys while preserving their customs, manners, and language.

records.l: Can's family, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The Cans, or family of CAN, are said to have founded Uxmal and Chichen-Itza, with their name appearing on monuments in both cities. They worshipped Deity under the symbol of the mastodon's head and also worshipped the sun and fire.

records.l: Chichen-Itza, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: Chichen-Itza is described as the city of the holy and learned Itzaes. Its monuments contain a tableau of worship involving the mastodon's head, but the narrator says that symbols of Nahualt phallic worship are not found there.

records.l: Uxmal, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: At Uxmal, the narrator photographed and surveyed ruined temples and palaces and found remnants of Nahualt phallic worship. He says that the Nahualts established their capital there and placed symbols of their religion in palace courts and on temple platforms.

records.l: Yucatan, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: Yucatan is described as the peninsula where Maya remains, language, and traditions survived despite invasions and Spanish efforts to erase them. Its stony soil is said to absorb surface water rapidly, which the narrator connects with the name Mayab.

records.l: colossal statue of Chaacmol, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The narrator says he discovered the statue at Chichen-Itza and gave it a name based on the circumstances of its discovery. Dr. Jesus Sanchez argued that it represented the god of the natural production of the earth, while Mr. Charnay identified it as the god of wine; the narrator left it wrapped in oilcloth beneath a palm-leaf hut after his men were disarmed.

records.l: Chichen-Itza palace and museum, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The monuments are presented as evidence for reconstructing ancient Maya customs, religious practices, and relationships among different peoples. Their inscriptions, sculptures, paintings, and architectural ornaments are used by the narrator to distinguish earlier Maya worship from later Nahualt influences.

records.l: the phallic worship of the Nahualts, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The narrator says he first found remnants of the phallic worship of the Nahualts at Uxmal. He states that its symbols occur frequently in northern Yucatan and in regions where Nahualt influence predominated, but not at Chichen-Itza.

records.l: Can, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The mastodon's head served as a symbol under which CAN and his family worshipped Deity. It appears prominently in the ornaments of their buildings, and figures are shown kneeling before it in a manner the narrator interprets as a sign of respect rather than proof of idol worship.

records.l: the worship of the sun and fire, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The Cans worshipped the sun and fire and represented them with the same hieroglyph that the narrator says the Egyptians used for the sun. He compares their fire worship with that of the Chaldeans and Hindoos, while distinguishing it from Egyptian attitudes toward fire.

records.l: Chaacmol, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: Chaacmol is described as having become, according to the chroniclers, a god of war who appeared amid battle surrounded by flames. Moo is identified as his wife and sister, and her shrine at Izamal was associated with oracles and a macaw form.

records.l: Quetzalcoatl, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: Kukulcan is identified as the culture hero of the Mayas and the winged serpent, worshipped by the Mexicans as Guetzalcoalt and by the Quiches as Cucumatz. The narrator suggests that he may have been Chaacmol's father or an ancestor, later associated with serpent emblems covered with feathers.

records.l: KU, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: KU is identified as the name by which the Mayas called the divine essence. The narrator suggests that this worship may have preceded later idolatrous rites introduced by invading tribes.

records.l: Maya language, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The Maya language survived wars, political and religious upheavals, invasions, and Spanish efforts to suppress ancient customs. It remained the vernacular of the people, and in some Central American localities it was said to survive in pristine purity.

records.l: Mayab, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: Mayab is said to mean a tammy or sieve in the Maya language. The narrator conjectures that the country received this name because its stony ground absorbs surface water, which later appears filtered and cool in cenotes and caves.

records.l: the Maya religious system, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The narrator presents the ancient Maya religious system as having changed over time through invasions and outside influences. He suggests that the Cans may have been monotheists who worshipped the divine essence, while later populations deified rulers and natural phenomena and adopted images and idolatrous rites.

records.l: the origin and distribution of the name Maya, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I have tarried so long on the description of my first important discovery becaus
records.s: The narrator says that the Mayas probably took their name from Mayab, the name of their country. He claims that the name Maya, with the same meaning wherever it occurs, is distributed across the ancient civilized world as well as Central America.

records.l: Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: The text argues that monuments, customs, religious rites, languages, and traditions link the prehistoric inhabitants of America with peoples of Asia, Hindostan, Egypt, and other regions. It proposes that the Mayas migrated westward from the American continent across the Pacific toward Asia and the Nile valley, citing similarities in stepped architecture, place-names, religious practices, and physical types. It compares Maya traditions in Yucatan, especially at Chichen-Itza and Uxmal, with accounts from India, Afghanistan, Babylon, Asia Minor, and Egypt. The discussion presents the red hand imprint, the name Maya, and the traditions associated with Atlantis as evidence for this proposed migration and for broader comparative cultural connections.

records.l: American continent, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: The American continent is presented as the starting point for a proposed westward route followed by the mound builders toward Asia and the valley of the Nile. Its mounds and monuments are described as early or comparatively rude examples of architectural forms later developed elsewhere.

records.l: Asia, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: Asia is described as containing monuments, customs, and religious rites that resemble those of prehistoric America. The text traces a proposed route from America across the Pacific and through Asia toward Egypt.

records.l: Egypt, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: Egypt is identified as the endpoint of a proposed route from the American continent through Asia. The text says that similar rough monuments and more advanced architectural forms occur across the regions leading toward the valley of the Nile.

records.l: Hindostan, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: Hindostan is said to contain megalithic monuments, stepped temples, Maya traditions, and customs resembling those of Yucatan. The text also connects the name Maya and several religious ideas with accounts from Hindostan.

records.l: America's prehistoric inhabitants, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: America's prehistoric inhabitants are compared with the peoples of Asia and Egypt through similarities in monuments, customs, religious rites, and traditions. The mound builders are said possibly to have followed a route from America toward Asia and the Nile valley.

records.l: Yucatan, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: Yucatan is presented as a major center of Maya monuments, customs, and traditions. Its inhabitants are said to practice the hetzmec ceremony, carry children astride the hip, use red hand imprints, and preserve architectural and religious forms comparable to those found in Asia.

records.l: Chichen-Itza, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: Chichen-Itza is described as having monuments, sculptures, mural paintings, and a palace or museum whose forms and symbols are compared with those of Asia. The text says that figures and traditions there correspond to the story of Chaacmol, Moo, and Aac, and that a panel contains an image interpreted as the cosmic egg.

records.l: Uxmal, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: Uxmal is said to preserve monuments and sculptures comparable to those of Asia. Its buildings contain numerous red imprints of open, upraised hands, including examples in the governor's house and on the archway of the palace of the priests.

records.l: Afghanistan, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: Afghanistan is described as still containing Maya tribes and place-names that the text interprets through the Maya language. The names of the Kabul River, valleys, clans, and the Khiber Pass are presented as having possible Maya meanings, and Afghan physical types are compared with figures at Chichen-Itza.

records.l: Mayas, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: The Mayas are portrayed as an ancient people whose name, architecture, customs, religious practices, and language are linked to regions from America through Asia Minor and Egypt. The text proposes that Maya tribes traveled or migrated from America across the Pacific and established themselves in places including Hindostan, Afghanistan, Babylon, and Asia Minor.

records.l: Maya language, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: The Maya language is used to interpret names, religious terms, and place-names in Yucatan, Afghanistan, Babylon, Greece, and elsewhere. The text claims that ancient inscriptions studied by the author are written in Maya and uses Maya words to explain names such as Kabul, Kunar, Khel, and Khiber.

records.l: red hand imprint, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: The red hand imprint is described as a symbol found on sacred buildings and rocks in Yucatan, among some North American aborigines, in Hindostan, and in the South Sea islands and Australia. The text interprets it as a mark associated with vows, prayers, blessings, possession, or the opening of a building for use.

records.l: Carians, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: The Carians are described as an ancient roving and piratical people of Asia Minor whose origin was considered unknown. The text claims that they may have spoken Maya or a Maya dialect, compares their customs with those of Yucatan, and says that Herodotus described them as being mocked for the way they spoke Greek.

records.l: Atlantis, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: Atlantis appears in the account that Maia, worshiped in Greece, was the daughter of Atlantis. The text interprets this tradition as suggesting that the Mayas came from beyond the Atlantic waters.

records.l: Maya migration theory, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: The Maya migration theory proposes that the Mayas or mound builders originated in the American continent and traveled westward across the Pacific through Asia toward Egypt. It is supported in the text by alleged similarities in architecture, customs, religious beliefs, personal appearance, language, place-names, and traditions.

records.l: comparative architectural and cultural coincidences, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, When, on January 28, 1873, I had the honor of reading a paper before the New Yor
records.s: The comparative coincidences include stepped platforms, pyramids, dolmens, tumuli, sun circles, religious rites, child-carrying customs, red hand imprints, deity worship, names, languages, and physical types. The text treats these similarities between America, Asia, Hindostan, Asia Minor, and Egypt as possible evidence of ancient relations and communications.

records.l: Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: The unit compares the primitive Chaldeans and the Mayas in their architecture, writing, burial customs, clothing, ornaments, and religion. It argues that Chaldean and Maya sacred buildings used superposed platforms, thick walls, staircases, and similar chambers, while their burial places and costumes also showed similarities. It compares Chaldean and Maya writing systems as using several classes of signs, including letters and monograms. It then proposes Maya-language etymologies for the names of several Chaldean divinities, including Ra, Ana, Bil, Beltis, Hea, Sin, San, Vul, and Ishtar.

records.l: Chaldeans, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: The primitive Chaldeans are described as strangers who settled in the lower Mesopotamian valleys in very remote ages, with Ur or Hur as their capital in the time of Abraham. Their architecture, writing, burial customs, clothing, ornaments, and religion are compared with those of the Mayas.

records.l: Mayas, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: The Mayas are presented as having architectural, burial, writing, clothing, ornament, and religious practices that closely resemble those attributed to the primitive Chaldeans. Their language is used to propose etymologies for Chaldean divine names.

records.l: architectural monuments, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: The architectural monuments of the Chaldeans and Mayas are said to share superposed platforms, cardinal orientation, thick walls, flat roofs, narrow chambers, exterior staircases, and similar construction methods. Chaldean buildings used clay and bricks, while Maya buildings used stone.

records.l: writing systems of the Mayas and Egyptians, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: The Chaldeans and Mayas are said to have used characters composed of straight lines enclosed in square or oblong figures. Their systems are compared as containing three classes of signs.

records.l: burial places, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: Burial places in Chaldea and Yucatan are compared through jar tombs, stone urns, coffins, and extensive artificial mounds. The burials could include dishes, vases, ornaments, and air holes.

records.l: etymology of the names of divinities, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: The unit proposes that the Maya language provides etymologies for the names of Chaldean divinities that correspond with their attributes. It discusses Ra, Ana, Bil, Beltis, Hea, Sin, San, Vul, and Ishtar, among others.

records.l: Mesopotamia, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: The lower Mesopotamian valleys are described as the region where the primitive Chaldeans settled. The Euphrates and Tigris are associated with the arrival of civilization attributed to Hea or Oannes.

records.l: Babylon, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: Babylon is associated with the name ka-ra, which the unit interprets through the Maya language as the city of infinite truth. Its supposed tower of Babel is identified with the Birs-i-nimrud.

records.l: Mugheir, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: Mugheir is described as having buildings filled with crude or sun-dried bricks and chambers possibly arched with bricks. Jar tombs and inscriptions in a hieratic form of writing are also associated with Mugheir.

records.l: Yucatan, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: Yucatan is described as having stone pyramid mounds, temples with two chambers, triangular-arched ceilings, and burial mounds containing urns and coffins. Its architecture and burial customs are compared with those of Chaldea.

records.l: Uxmal, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: Uxmal is described as having stone buildings filled with unhewn stones and faced with thick walls of hewn stone. A high priest named Cay and an effigy associated with a serpent are also connected with Uxmal.

records.l: Chichen-Itza, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: Chichen-Itza contains mural paintings and bas-reliefs used to compare Maya clothing and headbands with those of the Chaldeans. Its monuments are also said to have triangular-arched ceilings and stone construction.

records.l: Euphrates, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: The Euphrates is named as one of the rivers to which Hea or Oannes brought civilization. The unit associates this civilization with astronomy and letters.

records.l: Tigris, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: The Tigris is named with the Euphrates as a river whose early settlers were taught astronomy and letters by Hea or Oannes.

records.l: Canon Rawlinson, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: Canon Rawlinson is cited for descriptions of Chaldean clothing, religion, divine names, and writing. He is also cited for the view that Chaldean chambers were usually arched with bricks and for comments about Hea, Sin, and Ishtar.

records.l: primitive Chaldean religion, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: The primitive Chaldean religion is described as an elaborate polytheism that may have contained esoteric explanations reconciling many gods with monotheism. Its divine figures are interpreted through their attributes and proposed Maya-language etymologies.

records.l: Ra, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: Ra is placed at the head of the Chaldean pantheon and is said to mean God in the highest sense. The unit connects Ra with the sun and interprets the Maya word La as eternal truth.

records.l: Ana, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, I will make a brief parallel between the architectural monuments of the primitiv
records.s: Ana is described as a god associated with priority, antiquity, fatherhood, darkness, and death. The unit interprets his name through the Maya elements A and Na, rendered as thy mother.

records.s: The unit argues that the Maya language provides etymologies for names associated with places, peoples, deities, and ancient languages of Asia and the Near East. It links Urukh, Assyria, Asshur, Canaan, Tyre, and the Khati and their cities to Maya words, while comparing Chaldean, South American, Chinese, and Hindoo traditions concerning four divisions or provinces. It claims that the Book of Daniel’s words “Mene, mene, Tekel, upharsin” have meanings corresponding to Maya words. It also interprets Jesus of Nazareth’s reported final words as the Maya phrase “Helo, Helo, Lamah Zabac Ta Ni,” meaning that he was sinking and darkness covered his face.

records.s: The unit concerns Egypt, the Egyptians, and the proposed connections between them and the Mayas of Mayab. It compares Egyptian and Maya names, religious beliefs, writing, customs, color symbolism, and ideas about the soul, arguing that the two peoples shared a common origin or had ancient contact. It also describes the removal of the Chaacmol statue, the workers’ belief in reincarnation, and their acceptance of the narrator as a reincarnated Maya leader.

records.s: The unit compares the religious practices, funerary customs, clothing, divination, astronomy, calendars, numeration, and writing systems of the Mayas and Egyptians. It describes alleged similarities in practices and symbols at sites including Chichen-Itza, Chichen, Uxmal, and Chaacmol's mausoleum in Yucatan and Mayab. It presents the gnomon at Mayapan as evidence of Maya astronomical knowledge and compares the Maya and Egyptian calendars. The author argues that similarities between Maya and Egyptian languages and inscriptions raise the question of which people taught the other.

records.s: The Mayas are described as practicing circumcision, using a reverential arm gesture, playing the sistrum in religious rites, preserving bodies and grave goods, and worshiping deceased kings and heroes. They are also said to have practiced divination, astronomy, calendrical calculation, elaborate monumental art, and writing using phonetic, symbolic, and ideographic signs.

records.s: The Egyptians are described as practicing circumcision, using the same reverential arm gesture as the Mayas, and using the sistrum in religious ceremonies. They placed organs and professional implements in tombs, decorated tombs with paintings and sculptures, practiced divination, studied astronomy, used several writing systems, and employed systems of fives and tens.

His statue holds an empty vase, and his mausoleum contained stone urns, paintings, bas-reliefs, and objects interpreted through comparison with Egyptian funerary customs.

Typho killed and dismembered him, after which Horus finally defeated Typho.

records.s: Typho is identified as Osiris's brother and murderer. He killed Osiris, later stole his remains from Isis, cut them into pieces, scattered them over the earth, and was finally defeated by Horus.

records.s: Egypt is the setting of the Osiris myth and the kingdom ruled by Osiris. The text describes Isis as representing its irrigated land and Nephthis as representing the barren edge of its desert.

records.s: The Osiris myth concerns Osiris's life on Earth, his efforts to civilize the world, his killing and dismemberment by Typho, Isis's search for his body, and Horus's defeat of Typho. The text compares parts of this myth with traditions of the Maya culture heroes Kukulean and Quetzalcoatl.

records.s: Osiris's civilizing journey began after he became king of Egypt, when he taught his countrymen to improve and cultivate the fruits of the earth. He then traveled through the rest of the world and persuaded people to submit to his discipline.

records.s: Osiris's killing by Typho is followed in the account by the disposal of his remains, Isis's search for his body, Typho's theft and dismemberment of it, and the scattering of the pieces over the earth.

records.s: Quetzalcoatl is named as an Aztec culture hero whose traditions are compared with the civilizing deeds attributed to Osiris and Kukulean.

records.s: The Osiris mysteries were divided into greater and lesser mysteries. Candidates had to pass through the grades of the lesser mysteries, demonstrate a virtuous life, and meet additional requirements; admission to all the higher grades was described as a great honor.

records.s: Mayab is described as having mysteries that required initiates to pass through different gradations to reach a highest, apparently third, grade. The text connects these mysteries with rooms and symbols found at Uxmal.

records.s: Uxmal is the location of the monument generally called the Dwarf's House, where symbols connected with Mayan initiation mysteries were discovered.

records.s: The Dwarf's House at Uxmal contained symbols and signs that the text interprets as evidence of Mayab's mysteries. Its rooms appeared to be dedicated to different gradations of initiation, apparently culminating in a third and highest grade.

records.s: Mayan initiation mysteries are described as involving different gradations, with a highest or third level inferred from the number and arrangement of rooms in the Dwarf's House. The text also says that their affiliated members used signs and symbols resembling those of Freemasonry.

records.s: Mayan affiliated signs and symbols were discovered by the author in the Dwarf's House at Uxmal. The text says that they were perfectly identical to signs and symbols used among masons in their symbolical lodges.

records.s: The text compares Maya customs in Yucatan with those of peoples in Equatorial Africa, drawing heavily on observations by Mr. Du Chaillu. It discusses shared practices including tooth filing, witchcraft beliefs, fermented beverages, funerary offerings and sacrifices, abandonment of houses after deaths, drums, shrines, native dogs, and protective charms. It also describes Maya practices involving Chaacmol, Balche, and the worship of idols, while suggesting that some cannibalistic customs may have been introduced by the Nahualts and Aztecs.

records.s: The Mayas are described as sharing numerous customs with peoples of Equatorial Africa, including filing their teeth, believing in witchcraft, using fermented Balche in sacred ceremonies, placing possessions in tombs, abandoning houses after deaths, and using distinctive drums. They were said to have eaten the hearts of fallen enemies, although the text suggests that broader cannibalistic feasts may have been introduced by the Nahualts and Aztecs.

records.s: Equatorial Africa is presented as the region whose inhabitants share many customs with the Mayas. These customs include tooth filing, belief in sorcery, fermented honey-and-bark beverages, grave offerings and sacrifices, abandonment of places associated with death, large drums, fetish houses, native dogs, and protective leopard-skin charms.

records.s: Yucatan is described as the homeland of the Maya aborigines whose customs are compared with those of Equatorial Africa. Its inhabitants are said to have retained practices such as tooth filing, witchcraft beliefs, the use of Balche, house abandonment after deaths, village entrance shrines, and the keeping of native dogs.

records.s: Chaacmol's statue and mausoleum provide evidence that persons of high rank among the Mayas filed their teeth into sharp points. The bas-reliefs on his mausoleum are also said to show that the Mayas devoured the hearts of fallen enemies, while blood around his statue is taken to suggest that slaves may have been sacrificed at his funeral.

records.s: Witchcraft was widely believed in by the Mayas and their descendants. A sick man at X-Kanchacan attributed his illness to a spell and rejected the author's offer of treatment because he believed there was no remedy. In Equatorial Africa, Du Chaillu reported that belief in sorcery produced fear, suspicion, illness, and many murders.

records.s: Balche is a fermented liquor made from the bark of the Balche tree, water, and honey. The Mayas used it in sacred ceremonies from remote antiquity and continued to use it in their rites.

records.s: African peoples are described as filing their front teeth into sharp points, drinking a beverage made from honey, water, and tree bark, making offerings and sacrifices at graves, abandoning houses or village sites after repeated deaths, and using large drums for communication. Some African warriors are also said to wear a charmed leopard skin believed to make them immune to spears.

records.s: Du Chaillu is cited as an observer of the customs of Equatorial Africa in his account of the Land of Ashango. His reports concern tooth filing, sorcery, fermented beverages, funerary practices, drums, fetish houses, native dogs, and leopard-skin charms, and the text uses his descriptions to compare African peoples with the Mayas.

records.s: The unit argues that the Mayas were an ancient, highly civilized nation whose traditions, customs, language, and supposed colonies extended across Hindostan, Afghanistan, Egypt, Asia Minor, and other regions. It compares Maya traditions and figures from Mayab, especially Chaacmol, Moo, Aac, and Cay, with Egyptian accounts of Osiris, Isis, Typho, and related deities. The author uses similarities in names, religious symbols, writing, dress, monuments, and mural paintings at Chichen-Itza and Uxmal to argue for Maya influence or migration across the Old World. The unit also describes alleged Maya-Egyptian parallels involving leopard, macaw, serpent, sun, and baboon symbolism.

records.s: The Mayas are described as an ancient, powerful, and highly civilized nation whose enduring monuments provide only an incomplete record of their achievements. The text attributes to them widespread colonies, traditions, customs, language, religious symbols, architectural knowledge, mathematics, astronomy, and migrations into regions including Hindostan, Afghanistan, Egypt, and Asia Minor.

records.s: Mayab is presented as the homeland from which Maya colonies and migrants supposedly departed. The text places Mayab in the western region relative to Egypt and identifies it as the origin of a colony that allegedly settled along the Nile.

records.s: Hindostan is described as a place where Maya customs and traditions allegedly survived in altered mythic form. The text associates it with carrying children astride the hips, hand imprints made in red liquid, elephant worship, and traditions concerning Maya, Hema, Rama, and the death of Maya.

records.s: Afghanistan is presented as a destination reached by some Maya tribes after leaving a homeland south of Hindostan. The text claims that their descendants still lived near the river Kabul and that some village and tribal names, physical types, and warlike habits resembled those attributed to the Mayas.

records.l: Egypt, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Egypt is presented as a region whose priests preserved distorted or secret versions of traditions that the author identifies as Maya in origin. The text compares Egyptian deities, royal legends, religious symbols, writing, priestly dress, and western ancestral traditions with those of Mayab.

records.s: Yucatan is described as the region containing ruined cities and monuments attributed to the Mayas. Its architectural features, carved figures, inscriptions, mural paintings, and traditions are repeatedly compared with those of ancient Egypt and other regions.

records.l: Chichen-Itza, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Chichen-Itza is identified as the place where Chaacmol and Moo supposedly reigned and where their mausoleum, sculptures, bas-reliefs, mural paintings, and inscriptions were found. The text uses its bearded figures, royal scenes, leopard and macaw imagery, serpent symbolism, and depictions of Moo and a baboon to support alleged Maya-Egyptian parallels.

records.l: Uxmal, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Uxmal is described as a Maya city containing sculptures, a temple of death, a sacrificial altar, cynocephali, and representations of Aac and other figures. The text states that Aac's statue showed him surrounded by the Sun and that the escutcheon of Uxmal identified his territory as the land of the Sun.

records.s: MAYA is identified as the great architect whose widow HEMA is said to have explained the exclusion of foreigners from the country. The text also says that Maya was killed by the thunderbolt of Pourandara and treats this story as a parallel to traditions concerning Chaacmol and Moo.

records.s: Chaacmol is described as the husband and brother of Moo and a ruler at Chichen-Itza in Mayab. He was allegedly killed by his brother Aac with three spear thrusts in the back, and the author claims to have opened his mausoleum, found his heart and jade ornaments, and identified his effigy and name.

records.s: Moo is described as Chaacmol's wife and sister and as the Queen of Chichen. She is represented as a macaw, was worshiped at Izamal under the name Kinich-Kakmo, and is portrayed in mural paintings as protected by a serpent and warned by a baboon.

records.s: Aac is described as the brother of Chaacmol and Moo who killed Chaacmol out of jealousy in order to usurp the throne. His statue is said to have displayed the heads of Cay, Chaacmol, and Moo and to have rested on their flayed bodies, while his protecting spirit was the Sun.

records.s: Osiris is described in Egyptian tradition as the husband and brother of Isis, the victim of Typho, and king of the Amenti, the western region of the dead. The text associates him with a leopard skin, a leopard hieroglyph, and priestly leopard-skin dress, and presents him as a mythic counterpart of Chaacmol.

records.l: Isis, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Isis is described as the wife and sister of Osiris and as queen of the Amenti. The text compares her with Moo through their familial roles, western sovereignty, leopard symbolism, and association with a female animal totem, while stating that Isis was represented with wings and a vulture.

records.l: Typho, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Typho is described as the brother of Osiris and Isis who killed Osiris out of jealousy and a desire to seize the throne. The text compares him with Aac, who allegedly killed Chaacmol in a similar act of treachery.

records.l: Egyptian mythology, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Egyptian mythology is characterized as a transformed or mythical version of historical traditions that the author believes originated among the Mayas. The unit specifically compares its stories of Osiris, Isis, Typho, Aroeris, Nephthis, and Thoth with Maya figures, events, symbols, and monuments.

records.l: Maya language, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: The Maya language is used in the text to provide alleged etymologies for names and terms across several regions. Examples include Maya, Hema, Chaacmol, Moo, Kinich-Kakmo, Aac, Nic, Nukta, Thoth, Kal, and Khaldi.

records.l: Maya civilization, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Maya civilization is portrayed as ancient, powerful, technologically and intellectually advanced, and capable of producing major monuments, writing systems, mathematical and astronomical knowledge, and extensive settlements. The text says its full attainments cannot be known because most evidence has disappeared through time and atmospheric deterioration.

records.l: Maya migrations, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Maya migrations are presented as movements from Mayab into Hindostan, Afghanistan, Ethiopia, the Persian Gulf, Chaldea, Asia Minor, and Egypt. The text attributes to these migrations the spread of Maya names, languages, customs, traditions, religious ideas, and architectural or artistic practices.

records.l: Spanish conquest, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: The Spanish conquest is mentioned in connection with the warlike character attributed to the Mayas. The text says that the Mayas fought the Spanish invaders bravely and tenaciously.

records.l: Chichen-Itza palace and museum, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Maya monuments are described as the most enduring surviving evidence of Maya civilization. Their ruins, sculptures, inscriptions, architectural forms, tombs, and decorative symbols are used to reconstruct Maya history and to compare it with Egypt and other regions.

records.l: Maya mural paintings, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Maya mural paintings at Chichen-Itza and elsewhere are said to depict Chaacmol, Moo, Aac, Cay, their followers, religious symbols, and scenes from their stories. The text uses these paintings as evidence for alleged parallels with Egyptian mythology, including the stories of Osiris, Isis, Typho, and the garden of Eden.

records.l: Egyptian and Maya common origin, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, _" Let us now take a brief retrospective glance at the FACTS mentioned in the fo
records.s: Maya-Egyptian correspondences are claimed in names, myths, royal relationships, religious symbols, priestly practices, writing, dress, architecture, and astronomical or mathematical knowledge. The central comparison identifies Chaacmol with Osiris, Moo with Isis, and Aac with Typho, while also linking Maya serpent, leopard, macaw, Sun, and baboon imagery with Egyptian religious representations.

records.l: Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: The unit argues that the Mayas were indigenous to the western continent and that their civilization did not originate in Asia or Africa. It connects the name Mayas to MAYAB, a porous land in the region beyond the Atlantic, and compares Maya language, beliefs, symbols, and monuments with those of Hindostan, Greece, and Egypt. It presents the Ake monument and its thirty-six katun columns as evidence that Maya civilization was at least 5,760 years old when the monument was completed. The author concludes that further research, especially the interpretation of inscriptions and recovery of Maya libraries, is necessary before forming an unquestionable theory.

records.l: Mayas, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: The Mayas are presented as an autochthonous race of the western continent rather than people who received their civilization from Asia or Africa. They are said to have taken their name from MAYAB, deified eminent men and women after death, and carried religious customs and other practices to lands where they emigrated.

records.l: Mayab, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: MAYAB is described as a country beyond the Atlantic Ocean whose porous soil absorbed water like a sieve. Its inhabitants took the name Mayas from the country, and the text says that later peoples transformed MAYAB from a locality into a personality associated with the mother of the gods.

records.l: Maya civilization, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: The text argues that Maya civilization developed independently of the civilizations of Asia and Africa, although some relations and exchanges may have existed. Its antiquity is associated with monuments, calendrical records, and other evidence that the author claims may extend back more than 6,000 years.

records.l: Maya language, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: The etymology of the name Maya is said to be found only in the American Maya language. The text also claims that names of tribes and cities in Afghanistan belong to this language.

records.l: Egypt, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: Egypt is associated with a sieve and a land sign in the usual written character for its name. The text suggests that western invaders from MAYAB may have subdued the primitive inhabitants of the Nile valley and become its lords and masters.

records.l: Egyptians, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: The Egyptians are said to have shared many customs and attainments with the Mayas but also to have possessed differences in religious rites and habits. They reportedly pointed toward the West as the birthplace of their ancestors and worshiped figures whose remains were said to exist in MAYAB.

records.l: American continent, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: America is described as the western continent where the Mayas were indigenous. The text says that the ruined cities of tropical America may be older than the most ancient monuments of Egypt.

records.l: Yucatan, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: Yucatan is identified as the region containing the monuments, inscriptions, and vernacular studied by the author. The text places Mayab and its ancient cities in or near Yucatan and mentions ruined monuments there.

records.l: Ake, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: Ake is described as a city about twenty-five miles from Merida. It contains a monument with thirty-six columns of katuns, each representing 160 years, which the text uses to calculate an interval of 5,760 years.

records.l: Maya hieroglyphic writing, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: Maya hieroglyphic writing is said to use a sieve as the sign for a lord or master. The text treats this symbol as a possible indication of a connection between MAYAB and the people who ruled Egypt.

records.l: Chichen-Itza palace and museum, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: The monuments of Mayab are presented as evidence for the antiquity, customs, and possible movements of the Mayas. Their inscriptions, orientations, symbols, and construction are cited as subjects requiring further interpretation.

records.l: Ake monument, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: The Ake monument consists of three immense superposed platforms and a structure sustaining thirty-six katun columns. According to the text, the columns record 5,760 years between the laying of the first stone and the placement of the final capping stone, with the monument possibly completed around the time of the Spanish conquest.

records.l: the Maya religious system, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa, That the Mayas were a race autochthon on this western continent and did not rece
records.s: Maya religious customs included deifying and giving divine honors to eminent men and women after their deaths. The text says that the Mayas carried this hero worship and other customs to lands where they emigrated.

records.l: Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: The narrator introduces the Rough Diamond as a collection of true-to-life observations about American character and recounts experiences from the early nineteenth-century western and southern frontier. He describes traveling by canoe through Bush Bayou, crossing the Mississippi River, and reaching Helena, Arkansas, in time to see the race between Silver Heels and the Spotted Buck. He also recalls Alonzo Phelps, who escaped before his execution in Vicksburg but was shot and killed, and whose confession described a murder in Europe. Finally, he recounts Daymon's murder trial in Louisville, Kentucky, based on circumstantial evidence that his wife had drowned, until Daymon's wife unexpectedly entered the courtroom alive.

records.l: the narrator, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: The narrator presents the work as an account of events he witnessed or learned by tradition rather than his own history. He describes his early life, travels on the Mississippi River and its tributaries, a dangerous journey to Helena, Arkansas, and his observations of Alonzo Phelps and Daymon's trial.

records.l: Alonzo Phelps, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: Alonzo Phelps was sentenced to hang for murder in Vicksburg. He escaped from jail on the day of his scheduled execution but was pursued and shot dead by an officer of the law; the narrator learned that Phelps had written a confession.

records.l: Daymon, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: Daymon was a young laborer or boat hand who helped conduct boats across the falls at Louisville, Kentucky. He was dissipated and frequently abused his wife while intoxicated, and he was arrested and tried for allegedly drowning her in Beargrass Creek; despite circumstantial evidence, he pleaded not guilty.

records.l: Roxie Fairfield, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: Daymon's wife was described as young, intelligent, and free from any stain of character. After she disappeared, a shoe and a body wearing a dress said to be hers led people to believe she had drowned, but she entered the courtroom alive after Daymon was found guilty.

records.l: Mississippi River, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: The narrator traveled on the Mississippi River and its tributaries in his youth. He crossed the river at night in a heavily laden canoe amid turbulent, bank-full water and driftwood, using the light of a cabin as his guide.

records.l: Helena, Arkansas, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: Near Helena, Arkansas, old Billy Horner and Henry Mooney held a quarter-mile race between two ponies. The narrator traveled there from Bush Bayou to obtain the Governor of Arkansas's signature on a land grant and title.

records.l: Louisville, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: Louisville, Kentucky, was described as a principal point on the early route between Pittsburg and New Orleans. Its falls required boats to employ resident pilots, and the city was the setting of Daymon's murder trial.

records.l: Beargrass Creek, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: Beargrass Creek emptied into the Ohio near the suburbs of Louisville. Daymon's wife was believed to have been drowned there after her shoe and an unidentified woman's body were found along its margin, though she later appeared alive.

records.l: THE ROUGH DIAMOND, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: The Rough Diamond is presented as a work intended to preserve sentiments about America's earlier, rougher past and the character formed in it. The narrator compares the nation's log-cabin beginnings with later magnificence and hopes readers will retain pride in that past.

records.l: the race between Silver Heels and the Spotted Buck, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: The race was a quarter-mile contest near Helena, Arkansas, between ponies owned or ridden by old Billy Horner and Henry Mooney, with a stake of one hundred dollars. The Spotted Buck won, although some observers said it was a jockey race and that Silver Heels was the faster horse.

records.l: Alonzo Phelps's execution, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: Alonzo Phelps's execution was scheduled to take place by hanging on the day he escaped from jail. He did not hang; he was killed by a rifle shot while fleeing from the jail.

records.l: the confession of Alonzo Phelps, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: Alonzo Phelps's confession ended with the statement, "To-morrow is the day appointed for my execution, but I will not hang." It described his first murder in Europe, including how he placed the victim's body on top of a coffin in a newly made grave, and said papers taken from that victim were later discovered through the confession.

records.l: Daymon's murder trial, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: At Daymon's murder trial, the state presented a shoe identified as belonging to his wife and a body from Beargrass Creek wearing a dress identified as hers. Daymon had no defense counsel until the judge appointed attorneys, and the jury found him guilty before his wife entered the courtroom alive.

records.l: Daymon's wife's disappearance, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: Daymon's wife's disappearance caused great excitement in the neighborhood near Beargrass Creek. Searchers found a shoe believed to be hers and later a woman's body, prompting suspicion against Daymon and leading to his arrest.

records.l: Daymon's wife's apparent drowning, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: The apparent drowning was inferred from the discovery of Daymon's wife's shoe on the margin of Beargrass Creek and a woman's body in the creek. The body was badly damaged by fish and could not be recognized by its face, but witnesses identified its dress as one made for Daymon's wife; the conclusion was disproved when she appeared alive.

records.l: the American frontier and pioneer past, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Craig Kansas City, Missouri 1880 [Ill cover] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.
records.s: The unit portrays the American frontier and pioneer past through log-school education, early settlement, river navigation, flatboats, keelboats, frontier travel, rough local communities, and dangers from animals and waterways. The narrator treats this earlier period as a formative part of American character and says the log cabin should remain dear to the American heart.

records.l: Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: Don and Dan Carlo operate a wood yard at Shirt-Tail Bend, but Dan spends his share of the proceeds while Don pays the expenses. Brindle Bill, S. S. Simon, and Sundown Hill plot to swindle Dan at headquarters, where Don interrupts them and takes the money from the table. Don fights Brindle Bill until Simon's wife sets fire to the cabin, ending the contest and helping Don keep the money. Dan later dies in a saloon, while Don is identified among the dead or dying after the steamboat Red Stone explodes; he is remembered as the Hero of Shirt-Tail Bend.

records.l: Don Carlo, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: Don Carlo is Dan Carlo's equal partner in the wood business and pays all the expenses while Dan receives half the money. After reading about Alonzo Phelps, he goes to headquarters, enters through the chimney, takes the money from the gambling table, and fights Brindle Bill. He keeps the money after the fight and is later found among the dead or dying after the Red Stone explosion, becoming known as the Hero of Shirt-Tail Bend.

records.l: Dan Carlo, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: Dan Carlo is Don Carlo's brother and business partner, but he spends his share of the wood-yard proceeds and repeatedly fails to reform. He goes to headquarters with Brindle Bill, S. S. Simon, and Sundown Hill, where they plan to swindle him. Shortly after these events, he is found dead in a saloon.

records.l: Brindle Bill, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: Brindle Bill is a strong wood-chopper and the bully of the settlement who leads one of its social parties. He joins the scheme against Dan Carlo and claims the money when Don Carlo interrupts the game. He fights Don Carlo but is defeated when the fire at headquarters ends the contest, after which he leaves the new settlement.

records.l: Simon's wife, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: Simon's wife recognizes that trouble is coming when Don Carlo goes toward headquarters. She secretly follows with a firebrand and sets the cane pile against the cabin ablaze when she hears the fight. She then drags her husband away and cries out in shame.

records.l: the wood-cutters, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: The wood-cutters are the representative men of the neighborhood and supply the wood used by passing steamboats. Some are described as men of sterling integrity, while others belong to the floating population and gather at headquarters for drinking, cards, and entertainment. Their customary method of settling personal quarrels is an unarmed physical contest supervised by chosen seconds.

records.l: steamboats, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: Steamboats drive the wood trade on the Ohio and Mississippi rivers, with some taking on twenty-four cords of wood at one landing. Their calls for wood after dark cause woodmen to rush from their cabins with torches, giving Shirt-Tail Bend its name. The Red Stone later explodes while landing on the Kentucky shore, killing and injuring many people.

records.l: the Carlo wood yard, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: The Carlo wood yard is operated by Don Carlo and Dan Carlo as equal partners. After a large sale of wood there, Dan goes to headquarters with his companions while Don remains alone before deciding to confront them.

records.l: Shirt-Tail Bend, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: Shirt-Tail Bend is a Mississippi River locality known for its wood yards and for woodmen running out in their shirt-tails to supply steamboats at night. It has little social infrastructure, with no schoolhouse, church, or post-office at first. After Don Carlo's victory, planters settle there and small towns begin to develop.

records.l: headquarters, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: Headquarters is an abandoned cabin in the edge of a cane-brake where the jug is kept and men gather for drinking and cards. Brindle Bill, S. S. Simon, Sundown Hill, and Dan Carlo use it for their scheme against Dan. Don Carlo enters through the chimney, and the cabin is later set on fire by Simon's wife.

records.l: Ohio River, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: The Ohio River is described as a principal western waterway whose navigation by steam helped create new industries. Early supporters of free navigation wished to be buried on its bank so they could hear boatmen's songs and the sound of steam engines. The Red Stone explodes on the Kentucky shore of the Ohio, and some victims are consigned to its waters.

records.l: Mississippi River, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: The Mississippi River is central to the expansion of steamboat navigation and the wood trade. The Carlo wood yard and Shirt-Tail Bend are located along it, and early wood-cutters supply passing boats with fuel. The text also describes the legal struggle against exclusive monopolist claims to navigate its western waters by steam.

records.l: steam navigation, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: Steam navigation on the western waters is presented as a new era that creates unforeseen industries, including the sale of cordwood to steamboats. The Enterprise is said to have been the first steamboat to ascend the Mississippi River, while the Washington is connected with the legal challenge to exclusive claims over western steam navigation. The Supreme Court of the United States denied the monopolist's exclusive pretensions.

records.l: the wood business, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: The wood business is the principal source of revenue at Shirt-Tail Bend, and large quantities of cord or steam wood are sold to passing steamboats. Don and Dan Carlo operate as equal partners, but Don pays the expenses while Dan takes half the proceeds and spends them. The business brings thousands of dollars into the Bend without initially producing broader improvements.

records.l: the gambling scheme against Dan Carlo, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: S. S. Simon, Sundown Hill, and Brindle Bill are described as banding together at headquarters to swindle Dan Carlo after a large sale of wood. Simon's wife warns that Dan's money will go that night. Don interrupts the scheme by entering the cabin and raking the money from the table.

records.l: the fight between Don Carlo and Brindle Bill, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
records.s: Brindle Bill starts the fight after claiming the gambling money and saying that Don Carlo has insulted him. Brindle Bill is stronger, but Don is more active and fights with true pluck. The fight ends when Simon's wife sets fire to headquarters, and Don retains the money.

records.l: the fire at headquarters, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life, SCENE SECOND.
