records.s: Nahualts are invading people from the west. They destroy Chichen-Itza, establish a capital at Uxmal, introduce cannibalism with the Aztecs, and alter Uxmal’s ornaments to display phallic worship and symbols of reciprocal natural forces.

records.l: gnomon, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: An astronomical instrument discovered in the ruined city of Mayapan, the gnomon is said to show Maya scholars’ latitude calculations, solstitial-point and solar-declination identification, and a construction representing the sacred year through its stela centers’ joining line.

records.l: Maya language, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Maya language is described as an ancient language and the vernacular of the aborigines of Yucatan and other parts of Central America. It is said to have endured wars, invasions, political and religious upheavals, and Spanish attempts to suppress ancient customs, remaining in use and, in some localities, surviving in pristine purity. The records present individual Maya words, including Thallac, Axul, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin, MIZ, and a phrase translated as describing darkness covering a sinking speaker's face. They also state that it was known in Chaldea in remote ages and understood by some learned men in Judea at the beginning of the Christian era. Across the text, Maya is chiefly used as a source of etymologies: the author identifies inscriptions as Maya and employs its words to interpret names, religious terms, place-names, peoples, deities, and ancient expressions in Yucatan, Afghanistan, Babylon, Greece, Chaldea, Assyria, Phoenicia, and Egypt. The account further says the language changed through altered customs, invasions, and contact with other peoples, while claiming that the name Maya and names of tribes and cities in Afghanistan belong to it.

records.l: Maya hieroglyphic writing, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Maya hieroglyphic writing is presented as a system of letters proper, monograms, and pictorial characters, including straight-line signs enclosed in square or oblong figures. The records emphasize claimed similarities between Maya and Egyptian writing: Maya words are used to explain Egyptian and place names, U LUUMIL KIN at Uxmal is compared with an Egyptian land-and-sun sign, and a sieve sign for a lord or master is treated as possible evidence of a connection between MAYAB and rulers of Egypt.

records.l: Mexican government, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: can_grant requisite permission [to Augustus Le Plongeon to bring forth hidden volumes] The Mexican government is asked to grant permission for the author to recover ancient books from buildings where they are hidden. The text also states that the government transported the head of Chaacmol’s colossal statue to Mexico without the author’s consent or compensation.

records.l: American archaeology, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_neglected_by European scientists [in the opinion criticized by the author] American archaeology is defended against European scientists who dismiss it because they believe no relationship existed between American and Old World civilizations. The author argues that the ruins of Yucatan and Central America had not yet been thoroughly or scientifically explored.

records.l: Spanish, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Spanish first arrive in Yucatan in 1517, encountering a population described as mostly Indians. They are surprised by large stone monuments, cities, roads and boats, and meet inhabitants portrayed as civilized, wearing white cotton and having polite manners.

records.l: Ake, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Ake is a city in Yucatan, about twenty-five miles from Merida, containing a monument of thirty-six katun columns whose 160-year units yield an interval of 5,760 years.

records.l: Chichen-Itza, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Chichen-Itza is a city of the holy and learned Itzaes, said to have been founded by Cans together with Uxmal. Its architecture includes stone buildings with triangular-arched ceilings and platforms diminishing upward, a conception compared with Hindostan. It contains monumental buildings, sculptures, bas-reliefs, mural paintings, inscriptions, statues of dead personages, and a palace or museum. At the southern end of the eastern wall of the gymnasium is Chaacmol's funeral chamber; a colossal statue of Chaacmol was discovered in a burial context. The site is also identified as the place where Chaacmol and Moo supposedly reigned and where their mausoleum and related remains were found. Its imagery includes mastodon-head worship, reverential arm gestures, bearded and royal figures, leopard and macaw imagery, serpents, Moo, and a baboon; one panel is interpreted as the cosmic egg. The monuments are documented through photography, surveys, plans, and analysis of ornament and design. They are repeatedly used for comparisons with Asia, Hindostan, Chaldeans, Egyptians, and alleged Maya-Egyptian traditions, while the narrator says symbols of Nahualt phallic worship are absent.

records.l: Mrs. Le Plongeon, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Mrs. Le Plongeon arrived at Progresso in 1873, worked with Augustus Le Plongeon studying Maya monuments, and described Uxmal, Ake, and Mayapan in letters to the New York World.

records.l: Augustus Le Plongeon, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Augustus Le Plongeon worked with Mrs. Le Plongeon after arriving at Progresso in 1873 to photograph, survey, and study Maya monuments, excavating at Chichen-Itza and reporting Chaacmol’s tomb, colossal statue, and name interpretation.

records.l: Chaacmol, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Chaacmol is presented as a Maya ruler at Chichen-Itza: a great warrior and king, a member of Can's family, and, according to chroniclers, a god of war who appeared in battle amid flames. He ruled with Moo, described variously as his sibling and co-ruler and as his wife, sister, and consort. His identity was marked by a shield painted with round green spots, a spotted-tiger totem, leopard representations, and a leopard-skin shield. His statue, found in a buried monument, holds an empty vase; workers believed he would return to inhabit it. Accounts of the statue and mausoleum describe filed teeth, paintings, bas-reliefs, urns, jade ornaments, and other objects. The records interpret the urn contents as his brains, heart, and viscera, the carvings as evidence of enemies' hearts being devoured, and blood near the statue as possible evidence of funeral sacrifices. Chaacmol was allegedly killed by Aac, his brother, with three spear thrusts in the back out of jealousy. He was buried in a mausoleum at Chichen-Itza, which the author says he opened, identifying Chaacmol's effigy and name and finding his heart and jade ornaments.

records.l: Chaacmol's funeral chamber, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: contains mural paintings [including scenes of Chaacmol's death and cremation] Chaacmol’s funeral chamber is located on the eastern wall of the gymnasium at Chichen-Itza. Its mural paintings depict Chaacmol in battle, his corpse prepared for cremation, and funerary scenes involving the extraction and preservation of the heart and other organs.

records.l: Moo, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Moo, Queen of Chichen, is Chaacmol's wife and sister. Represented as a macaw, she is worshiped at Izamal as Kinich-Kakmo and portrayed in murals protected by a serpent and warned by a baboon.

records.l: colossal statue of Chaacmol, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The colossal statue of Chaacmol is an effigy discovered by the narrator at Chichen-Itza and named from the circumstances of its discovery. Found in an excavation, it was placed on rollers for removal, but workers first tried to rebury it face downward, fearing desecration of the future body of a great warrior and king. After the men were disarmed, the narrator left it wrapped in oilcloth beneath a palm-leaf hut. Its head, found near urns in its burial monument, was taken aboard the gunboat Libertad to the National Museum of Mexico without the narrator’s consent or compensation. Its identity remains disputed.

records.l: Egyptians, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Egyptians are presented as a group distinguished by beliefs and practices centered on death, religion, and ancestry. They believed the soul was immortal, faced judgment by Osiris, and would eventually return to its former body; accordingly, they embalmed bodies and placed organs and the deceased’s professional implements in tombs. Their tombs were decorated with paintings and sculptures. They practiced circumcision, divination, astronomy, several writing systems, and systems of fives and tens, and used the sistrum in religious ceremonies. They considered five supplementary days unlucky and showed reverence by crossing an arm over the chest to the opposite shoulder. They are said to have shared many customs and attainments with the Mayas, pointed westward as their ancestors’ birthplace, and worshiped personages from MAYAB as gods and goddesses.

records.l: Chaldeans, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Chaldeans are an ancient people described as settling the lower Mesopotamian valleys in remote ages, with Ur or Hur as their capital in Abraham’s time. They used a Chaldean writing system and built primitive mud-and-brick monuments with rectangular, cardinally oriented, stepped forms, staircases, and crowning shrines. Their traditions included a creation account, Thalatth and the sea, while early kings reportedly ruled four races. Their clothing included a tunic, abba cloak, and camel-hair ornamented head band; learned men were called Magi. Their architecture, writing, customs, dress, and religion are compared with those of the Mayas.

records.l: reincarnation, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Reincarnation is believed in by Mayas and Egyptians. Maya belief describes souls returning to earth after suffering and bliss to animate bodies; workers removing the Chaacmol statue saw it as a warrior’s future body and the narrator as a disenchanted great man returned.

records.l: Spanish arrival in 1517, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: When the Spanish came in sight of Yucatan in 1517, they were surprised by its well-built stone monuments, large cities, roads, causeways, boats, and civilized inhabitants. They compared the monuments favorably with the best structures of Spain and other parts of Europe.

records.l: the narrator, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: An investigator of ancient monuments studies Yucatan through patient analysis and comparison. After his men are disarmed and he abandons a statue at Chichen-Itza, he continues research at Uxmal using photography and surveys.

records.l: Itzaes, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: inhabit city of the holy men [during its period of splendor] The Itzaes are identified as the holy and learned people associated with Chichen-Itza. Some Itzaes reportedly fled Nahualt invasions and later lived in the islands of Lake Peten and in inaccessible mountain valleys while preserving their customs, manners, and language.

records.l: Can's family, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Can's family, named CAN, is described as seven members, Can, Coz, Cay, Aak, Chaacmol, Moo, and Nicte, who founded the principal cities of Mayab, including Uxmal and Chichen-Itza. Their name appears on monuments there. Associated with mounds, temples, priesthood, rulership, and posthumous worship, they revered Deity through a mastodon's head and also worshipped the sun and fire.
records.t: Can's family, named CAN, is described as seven members—Can, Coz, Cay, Aak, Chaacmol, Moo, and Nicte—who founded the principal cities of Mayab, including Uxmal and Chichen-Itza. Their name appears on monuments there. Associated with mounds, temples, priesthood, rulership, and posthumous worship, they revered Deity through a mastodon's head and also worshipped the sun and fire.

records.l: the phallic worship of the Nahualts, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The phallic worship of the Nahualts is an ancient worship whose remnants were first discovered at Uxmal; its symbols are frequent in northern Yucatan and Nahualt-influenced regions, but absent from Chichen-Itza.

records.l: Can, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Can, meaning serpent, is presented as the founder or head and family name of Chaacmol’s family, associated with principal cities of Mayab. Can and his family worshipped Deity beneath a mastodon-head symbol displayed on buildings, while the family’s feathered-serpent totem surrounded Chaacmol’s mausoleum and was said to influence Uxmal and Chichen.

records.l: the worship of the sun and fire, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The worship of the sun and fire was practiced by the Cans alongside worship of the mastodon's head. They represented sun and fire with the same hieroglyph used by Egyptians for the sun, resembled Chaldeans and Hindoos in fire worship, and differed from Egyptians, who venerated no fire.

records.l: Quetzalcoatl, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Quetzalcoatl is an Aztec and Maya culture hero, identified with the winged serpent and with Kukulcan. Worshipped by Mexicans as Guetzalcoalt and by Quiches as Cucumatz, he may have been Chaacmol's father or ancestor and became associated with feather-covered serpent emblems. His traditions are compared with the civilizing deeds of Osiris and Kukulean.

records.l: KU, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_a divine essence [worshipped by the Mayas] KU is identified as the name by which the Mayas called the divine essence. The narrator suggests that this worship may have preceded later idolatrous rites introduced by invading tribes.

records.l: Mayab, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Mayab is the Maya country, a name for Yucatan and a land of the Mayas. Its name is said to mean “tammy or sieve,” explained by stony, porous ground that absorbs surface water and yields it later, filtered and cool, in cenotes and caves. Its people are said to have taken their name from the country; MAYO_lo is described as a corruption of Mayab, and later peoples are said to have transformed Mayab from a locality into a personality associated with the mother of the gods. Mayab is portrayed through its monuments, paintings, customs, religious practices, language, writing, calendar, and astronomical knowledge. It had elaborate dress among higher classes and representations of rulers, priests, warriors, and others. It also had initiation mysteries with successive gradations, apparently culminating in a third grade, connected with rooms and symbols at Uxmal. The records repeatedly compare its color symbolism, sacred or funerary blue, religion, and ancient writing with Egypt. Finally, it is presented as a homeland from which Maya colonies and migrants departed, including an alleged colony that settled along the Nile.

records.l: the Maya religious system, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Maya religious system is presented as a changing body of beliefs and rites shaped by invasions and outside influences. It may have begun among the Cans with worship of a divine essence, then developed deified rulers, natural phenomena, images, and idolatrous rites. Its practices included sun worship, sistrum use, divination, oracles, priestesses, temples, offerings, reverence, and honors for deceased rulers, heroes, and eminent women and men, customs said to have spread with Maya emigrants.

records.l: the origin and distribution of the name Maya, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The origin and distribution of Maya centers on the claim that the Mayas probably took their name from Mayab, their country, and that Maya, with the same meaning wherever found, extends from Central America across ancient civilized regions of the Old World.

records.l: American continent, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The American continent is presented as the starting point for a proposed westward route followed by the mound builders toward Asia and the valley of the Nile. Its mounds and monuments are described as early or comparatively rude examples of architectural forms later developed elsewhere. America is described as the western continent where the Mayas were indigenous. The text says that the ruined cities of tropical America may be older than the most ancient monuments of Egypt.

records.l: Asia, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Asia is described as containing monuments, customs, and religious rites that resemble those of prehistoric America. The text traces a proposed route from America across the Pacific and through Asia toward Egypt.

records.l: Egypt, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Egypt is an ancient country, also called Mizraim in the Scriptures and frequently the Land of the Sun. It is portrayed as eminent among ancient nations for the grandeur and beauty of its monuments, advanced civilization, knowledge, industry, and religious traditions; one reported view calls it a source of human knowledge. A proposed route from the American continent through Asia ends in Egypt, where monuments and architectural forms are said to culminate toward the Nile valley. In conflict, Egypt fought the Khati, who obstructed its conquests until Rameses the Great defeated them; Egyptian records reportedly marked that defeat on his palace at Thebes. Egypt also provides the setting for Osiris's kingdom: Isis represents irrigated land and Nephthis the barren desert edge. Much of the account makes Egypt the principal comparison with Mayas or Mayab, claiming similarities in customs, monuments, rites, calendars, astronomy, numeration, language, writing, deities, and symbols. It finally advances the suggestion that western invaders from MAYAB subdued primitive Nile-valley inhabitants and became their rulers.

records.l: Hindostan, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Hindostan is a place containing highly elaborate, imposing temples and said to contain megalithic monuments and stepped temples. It is associated with Maya traditions, religious ideas, and altered surviving customs, including carrying children astride hips, red hand imprints, elephant worship, and accounts of Maya, Hema, Rama, and Maya’s death.

records.l: America's prehistoric inhabitants, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: America's prehistoric inhabitants had monuments resembling megalithic forms and, through shared monuments, customs, religious rites, and traditions, were compared with Asia and Egypt; mound builders possibly followed a westward route toward Asia and Nile valley.

records.l: Afghanistan, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Afghanistan is described as still containing Maya tribes and place-names that the text interprets through the Maya language. The names of the Kabul River, valleys, clans, and the Khiber Pass are presented as having possible Maya meanings, and Afghan physical types are compared with figures at Chichen-Itza. Afghanistan is presented as a destination reached by some Maya tribes after leaving a homeland south of Hindostan. The text claims that their descendants still lived near the river Kabul and that some village and tribal names, physical types, and warlike habits resembled those attributed to the Mayas.

records.l: Babylon, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Babylon, associated with ka-ra, is interpreted as the city of infinite truth and contains the temple of the seven lights, identified as the supposed tower of Babel, Birs-i-nimrud.

records.l: Maya, architect of the Davanas, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_killed_by Pourandara [with a thunderbolt, according to the account of Maya's death] MAYA is identified as the great architect whose widow HEMA is said to have explained the exclusion of foreigners from the country. The text also says that Maya was killed by the thunderbolt of Pourandara and treats this story as a parallel to traditions concerning Chaacmol and Moo.

records.l: Aac, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_brother_of Chaacmol [and Moo] Aac is described as the brother of Chaacmol and Moo who killed Chaacmol out of jealousy in order to usurp the throne. His statue is said to have displayed the heads of Cay, Chaacmol, and Moo and to have rested on their flayed bodies, while his protecting spirit was the Sun.

records.l: red hand imprint, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The red hand imprint is a religious and property symbol found on monuments, sacred buildings, rocks, caves, and among peoples in Yucatan, North America, Hindostan, the South Sea islands, and Australia. It is interpreted as marking vows, prayers, blessings, possession, or a building’s opening for use.

records.l: Carians, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Carians are described as an ancient, roving, piratical people of Asia Minor with unknown origin. They were reportedly mocked for their Greek speech; the author claims they may have spoken Maya or a Maya dialect and compares their customs with those of Yucatan.

records.l: Atlantis, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Atlantis appears in the account that Maia, worshiped in Greece, was the daughter of Atlantis. The text interprets this tradition as suggesting that the Mayas came from beyond the Atlantic waters.

records.l: Maya migration theory, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: proposes_migration_from American continent [westward across the Pacific toward Asia and Egypt] The Maya migration theory proposes that the Mayas or mound builders originated in the American continent and traveled westward across the Pacific through Asia toward Egypt. It is supported in the text by alleged similarities in architecture, customs, religious beliefs, personal appearance, language, place-names, and traditions.

records.l: comparative architectural and cultural coincidences, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_a comparative study The comparative coincidences include stepped platforms, pyramids, dolmens, tumuli, sun circles, religious rites, child-carrying customs, red hand imprints, deity worship, names, languages, and physical types. The text treats these similarities between America, Asia, Hindostan, Asia Minor, and Egypt as possible evidence of ancient relations and communications.

records.l: architectural monuments, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: include burial places [among the compared subjects] The architectural monuments of the Chaldeans and Mayas are said to share superposed platforms, cardinal orientation, thick walls, flat roofs, narrow chambers, exterior staircases, and similar construction methods. Chaldean buildings used clay and bricks, while Maya buildings used stone.

records.l: writing systems of the Mayas and Egyptians, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The writing systems of the Mayas and Egyptians are described as combining phonetic, ideographic, and symbolic characters. They are read generally right to left in vertical columns and horizontal lines. The Mayas are said to use straight-lined signs enclosed in square or oblong figures, and their inscriptions are claimed to resemble Egyptian, Chaldee, and Etruscan characters.

records.l: burial places, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Burial places in Chaldea and Yucatan are compared through jar tombs, stone urns, coffins, and extensive artificial mounds. The burials could include dishes, vases, ornaments, and air holes.

records.l: etymology of the names of divinities, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The unit proposes that the Maya language provides etymologies for the names of Chaldean divinities that correspond with their attributes. It discusses Ra, Ana, Bil, Beltis, Hea, Sin, San, Vul, and Ishtar, among others.

records.l: Mesopotamia, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The lower Mesopotamian valleys are described as the region where the primitive Chaldeans settled. The Euphrates and Tigris are associated with the arrival of civilization attributed to Hea or Oannes.

records.l: Mugheir, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Mugheir is a place marked by sun-dried-brick building filling, possible brick-vaulted chambers, and associated jar tombs and hieratic inscriptions.

records.l: Euphrates, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Euphrates is named as one of the rivers to which Hea or Oannes brought civilization. The unit associates this civilization with astronomy and letters.

records.l: Tigris, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Tigris is named with the Euphrates as a river whose early settlers were taught astronomy and letters by Hea or Oannes.

records.l: Canon Rawlinson, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Canon Rawlinson, author of Five Great Monarchies, is cited on Chaldean clothing, religion, divine names, writing, brick arches, and Hea, Sin, Ishtar, while identifying Ra as God emphatically.

records.l: primitive Chaldean religion, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Primitive Chaldean religion is an elaborate outward polytheism whose divine figures are interpreted by attributes and proposed Maya-language etymologies, while esoteric explanations may reconcile its gods with monotheism.

records.l: Ra, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Ra is a god at the head of the Pantheon, described as a supreme sun god worshiped throughout Egypt. Its emblem is a disk or circle, sometimes topped by the serpent Uraeus. Ra is also placed at the head of the Chaldean pantheon and said to mean God in the highest sense, while related Maya terms mean that which exists, eternal truth, or truth.

records.l: Ana, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Ana is a God in the highest sense, father of the gods, associated with priority, antiquity, fatherhood, darkness, and death; his name is interpreted as A and Na, “thy mother.”

records.l: Bil, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Bil, said to mean Lord and associated with NIPRU, is Maya-interpreted as way or road, and therefore as origin, father, and procreator.

records.l: Beltis, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Beltis, Great Goddess and mother of the gods, is described as wife of Bil and Bel-nipru; Mulita and Enuta receive proposed interpretations.

records.l: Hea, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Hea or Hoa is a fish god, half man and half fish, linked with serpent and knowledge. Coming from the Persian Gulf, he teaches astronomy and letters to the first settlers on the Euphrates and Tigris; his name is interpreted as a house or residence on the water.

records.l: Sin, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Sin, also called Hurki, is identified first as a bright, shining moon deity and lord of the month, then associated with buildings and architecture, including Bel-Zuna as lord of building or strong house.

records.l: San, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is Sun God [lord of fire and ruler of the day] San or Sansi is identified as the sun god, lord of fire, and ruler of the day. His Maya-related interpretation is connected with Zamal, the morning or dawn.

records.l: Vul, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Vul, or Iva, is prince of the powers of the air and lord of wind, tempest, and thunderbolt; he is connected with Maya words for rubbing or scouring and Hul, an arrow.

records.l: Ishtar, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Ishtar, also called Nana, is identified as Chaldean Venus; proposed Maya interpretations describe Ishtar as desiring bodily satisfaction and Nana as the great mother.

records.l: temple of the seven lights, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: have seven stages [or platforms] The temple of the seven lights is identified with the supposed tower of Babel, the Birs-i-nimrud. It is described as having seven stages or platforms.

records.l: Chaldean writing system, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Chaldean writing system included letters proper, monograms, and determinative characters; inscriptions at Warka and Mugheir used hieratic straight-line signs enclosed in geometric figures.

records.l: Maya architecture, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Maya architecture uses stone in Yucatan to form mounds, cones, or pyramids of superposed platforms, often oriented toward cardinal points. Generally seven platforms rise by exterior staircases to the summit. Temples have thick walls, flat roofs, triangular-arched long narrow chambers, squared recesses, and an inner Sanctum Sanctorum.

records.l: Maya civilization, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: originates_in America [according to the text's argument] The text argues that Maya civilization developed independently of the civilizations of Asia and Africa, although some relations and exchanges may have existed. Its antiquity is associated with monuments, calendrical records, and other evidence that the author claims may extend back more than 6,000 years.

records.l: astronomy, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Maya astronomy is described as involving close observation of celestial bodies, mathematical calculation, latitude, solstices, the equator, and the Sun's declination. The text presents these abilities as comparable to those attributed to Egyptian and Chaldean scholars.

records.l: Chaldea, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: had_first_king Urukh Chaldea is associated with the name Arba-Lisun, interpreted as “the four tongues.” The text also connects Chaldea with the early use of a language that it claims was related to Maya.

records.l: Urukh, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Urukh is the first king of the Chaldees and a great architect. Credited with the most archaic monuments of the plains of Lower Mesopotamia, he conceived plans for the Babylonian Temple. His name is derived from HUK and LUK, interpreted as “to make everything” and “mud.”

records.l: Assyria, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Assyria is a place said to be named after the deity Asshur, though scholars dispute the derivation; its name is interpreted through the Maya form Axul as “thy end.”

records.l: Asshur, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Asshur is the supreme god of the Assyrians, called “my lord” when his name is pronounced. Interpreted through the Maya form Axul as “thy end,” Asshur is associated with the beginning and end of all things.

records.l: Maya calendar, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Maya calendar distinguishes a civil year of eighteen twenty-day months plus five unlucky supplementary days from a sacred or sideral year of 365 days and 6 hours.

records.l: Book of Daniel, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: A book recounting King Belshazzar’s banquet, where “Mene, mene, Tekel, upharsin” appeared on a wall and eluded wise men until Daniel interpreted them as “numbered, numbered, weighed, dividing”; it also claims corresponding Maya meanings.

records.l: Jesus of Nazareth, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Jesus of Nazareth is portrayed at his death on the cross, speaking words interpreted as “Helo, Helo, Lamah Zabac Ta Ni,” meaning that he is sinking and darkness covers his face. His final moments are characterized by resignation and fortitude, ending with “It is finished.”

records.l: the crucifixion of Jesus, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: included_last_words It is finished [as reported by St. John] The crucifixion of Jesus is described through differing Gospel reports of his final words. The text rejects the interpretation “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” and instead presents a Maya interpretation expressing that Jesus was sinking and darkness covered his face.

records.l: Khati, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Khati was a powerful nation inhabiting Cale-Syria and the Orontes valley, also known in Scripture as the Hittites. It resisted Egyptian and Assyrian conquest, developed military arts, and became prominent in trade through Katish, its sacred city, and Carchemish. Rameses the Great defeated it, as recorded at Thebes.

records.l: Thebes, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Thebes is a place in Egypt, capital of Upper Egypt during the XVIII dynasty. It is called No or Na-Amun by Jeremiah and Nahum, written AP or APE in Egyptian hieroglyphs, and formed as TAPE or Taba; Greeks converted its name into Thebai and Thebes.

records.l: Helo, Helo, Lamah Zabac Ta Ni, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: means darkness covers my face while I am sinking [literal Maya interpretation] “Helo, Helo, Lamah Zabac Ta Ni” is presented as a Maya phrase attributed to the final moments of Jesus of Nazareth. The text translates it literally as “Now, now I am sinking; darkness covers my face,” and treats it as an expression that all was over rather than despair.

records.l: Nile, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_called Hapimu [by the Western invaders, according to the text] The Nile watered the Egyptian valley and may have been called Hapimu by Western invaders. The text interprets Hapimu through Maya as HA, meaning water, and PIMIL, meaning the thickness or abyss of flat things.

records.l: Osiris, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Osiris is an Egyptian god, son of Seb and Nut, brother of Aroeris, Horus, Typho, Isis, and Nephthis, and husband and brother of Isis. He became king of Egypt, tried to civilize its people, taught cultivation of the earth, and traveled to encourage his discipline. Typho killed and dismembered him; Horus later defeated Typho. Osiris is king and judging ruler of Amenti, the western region and mansion of the dead, where he adjudges souls’ rewards and punishments according to earthly deeds. Some authors make him the personification of Nile inundations. He is particularly worshiped at Philo and is associated with leopard imagery and priestly leopard-skin dress.

records.l: Amun, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Amun is worshiped as a deity associated with Thebes, whose name No or Na-amun means Amun’s residence; represented as a man with a light-blue body, he signifies an exalted, heavenly nature.

records.l: Egyptian hieroglyphs, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: represent Egypt [with a land character and another character read K] Egyptian hieroglyphs for Egypt are described as combining a land sign with another character read as K, said to represent a sieve but possibly depicting a small boat. Thebes is written in hieroglyphs as AP or APE with the feminine prefix T.

records.l: immortality of the soul, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Both Egyptians and Mayas are said to have believed in the immortality of the soul. Their beliefs included postmortem rewards and punishments followed by a return to material life.

records.l: Egyptian and Maya common origin, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The topic argues that Egyptians and Mayas shared common descent or intimate remote-age communication. It presents alleged correspondences in deities, myths, names, royal relationships, rites, symbols, priestly practices, writing, dress, architecture, and scientific knowledge, culminating in identifications of Chaacmol with Osiris, Moo with Isis, and Aac with Typho and comparisons of animal and Sun imagery.

records.l: sun worship, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Egyptians worshiped the sun as RA and often called Egypt the Land of the Sun. The Mayas also worshiped the sun, preserved a related dance, and called Uxmal U LUUMIL KIN, the land of the sun.

records.l: Egyptian funerary beliefs, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: include reincarnation [souls return after three thousand years] Egyptian funerary beliefs included judgment by Osiris, the immortality and eventual return of souls, and the need to preserve bodies through embalming. Blue was described as the color used at Egyptian funerals.

records.l: Chaacmol statue removal, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_associated_with reincarnation [the statue was regarded as a future bodily tenement] During the attempted removal of the Chaacmol statue, the workers tried to collapse the mausoleum and bury the statue rather than allow it to be moved. After the narrator presented himself as a reincarnated companion of Chaacmol, they accepted the removal and worked willingly to bring the statue to the surface.

records.l: Chichen, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Chichen contains the funeral chamber and mausoleum associated with Chaacmol, mural paintings, sculptures, and inscriptions. Its monuments are said to depict Maya clothing, religious practices, rulers, warriors, and the use of the number seven.

records.l: Chaacmol's mausoleum, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Chaacmol's mausoleum is a mausoleum with three superposed apartments, polished and painted concrete floors, and exterior bas-reliefs. It contains two stone funeral urns holding remains interpreted as brains, heart, and other viscera; its painted chambers depict Chaacmol's life, contemporaries, and neighboring peoples.

records.l: Egyptian calendar, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Egyptian solar year is described as having twelve months of thirty days, followed by five additional days called Epact. These five days were considered unlucky, and the Egyptians are also said to have used a sideral or sothic year of 365 days and 6 hours.

records.l: number seven, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_a mystic number [among the Mayas and many ancient nations] The number seven is described as a mystic number among the Mayas, Egyptians, and many other ancient peoples. Maya monuments are said to display seven platforms, mounds, turrets, serpent rattles, and feathers, while the text also lists numerous Egyptian and other traditions involving seven.

records.l: Uxmal inscriptions, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Uxmal inscriptions are Maya-language inscriptions arranged in squares or parallelograms, combining phonetic, symbolic, and ideographic signs. They include characters resembling Chaldee, Egyptian, and Etruscan signs and were used to identify Uxmal’s founders.

records.l: Horus, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Osiris’s son, Horus ultimately defeats Typho after Typho killed and dismembered Osiris.

records.l: Typho, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Typho, brother of Osiris and Isis, murders Osiris from jealousy and a desire for the throne. He later steals Osiris’s remains from Isis, cuts them into pieces, and scatters them over the earth. His course ends when Horus defeats him.

records.l: Isis, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Isis is a goddess, wife and sister of Osiris, queen of the Amenti, and personification of Egypt’s irrigated portion. Represented with wings and a vulture, she searches for and recovers Osiris’s body after his death, but Typho later steals it. Her roles, western sovereignty, leopard symbolism, and female animal totem are compared with Moo.

records.l: Osiris myth, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_a mythological history [of Osiris in Egypt] The Osiris myth concerns Osiris's life on Earth, his efforts to civilize the world, his killing and dismemberment by Typho, Isis's search for his body, and Horus's defeat of Typho. The text compares parts of this myth with traditions of the Maya culture heroes Kukulean and Quetzalcoatl.

records.l: Osiris's civilizing journey, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Osiris's civilizing journey began after he became king of Egypt, teaching his countrymen to improve and cultivate the earth's fruits, then traveling throughout the world and using mild persuasion to bring people under his discipline.

records.l: Osiris's killing by Typho, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_a killing [of Osiris by his brother Typho] Osiris's killing by Typho is followed in the account by the disposal of his remains, Isis's search for his body, Typho's theft and dismemberment of it, and the scattering of the pieces over the earth.

records.l: Maya culture heroes, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: include Quetzalcoatl [as a culture hero of the Aztecs] The Maya culture heroes Kukulean and Quetzalcoatl are presented as having traditions resembling the account of Osiris's efforts to civilize the world.

records.l: Osiris mysteries, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Osiris mysteries were mysteries divided into lesser and greater grades. Candidates progressed through the lesser grades, demonstrated a virtuous life, and met further requirements before higher admission, regarded as a great honor. According to Wilkinson, they were the source of Eleusis mysteries.

records.l: Dwarf's House, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: contains Mayan affiliated signs and symbols [discovered there by the author] The Dwarf's House at Uxmal contained symbols and signs that the text interprets as evidence of Mayab's mysteries. Its rooms appeared to be dedicated to different gradations of initiation, apparently culminating in a third and highest grade.

records.l: Mayan initiation mysteries, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: have_grades three grades [the highest was the third] Mayan initiation mysteries are described as involving different gradations, with a highest or third level inferred from the number and arrangement of rooms in the Dwarf's House. The text also says that their affiliated members used signs and symbols resembling those of Freemasonry.

records.l: Mayan affiliated signs and symbols, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: resemble Freemasonry [perfectly identical in use among affiliated groups and masons] Mayan affiliated signs and symbols were discovered by the author in the Dwarf's House at Uxmal. The text says that they were perfectly identical to signs and symbols used among masons in their symbolical lodges.

records.l: Freemasonry, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: has symbolical lodges Freemasonry is used as a comparison for the Mayan affiliated signs and symbols. The text also says that Zuni sacred orders have secret rites carefully guarded like the secrets of Freemasonry.

records.l: Zunis, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Zunis are Pueblo Indians of New Mexico with twelve sacred orders, secret societies, priests, and secret rites, whose institutions are described as resembling Freemasonry.

records.l: Frank H. Cushing, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Frank H. Cushing, a gentleman sent by the Smithsonian Institution to investigate Zuni customs and history, secures adoption into the tribe, learns its language and habits, and reports twelve sacred orders.

records.l: Zuni sacred orders, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Zuni sacred orders comprise twelve orders with their own priests and carefully guarded secret rites, described as having a strange resemblance to Freemasonry.

records.l: Equatorial Africa, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: has_customs_resembling Yucatan [in many customs of its inhabitants] Equatorial Africa is presented as the region whose inhabitants share many customs with the Mayas. These customs include tooth filing, belief in sorcery, fermented honey-and-bark beverages, grave offerings and sacrifices, abandonment of places associated with death, large drums, fetish houses, native dogs, and protective leopard-skin charms.

records.l: Maya mural paintings, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Maya mural paintings at Chichen-Itza and elsewhere depict strongly marked African features, Moo in her home and garden, Chaacmol, Aac, Cay, followers, religious symbols, and story scenes; they are presented as evidence for alleged parallels with Egyptian mythology.

records.l: witchcraft, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Witchcraft is widely believed in by Mayas and their descendants from remote antiquity. Belief leads some, such as a sick man at X-Kanchacan, to attribute illness to spells and reject treatment; in Equatorial Africa, sorcery belief produces fear, suspicion, illness, and many murders.

records.l: Balche, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: is_a liquor [made from tree bark, honey and water] Balche is a fermented liquor made from the bark of the Balche tree, water, and honey. The Mayas used it in sacred ceremonies from remote antiquity and continued to use it in their rites.

records.l: African peoples, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: African peoples are described through customs and warfare: they file front teeth, drink honey-, water-, and bark-based beverages, make offerings and sacrifices at graves, abandon homes after repeated deaths, communicate with large drums, and wear charmed leopard skins believed to protect warriors from spears.

records.l: Du Chaillu, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Du Chaillu is cited as an observer of the customs of Equatorial Africa in his account of the Land of Ashango. His reports concern tooth filing, sorcery, fermented beverages, funerary practices, drums, fetish houses, native dogs, and leopard-skin charms, and the text uses his descriptions to compare African peoples with the Mayas.

records.l: Egyptian mythology, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Egyptian mythology is characterized as a transformed or mythical version of historical traditions that the author believes originated among the Mayas. The unit specifically compares its stories of Osiris, Isis, Typho, Aroeris, Nephthis, and Thoth with Maya figures, events, symbols, and monuments.

records.l: Maya migrations, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: Maya migrations move from Mayab into Hindostan, Afghanistan, Ethiopia, the Persian Gulf, Chaldea, Asia Minor, and Egypt, reaching Afghanistan and the Euphrates and spreading Maya names, languages, customs, traditions, religious ideas, and artistic practices.

records.l: Ake monument, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
records.s: The Ake monument consists of three immense superposed platforms supporting a structure with thirty-six katun columns. The columns record 5,760 years from the laying of the first stone to the final capping stone, and it may have been completed around the Spanish conquest.

records.l: Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: The Rough Diamond is a collection of frontier observations and connected tales of American character, centered on families, inheritance, violence, migration, and war from the early nineteenth-century western and southern frontier through the War Between the States. It opens with the narrator’s travels through Bush Bayou, across the Mississippi, and to Helena for the race between Silver Heels and the Spotted Buck, alongside accounts of Alonzo Phelps’s failed escape from execution and Daymon’s trial, overturned when his supposedly drowned wife appears alive. At Shirt-Tail Bend, Don and Dan Carlo’s wood-yard partnership collapses because Dan wastes money. Brindle Bill, S. S. Simon, and Sundown Hill try to swindle him, but Don fights for the money; Dan later dies, while Don is presumed dead or dying after the Red Stone explodes and is remembered as the Hero of Shirt-Tail Bend. The story then follows Tom Fairfield’s three daughters, Roxie, Rose, and Suza, separated after their impoverished father disappears in a snowstorm. Roxie becomes Roxie Daymon and dies of cholera; Rose is used by Brindle Bill and S. S. Simon in their effort to secure the Lasco inheritance, then dies childless of yellow fever. Suza escapes captivity, inherits Aunt Katy Demitt’s property, and later becomes engaged to Don Carlo, who recognizes her as his rescuer from the Red Stone wreck. A second generation centers on the Simon estate. Young Simon, a wealthy but dying planter, becomes engaged to Roxie Daymon’s grown daughter and wills her his estate, worth more than a million dollars. His cousin Cæsar Simon, also called Cole Conway, is identified as an heir by Steve Brindle and hires Gov. Morock to contest Simon’s will. Against a background of expanding cotton, slavery, railroads, and telegraphs, Cæsar serves in General Sterling Price’s army, is wounded at Wilson’s Creek, and is haunted by the number 77 and his treatment of Steve. The war destroys Missouri, Arkansas, and the Simon plantations. At Helena on July 4, 1863, General Holmes’s attack fails; Cæsar falls, ending the Simon male line. After the Southern surrender, Simon land is sold to satisfy judgments, and the remaining figures enter separate postwar lives.

records.l: the narrator, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: A living man of respectable parentage, educated in a log schoolhouse, he gained early experience navigating western rivers and observing character. Using fancy names and young surveying assistants, he recounts witnessed or traditional events rather than his own history, including a perilous Helena journey and observations of Alonzo Phelps and Daymon's trial.

records.l: Alonzo Phelps, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Alonzo Phelps, convicted of murder and sentenced to hang in Vicksburg, had committed his first murder in Europe and confessed to hiding Lasco family papers. On the day set for execution, he escaped jail, was pursued, and was shot dead by an officer.

records.l: Daymon, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Daymon, a young laborer and boat hand, conducted boats across Louisville’s falls, abused his wife while intoxicated, and was arrested and tried for allegedly drowning her in Beargrass Creek, pleading not guilty.

records.l: Roxie Fairfield, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Roxie Fairfield, also known as Roxie Daymon, is Tom Fairfield’s eldest daughter, a young, intelligent woman of unstained character. Educated briefly each year at a country school, she becomes the heroine of a snowstorm when she keeps her sisters warm and leaves their cabin to find help; Aunt Katy’s party rescues them, and Aunt Fillis Foster later takes her in. Roxie runs away with her lover Daymon, marries him by common law, and helps build a wealthy life in Chicago after leaving Louisville. She has one daughter and dies of cholera, unaware of Susan Lasco’s fate. After her disappearance, she is believed drowned, but appears alive in court after Daymon’s conviction.

records.l: Mississippi River, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Mississippi River is a great river with tributaries, central to steamboat navigation, the wood trade, and travel. In youth, a narrator crosses it at night in a heavily laden canoe through bank-full, turbulent water and driftwood, guided by a cabin light. Along its course, wood-cutters at Carlo wood yard and Shirt-Tail Bend fuel passing boats amid disputes over steam-navigation monopolies. The Brandywine burns after grounding on a deep sand bar, killing passengers. The river region then extends through plantations, cotton cultivation, and slavery.

records.l: Ohio River, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Ohio River is a principal western waterway near a round-log cabin and passing Port William. Its steam navigation helped create new industries, and supporters of free navigation prized its bank for boatmen’s songs and steam engines. A Kentucky-shore explosion sends victims into its waters; later it frames Suza Fairfield’s homecoming.

records.l: Helena, Arkansas, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Helena, Arkansas, is a point on the west bank of the river, three hundred miles above Vicksburg. Near its former town seat was race ground where Billy Horner and Henry Mooney raced ponies. Fortified by federals with three forts, Helena was attacked by General Holmes’s forces on July 4, 1863.

records.l: Arkansas, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Arkansas contains the large estate that Steve Brindle says S. S. Simon left to Cæsar Simon. Arkansas is the state where the legal contest over the Simon estate takes place. The unit also states that Steve Brindle served in Price’s army from Arkansas and that the Simon plantations were located there.

records.l: Louisville, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: is_located_between Pittsburgh [on the route to New Orleans] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] Louisville, Kentucky, was described as a principal point on the early route between Pittsburg and New Orleans. Its falls required boats to employ resident pilots, and the city was the setting of Daymon's murder trial.

records.l: Beargrass Creek, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: empties_into Ohio River [at the suburbs of Louisville] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] Beargrass Creek emptied into the Ohio near the suburbs of Louisville. Daymon's wife was believed to have been drowned there after her shoe and an unidentified woman's body were found along its margin, though she later appeared alive.

records.l: New Orleans, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: New Orleans is the destination of the pleasure trip taken by Roxie Daymon and the young people from Chicago. Young Simon and cousin Cæsar also travel there before continuing toward the West Indies.

records.l: THE ROUGH DIAMOND, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: The Rough Diamond is a work representing America as a New World and its frontier, pioneer past; in its opening introduction, it preserves pride in log-cabin beginnings and the character formed before later magnificence.

records.l: the race between Silver Heels and the Spotted Buck, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Near Helena, Arkansas, Silver Heels and the Spotted Buck contest a quarter-mile race for one hundred dollars. The Spotted Buck wins, though observers say jockeying decided it and Silver Heels was faster.

records.l: Alonzo Phelps's execution, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: is_scheduled_for the day of the narrator's observation [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] Alonzo Phelps's execution was scheduled to take place by hanging on the day he escaped from jail. He did not hang; he was killed by a rifle shot while fleeing from the jail.

records.l: the confession of Alonzo Phelps, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Alonzo Phelps’s confession ends the day before his execution by declaring that he will not hang. It recounts his first murder in Europe, describes placing the victim’s body atop a coffin in a newly made grave, and leads to discovery of papers taken from the victim.

records.l: Daymon's murder trial, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Daymon’s first-degree murder trial centers on evidence identifying a Beargrass Creek body and clothing as his wife’s; after court-appointed counsel and a guilty jury verdict, his wife enters alive.

records.l: Daymon's wife's disappearance, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: concerns Daymon's wife [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] Daymon's wife's disappearance caused great excitement in the neighborhood near Beargrass Creek. Searchers found a shoe believed to be hers and later a woman's body, prompting suspicion against Daymon and leading to his arrest.

records.l: Daymon's wife's apparent drowning, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: is_alleged_to_occur_in Beargrass Creek [based on circumstantial evidence] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] The apparent drowning was inferred from the discovery of Daymon's wife's shoe on the margin of Beargrass Creek and a woman's body in the creek. The body was badly damaged by fish and could not be recognized by its face, but witnesses identified its dress as one made for Daymon's wife; the conclusion was disproved when she appeared alive.

records.l: steam navigation, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: is_a fixed fact [by the period described] Steam navigation on the western waters is presented as a new era that creates unforeseen industries, including the sale of cordwood to steamboats. The Enterprise is said to have been the first steamboat to ascend the Mississippi River, while the Washington is connected with the legal challenge to exclusive claims over western steam navigation. The Supreme Court of the United States denied the monopolist's exclusive pretensions.

records.l: the American frontier and pioneer past, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: is_represented_by Rough Diamond [the country a hundred years earlier] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] The unit portrays the American frontier and pioneer past through log-school education, early settlement, river navigation, flatboats, keelboats, frontier travel, rough local communities, and dangers from animals and waterways. The narrator treats this earlier period as a formative part of American character and says the log cabin should remain dear to the American heart.

records.l: Don Carlo, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Don Carlo is Dan Carlo's brother and equal partner in the wood business, paying its expenses while Dan receives half the money. Associated with the Carlo wood yard, he supports the party seeking to improve society and is its silent spirit. After reading about Alonzo Phelps, he enters headquarters through a chimney, takes gambling-table money, defeats Brindle Bill, and becomes the Hero of Shirt-Tail Bend. Following the Red Stone explosion, papers from his pocket identify him as a recovered dead man, yet he survives after Suza Fairfield rescues him. He buys a small Kentucky farm, remains a bachelor, recognizes Suza at a camp meeting, courts her, and rides with her toward Port William.

records.l: Dan Carlo, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Dan Carlo, Don Carlo's brother and equal wood-business partner, receives half the sales money but spends it and repeatedly fails to reform. As Shirt-Tail Bend improves, he feels out of place. He goes to headquarters with Brindle Bill, S. S. Simon, and Sundown Hill amid plans to swindle him, then is found dead in a saloon.

records.l: Brindle Bill, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Brindle Bill is a five-foot-eight, square-shouldered man, strong as a buffalo, a little-working wood-chopper, former three-card-monte gambler, and bully of the settlement. A floating-population member raised in Port William, he leads the party favoring degradation and is Dan Carlo’s fast friend, yet joins a scheme against him. After fighting Don Carlo and leaving the new settlement, he conspires over the Lasco inheritance, pressures S. S. Simon, and is imprisoned for Lasco inheritance fraud.

records.l: S. S. Simon, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: S. S. Simon is a wood-yard proprietor, neighborhood planter, husband of Rose Simon Fairfield, and father of Young Simon. He helps Brindle Bill establish Rose’s Lasco inheritance claim through false testimony, takes control of the money, and uses Rose’s share to become a keen financier, acquire four thousand acres and more than six hundred slaves, and build a costly residence. A hard master who works relentlessly for wealth, he dies of swamp fever, deliriously calling for Roxie Daymon.

records.l: Simon's wife, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: is_a_leading_spirit_of the other party [the party seeking to improve society] Simon's wife recognizes that trouble is coming when Don Carlo goes toward headquarters. She secretly follows with a firebrand and sets the cane pile against the cabin ablaze when she hears the fight. She then drags her husband away and cries out in shame.

records.l: Susan Lasco, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
records.s: Susan Lasco, daughter of an English gardener and sister of John A. Lasco, emigrated with her father and later married Tom Fairfield. Her inheritance was a cart-load of gourds, though she and Tom hoped important papers would recover a family fortune. She became mother to Rose Simon Fairfield and other daughters, inherited John’s bequest with her descendants, experienced the jerks at a New Lights meeting, and died beside Tom in their cabin after a cold winter evening.

records.l: the wood-cutters, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
