records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: Yuba Bill stops the stagecoach after a fallen tree blocks the road near the site of a robbery six months earlier. While Bill and several passengers work on clearing the road, other members of the coach party take shelter in a cabin occupied by Hiram, Sophy, and Flo, the niece of Snapshot Harry, the alleged coach robber. Flo’s bold humor eases the tension caused by the family’s resentment of investigators and travelers. After the road is cleared, the passengers return to the coach, while the quiet, observant passenger and the box-seat occupant are said to have joined the clearing party.

records.l: Yuba Bill, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: Yuba Bill, the stagecoach driver, stops the coach when a fallen tree blocks the road and orders the stranger to bring a large wood axe. He is impatient with the passengers and the cabin’s occupants, but leads the road-clearing effort and returns after the obstruction is removed.

records.l: Ned Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: Ned Brice is the expressman traveling with the coach and initially reports that a tree has fallen across the road. He remains concerned about his duty and the key to the treasure compartment, accompanies the passengers to the cabin, and defends Yuba Bill’s roughness by mentioning the recent robbery.

records.l: Frank Frenshaw, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: Frank Frenshaw, editor of the Mountain Banner, offers to accompany the lady to the cabin and joins the other passengers there. He tries to suggest explanations for the family’s persecution but is interrupted by Flo’s laughter.

records.l: Heckshill, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: Sam Heckshill of Heckshill & Dobbs’s Flour Mills introduces the passengers at the cabin and uses a light, noncommittal philosophy to ease the awkward situation. He reaches for the whiskey and competes with Frenshaw for Flo’s attention.

records.l: Snapshot Harry, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: Snapshot Harry is identified as the man who stopped the coach six months earlier. Flo is said to be his niece, and she jokes that he will hold up the next Pioneer Coach to make enough money to send her to Europe.

records.l: Flora Dimwood, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: Flo is Snapshot Harry’s niece and a young woman with an audacious, attractive manner. She openly acknowledges her uncle’s identity, defends Hiram and Sophy against the stage company’s treatment, serves whiskey and coffee to the passengers, and playfully unsettles the expressman.

records.l: Hiram Tarbox, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: Hiram is one of the cabin’s occupants and is treated as an old cousin by Flo. He and Sophy have endured visits from constables, detectives, newspaper men, and other strangers because of their connection to Snapshot Harry, and he helps receive the passengers with an apathetic manner.

records.l: Mrs. Tarbox, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: Sophy is Hiram’s wife or close household companion and helps prepare coffee in the cabin. She complains that the stage company’s suspicion and persecution have made life difficult, while affectionately rebuking Flo for being a discredit and bother.

records.l: the quiet, observant passenger, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: The quiet, observant passenger reassures the lady that there is no immediate danger and criticizes the expressman indirectly for leaving his post. He refuses to go to the cabin at first, but is later reported to have joined the road-clearing party.

records.l: the coach party, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: The coach party is awakened when the stagecoach stops and becomes uneasy after learning that the obstruction is near the site of a former robbery. Several passengers shelter in the cabin, where Flo’s humor breaks the tension, and they later return hurriedly to the coach without questioning Yuba Bill as planned.

records.l: the stagecoach, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: The stagecoach is halted on a rainy night by a fallen tree across the road. It is near the location where the up coach was robbed six months earlier, and it resumes its journey after the passengers and road workers clear the obstruction.

records.l: the stage road, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: The road is obstructed by a fallen tree near a cabin and a former coach-robbery site. Yuba Bill and several helpers work to clear it, while the stranger warns that the coach might otherwise have gone down a canyon.

records.l: uncle Hiram's cabin, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: The cabin is an unpainted, four-roomed redwood structure with a fire but little other comfort or light. Hiram, Sophy, and Flo shelter the visiting passengers there with coffee and whiskey while the road is being cleared.

records.l: tree obstruction, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: The fallen tree lies across the road and forces the stagecoach to stop. Yuba Bill considers the coach’s regulation axe ineffective, obtains a larger axe and ropes, and leads the effort to remove the tree.

records.l: the coach robbery, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: The coach robbery occurred six months earlier less than a hundred yards from the cabin. The event caused continuing suspicion and official and public attention toward Hiram and Sophy because of their association with Snapshot Harry.

records.l: the road-clearing, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
records.s: The road-clearing is organized by Yuba Bill, who calls for passengers and the stranger to bring proper tools and help. Several outside passengers assist, and the quiet, observant passenger and the box-seat occupant are later said to have joined them.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: Yuba Bill's coach is stopped by a masked horseman and armed accomplices, who take the express box during a stage robbery. Brice discovers that the treasure, a packet of greenbacks, had already been removed from the box, apparently while he was away at a settler's cabin. Bill believes the thieves were sneaks or traitors among the passengers rather than Snapshot Harry, who would likely pursue them after discovering the deception. Brice decides to seek out Snapshot Harry, while Bill promises to protect him in his report to the company.

records.l: Yuba Bill, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: Yuba Bill guides the coach through the obstructed road and stops when a masked horseman orders him to halt. He prevents the expressman from using his rifle, has him surrender the express box, and later urges Brice to remain calm. Bill believes Snapshot Harry was not involved in the theft of the treasure and suggests that sneaks or traitors among the passengers took it.

records.l: Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: Brice, the expressman, prepares to defend the express box but obeys Yuba Bill's command to hand it down. He discovers that the lock has been forced and the packet of greenbacks is already missing, then tells Bill that he believes the money was taken while he was at the settler's cabin. After hearing about Snapshot Harry, Brice decides to find him.

records.l: Snapshot Harry, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: Snapshot Harry leads or is associated with the gang that stops the coach, but Bill insists that Harry did not arrange the tree obstruction or participate in the underhand theft. Bill expects Harry to discover that his gang has deceived him and pursue the thieves. He says Harry is more than half white, lives somewhere near a cabin in the bush, and has a crippled sister and her daughter.

records.l: Ned Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: The expressman reaches for his rifle when the coach is stopped, but Yuba Bill restrains him because the attackers have them covered. He hands the express box to one of the masked figures after finding that its lock has been forced and its packet of greenbacks removed.

records.l: the gang, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: The robbers stop the coach with a fallen tree, cover the passengers with hidden guns, and take the express box. The text suggests that other robbers or traitors had already removed the treasure before the main group stopped the coach.

records.l: Snapshot Harry's gang, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: Snapshot Harry's gang is scattered for miles after the robbery, and a posse is sent down the road in pursuit of Harry. Bill suspects that two sneaks or traitors who traveled as passengers may have taken the treasure without Harry's knowledge.

records.l: the stagecoach, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: The coach passes through a narrow opening between sections of a fallen pine tree before being halted by masked robbers. After the express box is taken, Yuba Bill drives it furiously for three miles to the first station, where it later departs with the passengers.

records.l: express box, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: The express box is surrendered to the robbers during the stage robbery. Brice has found that its lock was forced and manages to snap it shut again before handing it down, concealing that the treasure is already gone.

records.l: the recovered treasure, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: The treasure is a packet of greenbacks that was missing from the express box before the robbers took it. Brice believes it was removed while he was away at the settler's cabin, leaving the robbers with an empty box.

records.l: Tarbox's cabin, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: Brice had left the coach and gone to a settler's cabin before the robbery. He believes the treasure was taken during his absence.

records.l: the stage robbery, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
records.s: The stage robbery involves masked and armed men stopping Yuba Bill's coach, taking the express box, and allowing the coach to continue. The robbery is later revealed to have been preceded by the theft of the treasure from inside the box, possibly by passengers connected with the gang.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: Mr. Ned Brice visits Hiram Tarbox and his wife, using a flattering newspaper account of the robbery to gain their cooperation and learn how to reach Flora Tarbox and Snapshot Harry's secluded home. Brice follows a narrow mountain trail marked at times by Flora's footprints, crossing the ridge and the North Fork canyon into an isolated hollow. Near the hollow, an unidentified rifleman shoots Brice's hat, dispatch bag, and handkerchief without killing him. The rifleman then approaches, recognizes Brice as the expressman, and offers him whiskey at a cabin while Brice says he wants to see Snapshot Harry.

records.l: Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: Mr. Ned Brice brings Hiram Tarbox a copy of the Red Dog Clarion containing praise for Hiram's assistance during the robbery, then asks for directions to Flora Tarbox. He follows the mountain trail toward Snapshot Harry's home, survives several deliberately aimed rifle shots, and continues toward the shooter. He tells the shooter that he wants to see Snapshot Harry.

records.l: Yuba Bill, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: Yuba Bill is praised in the local press for his well-known coolness during the robbery. The newspaper account also says that Hiram Tarbox timely warned him about the obstruction.

records.l: Hiram Tarbox, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: Hiram Tarbox is delighted to read a newspaper account naming him as an esquire who helped remove the obstruction and provided hospitality to delayed passengers. He gives Brice directions to the hidden trail leading toward Harry's home, while warning him to look out for himself.

records.l: Flora Dimwood, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: Flora Tarbox has left the Tarbox cabin at sun-up and gone to her uncle's home. Her footprints mark parts of the difficult trail Brice follows, and Hiram's wife says Flora sometimes wanders outside the hollow when she becomes lonesome.

records.l: Snapshot Harry, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: Snapshot Harry lives in a secluded valley or hollow reached by a concealed trail from the road. Hiram says Harry visits the Tarbox cabin only on nights when the coach is not running and there is no travel. Brice travels toward the hollow intending to see him.

records.l: the stagecoach, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: The stagecoach was delayed by the tree obstruction and was then robbed. The newspaper account claims that, without Hiram Tarbox's warning to Yuba Bill, it might have crashed into the tree.

records.l: the stage road, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: The road passes the place where the tree was thrown down and runs along a mountain shelf above the North Fork canyon. A narrow trail parallels part of it while remaining hidden by thorn and brush, and the stage road eventually crosses the canyon on a high bridge.

records.l: obstruction site, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: The obstruction site is where the tree blocked the road and where the trail up the mountain begins. Brice uses this location to find the concealed route described by Hiram Tarbox.

records.l: the narrow mountain trail, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: The mountain trail is less than a foot wide in places and remains hidden from the road by brush while providing a view of the road below. It climbs to a ridge, descends through a wilder area, and ultimately leads toward the North Fork canyon and Harry's hollow.

records.l: North Fork, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: The North Fork flows through a canyon below the stage road and then turns along the mountain side. Brice follows a faint ledge beside its current while using Flora's footprint as a guide.

records.l: North Fork canyon, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: The North Fork canyon is enclosed by narrow, precipitous walls, with the stage road and its bridge hundreds of feet above. Brice reaches the canyon, crosses along a faint ledge formed by driftwood and cliff debris, and emerges near the isolated hollow.

records.l: outlaw's hollow, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: The outlaw's hollow is a small, secluded valley enclosed by surrounding heights and little buckeye-covered hills. It is inaccessible from the stage road's side because of a sheer cliff and is protected by difficult approaches.

records.l: tree obstruction, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: The tree obstruction was thrown across the road and was described in the newspaper as possibly the preliminary work of the robber gang. It was removed with Hiram Tarbox's assistance, and its location helps Brice find the mountain trail.

records.l: the stage robbery, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: The robbery receives extensive praise-filled coverage in the local press, including commendations of Yuba Bill, the young expressman, the passengers, and a lady passenger. The article also calls for a Vigilance Committee, though local readers apparently think the wealthy express companies can protect their own property.

records.l: shooting at Mr. Ned Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
records.s: An unseen marksman fires at Mr. Ned Brice near the hollow, piercing his hat, shooting through his dispatch bag, and tearing his handkerchief from his fingers. Brice realizes the shooter is under a sycamore and walks toward him; the marksman then emerges alive and treats the encounter as a test of Brice's courage.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: Brice tells Henry Dimwood, alias Snapshot Harry, that he knew the coach's lock had been forced and accepts blame for failing to warn anyone. Henry explains that two men from the gang secretly robbed the coach before the gang stopped it, making Yuba Bill and the coach victims of two robberies in one evening. Brice proposes recovering the greenbacks and turning the thief over to the express company, but Henry must consult his gang before agreeing. Henry sends Flora with Brice as a guide, and the two discuss their growing familiarity while traveling away from the gang's hideout.

records.l: Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: Brice tells Henry Dimwood that he knew the coach's lock had been forced when he handed down the box, but snapped it together again and accepted sole blame. He proposes working with Henry to recover the greenbacks and later travels with Flora, whose company protects him from questioning by the gang.

records.l: Snapshot Harry, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: Henry Dimwood, also known as Snapshot Harry, explains the circumstances of the two robberies and says the thief is trapped along the road. He listens to Brice's recovery plan, agrees to sound out the gang, and sends Flora to guide Brice safely away.

records.l: Flora Dimwood, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: Flora accompanies Brice as his guide and protection from the gang's questions. She jokes and flirts with him, gives him her handkerchief while offering to mend his, and reveals that Henry is protective of her because of his outlaw reputation.

records.l: Yuba Bill, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: Yuba Bill did not know about the first robbery when it occurred, but Brice told him at the station. Henry takes pleasure in the fact that Yuba Bill and his coach were robbed twice in one evening.

records.l: the gang, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: The gang includes about twenty-five men, each of whom has a share in the greenbacks. Two gang members secretly arranged the first robbery, while the rest later stopped the coach without knowing that those two had betrayed them.

records.l: the express company, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: Brice proposes that the express company be told that the stealthy introduction of robbers as passengers was not Henry's method. He suggests that recovering the greenbacks and delivering the thief to the company could earn a reward and its good opinion.

records.l: Tarbox's cabin, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: Tarbox's cabin is connected with the events surrounding the robbery because the two conspirators got a scout to cut down the tree by falsely claiming it was part of Henry's orders. The road from Tarbox's cabin to the bridge remains watched by Henry's men, trapping the escaped thief.

records.l: the stagecoach, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: The coach carried the greenbacks and was first robbed by two men who had taken seats as passengers. Henry's gang then stopped the coach as well, causing it to be robbed twice within half an hour.

records.l: the recovered treasure, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: The greenbacks were secretly taken from the coach before Henry's gang stopped it. The escaped thief still has them and is believed to be trapped on the watched road.

records.l: the robbery of greenbacks, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: The robbery of greenbacks was carried out by two men who were supposed to verify that the money was aboard and report to Henry's gang. Instead, they arranged a false obstruction, stole the money during the confusion, and fled.

records.l: the second robbery by the gang, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: The second robbery by the gang occurred after the first robbery and involved Henry's men stopping the coach in their usual manner. Henry emphasizes that Yuba Bill and the coach were therefore robbed twice in one evening.

records.l: Brice's recovery plan, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: Brice's recovery plan is to cooperate with Henry, retrieve the greenbacks, and deliver the culprit to the express company. Henry is willing to consider it but must first obtain the consent of the gang's approximately twenty-five shareholders.

records.l: the cynical traveler, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: One of the two conspirators was killed after being caught by a patrol and confessed that the escaped accomplice had the greenbacks. The surviving thief is trapped somewhere between Tarbox's cabin and the bridge, with the road and trail watched by Henry's men.

records.l: the stage robbery, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
records.s: The stage robbery involved the coach carrying the greenbacks and consisted of two separate robberies in one evening. The first was carried out secretly by two supposed scouts, and the second was the gang's later overt hold-up.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: Flora Dimwood secretly leads Brice through a buckeye thicket and along a narrow trail toward a hidden route up the mountain to the stage road. They find the cynical traveler dead beneath debris after apparently falling from the road, and Brice recovers the stolen greenbacks from his treasure belt. Flora persuades Brice not to return immediately to uncle Harry, warning that the gang may endanger him and the money. She directs Brice up a fallen pine and through an old waterway, then disappears among the trees as he escapes.

records.l: Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: Brice follows Flora Dimwood through a concealed trail and helps uncover the dead traveler. He removes the stolen greenbacks from the traveler's treasure belt, then accepts Flora's argument that he should escape with them rather than return immediately to uncle Harry.

records.l: Flora Dimwood, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: Flora Dimwood reveals a hidden route up the mountain that she has discovered while exploring the valley. She helps Brice find the stolen money, argues against taking it back to uncle Harry, and directs Brice up the fallen pine toward a trail leading beyond the cabin.

records.l: Snapshot Harry, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: Uncle Harry is associated with the guards and the gang controlling the hollow, and Flora says he must do what the gang says. Brice initially intends to return the recovered money to him, but Flora warns that the money may not remain safe in his possession.

records.l: the cynical traveler, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The cynical traveler from the coach is identified as the man who robbed it. He is found dead after apparently falling from the road above, with the stolen money still secured around his waist.

records.l: North Fork canyon, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: Flora pretends to lead Brice through the canyon so that anyone watching them will believe they have taken that route. Instead, she turns into the buckeye thicket before reaching it.

records.l: the mountain, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The mountain has towering, nearly perpendicular flanks marked by fissures, thorn, scrub, rocks, and fallen trees. Flora shows Brice a route ascending its side toward the stage road.

records.l: the stage road, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The stage road lies above the mountain and can be reached by the hidden route Flora shows Brice. The dead traveler apparently fell from this road while trying to escape.

records.l: the narrow mountain trail, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The narrow trail runs between the mountain wall and the river-side thicket. It is uneven and slowly ascending, and Flora leads Brice along it before taking him to the fallen pine.

records.l: the fallen pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The fallen pine has a long, partly upright trunk leaning against the mountain wall like a ladder. Flora instructs Brice to climb it to reach a cleft and an old waterway leading toward the stage road.

records.l: the dead traveler, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The dead traveler lies maimed beneath recently fallen debris and uprooted shrubs, with his head twisted under his shoulder. Brice recognizes him as the cynical traveler and finds the stolen greenbacks on his body.

records.l: the recovered treasure, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The stolen greenbacks are recovered intact from the dead traveler's treasure belt. Brice secures them inside his breast before escaping along Flora's hidden route.

records.l: the envelope, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The envelope containing the packet of greenbacks is found inside the traveler's treasure belt, with its seal still unbroken. Brice secures the envelope within his breast before climbing away.

records.l: the treasure belt, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The treasure belt remains around the dead traveler's waist beneath his torn shirt. Brice unloosens it and finds the envelope containing the stolen greenbacks inside.

records.l: the actual thief's death, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The man's death appears to have resulted from his attempt to escape along the road above, ending in a fall down the mountain. Brice believes the guards and uncle Harry might claim credit for the circumstances, but Flora challenges that conclusion.

records.l: the traveler's fall, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The traveler apparently falls from the road above onto the mountain flank, bringing rocks, brush, and debris down with him. His body is found below, while part of his clothing hangs from a bush higher up.

records.l: the robbery of greenbacks, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: The cynical traveler is identified as the person who robbed the coach. The money taken in the robbery is recovered from his body.

records.l: Brice and Flora's escape, From Sand Hill to Pine, "I am going to be a real guide to you now," she said suddenly.
records.s: Flora leads Brice away from the canyon through the thicket and along the mountain trail. She directs him up the fallen pine and waits below until he reaches the cleft, then disappears among the trees.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Edward Brice reaches San Francisco with the recovered treasure and reports to the manager, who keeps the affair out of the newspapers while arranging Brice's promotion. After receiving no replies to his letters, Brice follows a clue sent with his mended handkerchief and learns from Hiram Tarbox that Flora Dimwood is safe and attending a Catholic convent school. Flora reunites with Brice, explains that she buried the actual thief and burned the empty belt, and they begin courting. Tarbox reveals that the newspaper paragraph helped him become a land and timber agent and that Snapshot Harry may eventually sell his valley and water-power rights.

records.l: Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Edward Brice reaches San Francisco with the recovered treasure and confides the full story to the manager, who advises him to keep it out of the newspapers. He receives a company check and a promotion to the San Francisco office, then finds Flora and learns that his suspicions about her silence were mistaken.

records.l: Flora Dimwood, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Flora sends Edward Brice's repaired handkerchief as a clue to Hiram Tarbox's address and remains loyal by keeping the events in the hollow secret. She is placed in a Catholic convent school, reunites with Brice, and tells him that she buried the actual thief and burned the empty belt.

records.l: Hiram Tarbox, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Hiram Tarbox admits that he destroyed Brice's enclosed letter and initially refused to correspond, but explains that he had broken with Snapshot Harry and offered to take Flora with him. He has become a land and timber agent in San Francisco, is building a business, and is trying to persuade Harry to sell his valley and water-power rights.

records.l: Snapshot Harry, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Snapshot Harry is identified as Flora's uncle and as a former road agent whose niece has been separated from him. Tarbox is trying to persuade him to leave the valley and sell his rights in the valley and the water power on the Fork.

records.l: the manager, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: The manager believes Brice's account because Brice has not embellished himself as a hero. He keeps the story from the public, hands the recovered greenbacks to the company, and supports Brice's advancement.

records.l: the express company, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: The express company assumes the risk for the lost money and repays the shippers without publicizing its recovery. It sends Brice a letter of thanks and a check and promotes him from the road to its San Francisco office.

records.l: Snapshot Harry's gang, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Flora says Snapshot Harry's gang would have found the actual thief's body and the empty belt if she had not buried the body and burned the belt. She states that nobody knows what happened.

records.l: Catholic convent school, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Flora is placed in a Catholic convent school after her mother dies, a school that asks no questions about where its students come from and turns them out 'first-class plank all round.'

records.l: San Francisco, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Edward Brice arrives in San Francisco and is promoted to the company's office there. Hiram Tarbox also establishes his land and timber business in San Francisco, where Flora is temporarily staying with her mother.

records.l: the recovered treasure, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Edward Brice brings the recovered treasure to San Francisco and gives the treasured envelope to the manager. The manager hands the greenbacks over to the express company, which repays the shippers while keeping the recovery private.

records.l: Flora's handkerchief, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Flora returns Edward Brice's handkerchief by mail after having its bullet-rent carefully mended so that it nearly resembles embroidery. Its return, accompanied by Tarbox's printed address, gives Brice a clue that Flora has not forgotten him.

records.l: Edward Brice's letter, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Edward Brice sends Flora a letter enclosed in a letter to Hiram Tarbox, but receives no reply and later sends another. Tarbox admits that he destroyed the enclosed letter rather than act as a go-between.

records.l: the newspaper paragraph, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: The newspaper paragraph leads Tarbox to decide that association with Snapshot Harry is damaging and to break with him. It also brings Tarbox new business when Heckshill recognizes him as a 'well-known citizen' and asks him about timber lands.

records.l: the robbery and recovery, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: The robbery and recovery are reported privately to the manager rather than to the company's president, directors, or the public. Brice's recovery of the money earns him the company's thanks and promotion, while the company assumes responsibility for repaying the shippers.

records.l: the actual thief's death, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: The actual thief's death proves Brice's salvation by leaving him able to recover the money without being contradicted. Flora later says she buried the body so Snapshot Harry's gang would not find it.

records.l: Flora's mother's death, From Sand Hill to Pine, III In twenty-four hours Edward Brice was in San Francisco.
records.s: Flora's crippled mother dies three weeks before Brice's visit to Tarbox. Her death leaves Snapshot Harry free, after which Tarbox settles matters by taking Flora away from her uncle and arranging for her to attend a convent school.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A TREASURE OF THE REDWOODS PART I Mr.
records.s: Jack Fleming, a youthful prospector, becomes lost in the redwood forest while returning to camp and discovers a spring and quartz outcrop. He borrows a battered bread pan from Katinka Jallinger at her isolated cabin, leaving his gold specimen ring as a deposit. Fleming washes soil from the outcrop but finds only a few tiny flakes of gold, then returns the pan and retrieves his ring. He learns that Katinka's father, Henry Boone Jallinger, dislikes miners and lives by hunting, while Katinka is a seventeen- or eighteen-year-old young woman.

records.l: Mr. Jack Fleming, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A TREASURE OF THE REDWOODS PART I Mr.
records.s: Jack Fleming becomes lost in the redwood forest after leaving the path while returning from a mining town. He discovers a spring and quartz outcrop, borrows a bread pan from Katinka Jallinger, and finds only a few tiny flakes of gold while prospecting. He returns the pan, retrieves his gold specimen ring, and helps Katinka adjust her ill-fitting clothes.

records.l: Katinka Jallinger, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A TREASURE OF THE REDWOODS PART I Mr.
records.s: Katinka Jallinger, also called Tinka, lives at an isolated cabin with her father, Henry Boone Jallinger. She initially appears to Fleming to be a child because she wears oversized clothing and a large sunbonnet, but she is revealed to be a young woman of seventeen or eighteen. She lends Fleming the bread pan in exchange for his gold specimen ring and tells him that her father dislikes miners.

records.l: the redwood forest, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A TREASURE OF THE REDWOODS PART I Mr.
records.s: The redwood forest causes Fleming to lose his way because its thickly interlaced branches obscure the sun. Its decaying bark, dust, and primeval seclusion create a silent, gloomy environment. Fleming eventually reaches a rocky hillside and an opening leading toward the Jallinger cabin.

records.l: the Jallinger cabin, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A TREASURE OF THE REDWOODS PART I Mr.
records.s: The Jallinger cabin stands in an isolated green valley surrounded by a clearing and a roughly fenced cultivated area. Its exterior and fence are covered with the drying skins of animals and displayed wings of birds. Fleming visits it to borrow a pan and inquire about the road.

records.l: the prospecting pan, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A TREASURE OF THE REDWOODS PART I Mr.
records.s: Katinka lends Fleming the family's battered bread pan so he can wash soil for gold. The pan is leaky, with a damaged bottom, but Fleming uses it at the spring for two tests of soil from the quartz outcrop. He returns it to Katinka after finding little gold.

records.l: gold specimen ring, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A TREASURE OF THE REDWOODS PART I Mr.
records.s: Fleming leaves a small ring made from his first gold findings with Katinka as a deposit for the borrowed bread pan. Katinka reluctantly returns it when Fleming comes back, and he says that he values it very much.

records.l: gold, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A TREASURE OF THE REDWOODS PART I Mr.
records.s: Fleming finds only one or two minute yellow scales in each of his first tests, enough to show 'the color' but not a worthwhile result. The gold adheres to the bottom of the pan because of its specific gravity.

records.l: prospecting, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A TREASURE OF THE REDWOODS PART I Mr.
records.s: Fleming's instincts as a prospector lead him to return to the spring and quartz outcrop instead of leaving the forest immediately. He uses the borrowed pan to wash soil, but the prospecting attempt produces only a disappointing trace of gold.

records.l: lost way in the woods, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A TREASURE OF THE REDWOODS PART I Mr.
records.s: Fleming loses his way after deviating from the path to take a shortcut through the forest while daydreaming. He describes a circle familiar to people lost in the woods and eventually finds his way to the Jallinger cabin, from which he can return toward the main road.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: Mr. Jack Fleming receives a letter and gold flakes from Katinka Jallinger, who claims that gold escaped from his broken prospecting pan and appeared in biscuits made at the Jallinger cabin. Fleming returns to the spring and outcrop, finds no significant gold, and meets Katinka, who confesses that she salted the pan to make him come back. They investigate the Run and discover gold-bearing quartz, leading to Fleming and Katinka's engagement. Their discovery is associated with the Jallinger gold strike, while Fleming's partners remain skeptical of the story.

records.l: Mr. Jack Fleming, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: Mr. Jack Fleming works a mining claim with two partners but is described as not much of a miner. After receiving gold flakes and a letter from Katinka Jallinger, he investigates the spring and outcrop, discovers that the pan had been salted, and then finds gold-bearing quartz in the Run. He becomes engaged to Katinka Jallinger.

records.l: Henry Boone Jallinger, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: Mr. Jallinger is Katinka Jallinger's father, a religious hunter who dislikes miners and mining camps. He is said to have secretly prospected the lode and later makes a big strike at Lone Run, although the account is disputed by Fleming's partners.

records.l: Katinka Jallinger, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: Katinka Jallinger sends Fleming gold flakes and a letter to bring him back, but later admits that she salted his pan because she wanted him to return. She leads Fleming to the Run, where they find gold-bearing quartz, and becomes engaged to him.

records.l: Fleming's two partners, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: Fleming's two partners work the mining claim with him and gather enough gold for their daily wants. They misunderstand Mammy Curtis's visit as a billing matter and later suspect that Fleming's engagement story is false or incomplete.

records.l: the redwood forest, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The redwood forest contains the spring, the outcrop, and the secluded area where Fleming tests the soil. Fleming and Katinka meet there and briefly mistake their reflections in the spring for a romantic omen.

records.l: the spring, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The spring is near the outcrop and is used by Fleming to wash several pans of soil. It yields only a few pin-points of color and does not confirm a substantial discovery.

records.l: quartz outcrop, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The outcrop near the spring is tested by Fleming with borrowed mining tools. Several pans taken from it yield little or no gold, leading him to conclude that his apparent discovery was only a small pocket.

records.l: the Jallinger cabin, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The Jallinger cabin is near the spring and outcrop, and Fleming worries that locating a permanent claim there might offend Katinka's father. Katinka's father later plans to move farther into the mountains.

records.l: Lone Run, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: Lone Run is identified in the partners' discussion as the place where Mr. Jallinger made a big strike.

records.l: the Run, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The Run is a half-dried watercourse beyond the Jallinger cabin that Katinka says nobody has visited since her father dug a well. Fleming and Katinka investigate it and find a fragment of quartz seamed and celled with gold.

records.l: the mining claim, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The mining claim is worked for three months by Fleming and his partners, producing exercise, independence, and enough gold to pay their daily wants. Fleming considers putting up a notice of claim at the spring and outcrop but initially decides against it.

records.l: the prospecting pan, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: A broken prospecting pan brings gold flakes to light when Katinka uses it to mix bread dough. Fleming later borrows another pan to test the spring and outcrop, and Katinka uses the pan he brought to the Run while searching for the real source of the gold.

records.l: the folded letter, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The folded letter is written by Katinka on a leaf from an old account book. It explains that gold flakes appeared in biscuits made with the pan Fleming had brought back and tells him about the supposed discovery.

records.l: the cardboard box, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The cardboard box is given to Fleming by Mammy Curtis along with the folded letter. It contains three flakes of placer or surface gold weighing about a quarter of an ounce.

records.l: the gold flakes, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The gold flakes appear in biscuits made from dough mixed in Fleming's broken pan and are sent to him in a small box. They initially persuade Fleming that his washing may have uncovered a valuable deposit, but Katinka later reveals that she had planted the gold in the pan.

records.l: the gold-bearing quartz, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The gold-bearing quartz is uncovered in the Run after Fleming's pick causes part of the bank to cave. The fragment is honeycombed with gold and reveals the genuine richness of the deposit.

records.l: the mining operation, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The mining operation consists of Fleming and his two partners digging and washing material from their claim. Their work provides healthy exercise and enough gold for daily needs, but Fleming is regarded as an inefficient miner.

records.l: Fleming's gold discovery, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: Fleming first believes he has discovered gold near the spring and outcrop, but repeated tests show only a small amount of color. His genuine discovery occurs later in the Run, where he uncovers gold-bearing quartz.

records.l: the Jallinger gold strike, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: The Jallinger gold strike is the major discovery associated with the Run and with Mr. Jallinger's property. Fleming's partners say that Fleming never struck anything and that Mr. Jallinger passed the strike to him through his connection with Katinka.

records.l: Katinka's salting of the pan, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: Katinka's salting of the pan involved placing gold in Fleming's pan to make him believe he had found a deposit. She confesses that she did this because she wanted Fleming to come back.

records.l: Jack Fleming and Katinka Jallinger's engagement, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II Mr.
records.s: Jack Fleming and Katinka Jallinger's engagement is announced two weeks after their discovery in the Run. The engagement excites skeptical discussion among Fleming's partners, who debate whether Fleming won Katinka through his mining or through his relationship with her.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Cissy Trixit, the acknowledged belle of Canada City and daughter of banker Montagu Trixit, prepares to go out wearing her new hat. She and Miss Piney Tibbs parade through town, receiving the attention of miners, townsmen, and other residents before visiting the Reverend Mr. Windibrook's parsonage. Cissy dismisses the young engineer, Masterton, while Piney finds him attractive and respectable. On her return, Cissy notices that the townspeople are unusually preoccupied and that crowds have gathered around her father's bank and the newspaper office, leaving her vaguely frightened and confused.

records.l: Cissy Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Cissy is the acknowledged belle of Canada City and the daughter of its principal banker. She is vain about her new hat, socially imperious, and largely unaware of her father's business or the responsibilities surrounding his wealth. After visiting the parsonage, she returns through town and becomes uneasy when people avoid her and crowds gather around the bank and newspaper office.

records.l: Miss Piney Tibbs, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Miss Piney Tibbs is Cissy's bosom friend and a girl only slightly less pretty than Cissy. As the hotel-keeper's daughter and Cissy's protégée, she is conscious of their difference in social position, but remains loyal to Cissy. She admires the young engineer and accompanies Cissy on her parade through town before leaving her at the parsonage.

records.l: Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Montagu Trixit is Cissy's father and Canada City's principal banker, reputed to be a fearless and highly successful speculator. The Reverend Mr. Windibrook says that Trixit made fifty thousand dollars in a Comstock deal and gave one thousand dollars toward a new organ. He is away, apparently in San Francisco, while Cissy remains unaware of the details of his business.

records.l: Canada City, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Canada City is a new, glaringly unpicturesque mining town set among mountains, canyons, and pines. Its residents treat Cissy and Piney as a civic spectacle when they walk down Main Street. By Cissy's return, groups of townsmen are preoccupied, crowds surround the bank and newspaper office, and an extra carries news that visibly alters the town's mood.

records.l: Cissy and Piney, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Cissy and Piney go out together in Cissy's new hat, intending to walk down Main Street, view the town's reaction, and visit the parsonage. They receive bows, removed obstacles, and other signs of public attention as they pass through Canada City. Piney leaves Cissy at the parsonage and returns home.

records.l: young Masterton, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Young Masterton is the new engineer of the mill works and the son of Judge Masterton, with wealthy relations. He works alongside common laborers to understand how the mill operates and why the old works failed. Cissy considers him conceited and disrespectful, while Piney regards him as smart, well educated, and attractive; he later greets Cissy with unusual gravity.

records.l: the miners and townsmen of Canada City, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: The miners and townsmen of Canada City enthusiastically honor Cissy and Piney as they pass, removing obstructions, taking off their hats, and interrupting their work or horseplay to watch them. Later, groups of men gather around the bank, newspaper office, and a newspaper extra, becoming so preoccupied that they avoid noticing Cissy.

records.l: Montagu Trixit's bank, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: The Canada City Bank is identified as Cissy's father's bank, and Montagu Trixit is known as its principal banker. A large crowd gathers around the bank while Cissy is returning home, contributing to her growing fear that something is wrong.

records.l: Cissy's new hat, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Cissy's new hat comes from the best milliner in San Francisco and is an object of pride and vanity to her. She expects it to impress Piney, the Secamp girls, and the townspeople, and uses it as a reason to parade down Main Street. On her return, she briefly suspects that the hat may be the cause of the town's strange reaction.

records.l: the banker's wealth, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: The banker's wealth gives Cissy an elevated social position and helps make her the acknowledged belle of Canada City. Cissy assumes that her father's money can secure opportunities for Piney's father and regards the family's prosperity as a natural consequence of being Montagu Trixit's daughter. The Reverend Mr. Windibrook praises Trixit's speculative success and donations.

records.l: Cissy's visit to the parsonage, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Cissy visits the Reverend Mr. Windibrook and his family at the dwelling known as the Pastorage. Mr. Windibrook boasts about Montagu Trixit's financial success, while Mrs. Windibrook discusses the Secamp girls, young Masterton, and the supposed dangers of Canada City's rough society. Cissy enjoys the visit somewhat, plays with the younger Windibrooks, climbs a tree, and leaves after tea.

records.l: the parade-like progress through Canada City, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Cissy and Piney's walk through Canada City resembles a civic procession because residents stop to watch and honor them. Men remove their hats and obstructions, miners and workers pause, riders perform displays, and Vaquero Billy rears his mustang before them. Cissy enjoys the attention and assumes a slightly haughty air, while Piney shares in the reflected glory.

records.l: Cissy's upbringing and social privilege, From Sand Hill to Pine, " A BELLE OF CANADA CITY Cissy was tying her hat under her round chin before a small glass at her window.
records.s: Cissy has grown up as Montagu Trixit's daughter in the most prominent house in Canada City, which has an unusually luxurious double drawing-room and a carefully landscaped garden. Since her mother's death, she has treated her father's wealth and authority as constant and natural, without understanding his business responsibilities. Her social privilege makes her confident that the town will defer to her and that her father can satisfy her wishes.

records.s: Cissy receives a note from Piney saying that Piney's father will not let Piney come to her then, though Piney will try to slip out late that night. After the messenger leaves, Cissy discovers that the house is empty, with the kitchen left open, fires burning, and dishes on the table. A damp newspaper extra reports that Montagu Trixit has absconded, 50,000 dollars are missing, and there is a run on the bank.

records.s: Cissy Trixit learns that her father is accused of stealing money from the Canada City bank and fleeing, while the family house has been placed in the hands of the law. She rejects Mr. Windibrook's condemnation and offer of shelter, then receives a note and key from Ah Fe directing her to retrieve an envelope marked "Private Contracts." Cissy takes the envelope and some of her father's money, then disguises herself in an older dress and leaves with Ah Fe to find Hop Li.

records.l: Cissy Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, Then, in a revulsion of feeling lest any one should find her there, she ran upst
records.s: Cissy believes her father's alleged theft is a wicked lie and fiercely denounces Mr. Windibrook for condemning him after previously praising him. When told that the family house is in the hands of the law, she refuses to leave until her father tells her to go, but then takes the private contracts envelope and some of her father's money and secretly leaves with Ah Fe to find Hop Li.

records.l: Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, Then, in a revulsion of feeling lest any one should find her there, she ran upst
records.s: Cissy's father is accused of stealing money from the Canada City bank and fleeing, leaving her to face the disgrace. He sends Cissy a note and a small key instructing her to retrieve an envelope marked "Private Contracts" and give it to the bearer.

records.l: Canada City, From Sand Hill to Pine, Then, in a revulsion of feeling lest any one should find her there, she ran upst
records.s: Canada City is the community whose townspeople turn away from Cissy after hearing of her father's alleged crime. Mr. Windibrook says Cissy's father helped make Canada City what it was.

records.s: A run occurs on the Canada City bank, prompting Norah to withdraw the money she had deposited there. Cissy's father is accused of stealing money from the bank and running away.

records.s: The bank run causes people to withdraw their money from Cissy's father's bank. Norah hears about it from Jim and goes to take out her own money.

records.l: Mr. Windibrook, From Sand Hill to Pine, Then, in a revulsion of feeling lest any one should find her there, she ran upst
records.s: Mr. Windibrook visits Cissy and urges her to present her father's church donation and liberality favorably if questioned. He offers to have her stay with Mrs. Windibrook, then angrily calls Cissy's father a thief and felon; Cissy denounces him as a hypocrite and drives him away.

records.l: Norah, From Sand Hill to Pine, Then, in a revulsion of feeling lest any one should find her there, she ran upst
records.s: Norah, the cook, tells Cissy that Jim warned her about the run on the bank and that she should withdraw the money she had deposited. She also informs Cissy that Mr. Windibrook and a man on the veranda are waiting for her.

records.s: The sheriff's officer on the veranda represents the authority taking possession of the house and its contents. He explains that the house is in the hands of the law and later permits Cissy to set aside personal keepsakes before an inventory and sealing are completed.

records.l: Ah Fe, From Sand Hill to Pine, Then, in a revulsion of feeling lest any one should find her there, she ran upst
records.s: Ah Fe secretly gives Cissy her father's note and key, then helps her retrieve the envelope and carry it away. He explains that the note passed through several Chinese messengers and agrees to take Cissy to Hop Li.

records.l: Hop Li, From Sand Hill to Pine, Then, in a revulsion of feeling lest any one should find her there, she ran upst
records.s: Hop Li is identified as the person who gave the envelope to the next Chinese messenger after receiving it through the messenger chain. Cissy leaves with Ah Fe to find him.

records.s: The Chinese messengers pass Cissy's father's note from one person to another to prevent an American man from intercepting it. Ah Fe says the envelope will be sent onward through the same chain.

records.s: The family house is seized because it is in the hands of the law, and a sheriff's officer is stationed there. Cissy realizes it is no longer hers and leaves it through the back way.

records.s: The law takes possession of the family house and everything it contains. The sheriff's officer has not yet completed an inventory or sealed the property when Cissy removes the envelope and money.

records.s: Cissy hears that her father stole money from his own bank and fled, leaving her to bear the consequences. She rejects the accusation as a jealous lie, while Mr. Windibrook calls him a disgraced felon who cannot show his face in Canada City.

records.s: Norah withdraws her own money from the bank during the run, believing she is taking it from the people who are drawing it out and dividing it. Cissy finds a small roll of greenbacks in her father's desk and takes it with the private contracts envelope.

records.s: The envelope marked "Private Contracts" is in the second drawer of Cissy's father's desk. Cissy retrieves it with the small key and gives it to Ah Fe for delivery through the Chinese messenger chain.

records.s: Cissy's father sends a small key with his note. Cissy uses it to open the second drawer of his desk and retrieve the private contracts envelope.
