records.s: The note tells Cissy to take the envelope marked "Private Contracts" from the second drawer of her father's desk and give it to the bearer. It reaches her through Ah Fe after being passed among Chinese messengers.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: The failure of Montagu Trixit's bank caused widespread excitement, distrust, and suspicion in Canada City, though the reported defalcations were exaggerated. Montagu Trixit was linked to the suspended Excelsior Bank and had fled eastward across the Sierras, but was believed to be hiding near the Summit. The directors of the New Mill sent Dick Masterton to locate Trixit and, if possible, obtain an interview with him. They hoped to recover securities that Trixit held privately for money advanced to the New Mill, because he might declare them as assets of his bank.

records.l: Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: Montagu Trixit was the disgraced manager of the bank and a managing director of the Excelsior Bank. He had fled eastward across the Sierras but was believed to have been stopped by frontier police and to be hiding, possibly near the Summit. He privately held securities belonging to the New Mill for money he had advanced to it.

records.l: Montagu Trixit's bank, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: Montagu Trixit's bank failed amid reports of defalcations, though the amount was said to have been exaggerated. The bank was closely identified with Trixit, and there was concern that he might declare the New Mill's securities as its assets.

records.l: failure of Montagu Trixit's bank, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: The failure caused excitement that lasted until midnight and produced widespread distrust and suspicion. It threatened the fortunes of those who had invested in the bank and raised fears that others were implicated.

records.l: Excelsior Bank, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: The Excelsior Bank of San Francisco had been suspended before Montagu Trixit's bank failed. Its suspension followed the discovery that securities had been withdrawn for use in the branch bank at Canada City, and Trixit was one of its managing directors.

records.l: Canada City, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: Canada City was associated with the bank and its operations; a branch bank there had used withdrawn securities. Even Trixit's enemies acknowledged the saying that Canada City was the bank and the bank was Trixit.

records.l: securities, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: Securities had been withdrawn for use in the Excelsior Bank's branch bank at Canada City. Other securities were held by Trixit for the New Mill and might be declared as assets of his bank.

records.l: directors of the New Mill, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: The directors of the New Mill held an excited meeting and summoned Dick Masterton. They selected him to locate Trixit, seek an interview if possible, and recover the securities Trixit held for the mill.

records.l: New Mill, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: The New Mill had kept itself aloof from the bank and its methods. Nevertheless, it had received money advanced privately by Trixit and faced financial danger because securities connected with that advance did not appear on its books.

records.l: meeting of the directors of the New Mill, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: The meeting was held in an atmosphere of excitement after the bank's failure. During it, the president told Dick Masterton about the securities held by Trixit and assigned him the mission of finding Trixit and recovering them if possible.

records.l: Dick Masterton, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: Dick Masterton was the New Mill's engineer and was hurriedly summoned to the directors' meeting. Though disgusted by the purpose of the assignment, he accepted the adventurous mission to find Trixit and possibly obtain an interview. He rejected the suggestion that he seek information from Trixit's daughter because he was acquainted with her.

records.l: mission to find Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: The mission was to discover where Montagu Trixit was and, if possible, procure an interview with him. It also required finding and obtaining the securities held by Trixit for the New Mill; Masterton was instructed to take the up stage that night and make inquiries at Trixit's house if appropriate.

records.l: securities held by Montagu Trixit for the New Mill, From Sand Hill to Pine, The excitement over the failure of Montagu Trixit's bank did not burn itself out
records.s: Trixit held the New Mill's securities for money he had advanced to the mill privately. The securities did not appear on the New Mill's books, and the mill feared that Trixit might declare them as assets of his bank or that they would be lost if he escaped or committed suicide.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: Mr. Masterton travels by mountain wagon toward the next station while pursuing a mission connected with Montagu Trixit, whose financial scandal has prompted a staged search. During a severe snowstorm, the coach becomes stuck, and Masterton learns that Trixit may be hiding nearby and that Jake Poole, a deputy sheriff, is also involved. Suspecting that Chinese travelers are acting as spies through a signaling system, Masterton takes a saddled mustang and follows one of them toward a prospector's ruined hut. His horse breaks through the snow near the summit, throwing him into a suffocating depth and rendering him unconscious.

records.l: Dick Masterton, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: Mr. Masterton travels by mountain wagon toward the next station while reflecting uneasily on his mission and on Cissy's father's disgrace. After hearing that Montagu Trixit may be nearby, he takes a saddled mustang and follows a Chinese messenger toward the prospector's ruined hut, but his horse plunges through the snow and he is knocked unconscious.

records.l: the coach, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The coach is a heavy, lumbering mountain wagon that has replaced the smart Concord coach. It struggles through a severe snowstorm, is converted to a sledge, and finally becomes stuck in deep, wet snow.

records.l: the driver, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The driver expresses strong hostility toward Chinese people in California and tells stories about their supposed signaling methods. He drives into the storm, helps attempt to convert the wagon into a sledge, and later leads the passengers toward the next station.

records.l: Chinese people in California, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: Chinese travelers are seen walking along the mountain road in groups, wearing sheepskin jackets, blue blouses, and heavy leggings. The driver portrays them as widespread, secretive, and coordinated, while the narrative shows them warning one another and possibly assisting Montagu Trixit.

records.l: Cissy Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: Cissy's flushed and defiant face stays in Mr. Masterton's thoughts. He believes that her father's disgrace and the loss of her social position will deeply affect her, despite her frivolity.

records.l: Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: Cissy's father has been disgraced through methods connected with the financial scandal. Mr. Masterton had previously regarded him with contempt and had treated his daughter with tolerant pity because of her pride in her father's position.

records.l: directors of the New Mill, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: Mr. Masterton learns that his own directors used the methods associated with Cissy's disgraced father. The directors are also described as wanting a public search for Montagu Trixit to satisfy the stockholders.

records.l: Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: Montagu Trixit is believed to be hiding somewhere near the mountain stations, possibly near a prospector's cabin. He allegedly possesses papers that could frighten influential men and has managed to send a telegraphic dispatch from Black Rock station despite the search.

records.l: Jake Poole, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: Jake Poole is identified as a deputy sheriff traveling with Mr. Masterton under the pretense of hunting Montagu Trixit. He appears to be acting under orders and is seen approaching the Chinese group, causing one of them to act as a messenger.

records.l: the San Francisco detectives, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The San Francisco detectives have come up the mountain to conduct a search for Montagu Trixit. Their pursuit is described as a public show intended to satisfy stockholders, and they are misdirected toward Chinese travelers near a prospector's cabin.

records.l: the bar-room lounger, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The bar-room lounger tells Mr. Masterton that Jake Poole is a deputy sheriff and that the search for Montagu Trixit is largely a performance. He also reports rumors about Trixit's hiding place, his alleged papers, his spies, and a saddled horse kept ready for his escape.

records.l: the horses, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The four horses pull the mountain wagon through rocky defiles and the snowstorm. They become exhausted and flounder in the accumulating snow before the wagon is converted into a sledge.

records.l: Masterton's horse, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: A mustang is found tethered, saddled, and bridled in the station's shed, apparently prepared for Montagu Trixit's escape. Mr. Masterton takes it and rides after the Chinese messenger, but it crashes through the snow crust and plunges into a hidden depth.

records.l: the mountain road, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The mountain road passes through rocky defiles, terraces, and steep descents, with stations and occasional travelers along it. The snowstorm first leaves parts of it bare and wind-swept, then covers it deeply enough to stop the wagon.

records.l: the next station, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The next station is less than a mile away from where the wagon becomes stuck. The driver leads the passengers there by a narrower, more sheltered trail, and they warm themselves around a stove in its bar-room.

records.l: the prospector's ruined hut, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The prospector's ruined hut is believed to be near the summit and is treated as a possible hiding place for Montagu Trixit. A Chinese messenger heads toward it while Mr. Masterton follows.

records.l: the snowstorm, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The snowstorm changes from fine, gritty pellets driven by a keen wind into enormous flakes that fall like an avalanche. It blankets the wagon, horses, passengers, and road, stops the vehicle, and later creates a crust and hidden depths that cause Mr. Masterton's horse to fall.

records.l: interview with Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: Mr. Masterton's mission is to reach Montagu Trixit, though he finds its nature unpleasant and feels some self-reproach about it. The storm, the suspected Chinese spies, and Jake Poole complicate the mission, but also appear to give him an opportunity to reach Trixit first.

records.l: mission to find Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The search for Montagu Trixit involves San Francisco detectives, Jake Poole, and supposed spies among the Chinese travelers. It is presented as partly staged for the stockholders, while the real pursuit is obstructed by warnings and misinformation.

records.l: the financial scandal, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The financial scandal has resulted in Cissy's father's disgrace and the loss of the social position that supported her family's prosperity. Mr. Masterton realizes that his own directors benefited from the disgraced man's methods.

records.l: the Chinese signaling system, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The driver claims that Chinese travelers can warn one another through coordinated signals, including funeral paper carried by the wind. A story is told in which a Chinese man burns or scatters paper and another group escapes before an attack; the travelers later alter their route after apparently recognizing Jake Poole.

records.l: the papers hidden with a friend, From Sand Hill to Pine, A few hours later he was on the coach.
records.s: The papers hidden with a friend are said to contain information that could frighten important men connected with Montagu Trixit. Their existence is presented as one reason Trixit may be protected and dangerous to capture.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Masterton regains consciousness in a Chinese hut after falling into a prospector's hole while pursuing Cissy Trixit. Cissy, disguised as a Chinaman, saved him and explains that she traveled secretly to find her father, Montagu Trixit. Montagu tells Masterton that the proceedings against him have stopped and offers to return the securities if the directors send renewed notes to Sacramento within three days. Masterton and Cissy travel toward the station, and Masterton agrees to follow her to Sacramento.

records.l: Dick Masterton, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Masterton is rescued after lying unconscious and nearly frozen in a prospector's hole. He learns that Cissy saved his life, admits that he came under orders from his directors to see Montagu Trixit, and agrees to go to Sacramento after Cissy tells him he will be there.

records.l: Cissy Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Cissy reveals that she disguised herself as a Chinaman and traveled to find her father. She saved Masterton after his fall, arranged for him to be cared for, and accompanies her father toward Sacramento.

records.l: Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Montagu meets Masterton at the hut and says he is going directly to Sacramento. He has the securities and offers to return them if the directors send renewed notes to Sacramento within three days.

records.l: directors of the New Mill, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: The directors ordered Masterton to pursue a business interview with Montagu Trixit. They are told to send renewed notes to Sacramento if they want the securities returned.

records.l: the two Chinamen, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Several Chinamen rescue Masterton from the snow, rub him with loose snow, wrap him in warm blankets, and bring him to a hut. One Chinaman helps Cissy travel and another helps her pull Masterton from the hole.

records.l: Canada City, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Masterton first met Cissy in the new church at Canada City. Cissy says she will never return there after leaving to find her father.

records.l: Sacramento, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Montagu is traveling to Sacramento, where he intends to go directly. Cissy says she will go there with her father, and Masterton agrees to follow her there in three days.

records.l: Black Rock station, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Montagu goes to the station to fetch Cissy's clothes and later gives Masterton a lift there in a covered sleigh. The securities and Masterton's business message are discussed before they leave.

records.l: securities held by Montagu Trixit for the New Mill, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Montagu shows Masterton the securities and says they are safe in his hands and have not been seen by anyone else. He agrees to return them after receiving the directors' renewed notes in Sacramento within three days.

records.l: the renewed notes, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: The renewed notes are to be sent to Montagu in Sacramento, dated from the day of the agreement. Their delivery within three days is the condition for the return of the securities.

records.l: Cissy's Chinese disguise, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Cissy obtained Chinese clothes from her family's laundryman, traveled in wooden sandals, and concealed her hair beneath a battered conical hat. She says that no white man detected the disguise, although part of her brown braid escaped and Masterton noticed it.

records.l: interview with Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Masterton came to see Montagu on the order of his directors. He says the intended interview was a business matter that might have been as much in Montagu's interest as his own.

records.l: the pursuit, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Masterton pursued Cissy while she was disguised as a Chinaman. She says she would have outrun him even with his horse's help, but turned back after he fell into the prospector's hole.

records.l: Masterton's fall, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Masterton fell into a prospector's hole with his horse, whose neck was broken, on top of him. He was badly bruised and shaken, but Cissy and another Chinaman pulled him out and saved his life.

records.l: Cissy's journey to find her father, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Cissy traveled alone with Chinese guides, mostly on foot, to find her father. She passed from one Chinaman to another, sometimes being carried on a pole, while avoiding shops, restaurants, and sleep in Chinese dens.

records.l: the proceedings against Montagu Trixit, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: The proceedings against Montagu have been stopped, leaving him free to go where he likes and meet whom he likes.

records.l: the agreement to return the securities, From Sand Hill to Pine, How long he lay there thus he never knew.
records.s: Montagu agrees to return the securities if the directors send their renewed notes, dated from that day, to Sacramento within the next three days. He gives Masterton this message to deliver to the directors.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: The editor of the Mountain Clarion, Mr. Grey, discusses Colonel Starbottle's reported horse accident with his foreman, Richards, who suspects the colonel was attacked. Colonel Starbottle insists that he was thrown by the mustang he rode after leaving the Ramierez fonda, but his uneasy response to questions about choking leaves Mr. Grey curious. Richards investigates the fonda and is himself nearly strangled while watching the road, apparently by an unseen assailant. His encounter renews Mr. Grey's concern about the Ramierez family and the identity of a fair-skinned girl seen at the fonda.

records.l: Mountain Clarion, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: The Mountain Clarion has already printed a report on Colonel Starbottle's accident and an editorial about the dangers of riding half-broken Spanish mustangs. Mr. Grey decides that it will not publish speculation about Colonel Starbottle's secret without his permission.

records.l: Mr. Grey, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Mr. Grey is the editor of the Mountain Clarion. He questions Colonel Starbottle about the accident, discourages Richards from handling the matter privately, and considers investigating the Ramierez family and the girl seen at the fonda.

records.l: Richards, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Richards, the Mountain Clarion's foreman and acting pressman, suspects that Colonel Starbottle was attacked rather than injured in an accident. While investigating the Ramierez fonda, Richards is seized from behind and nearly strangled, then resolves to handle the matter himself rather than call the sheriff.

records.l: Colonel Starbottle, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Colonel Starbottle says he was thrown when a mustang bolted and buck-jumped after he left the Ramierez rancho. He denies being attacked, but becomes uneasy when Mr. Grey mentions that some people believe he was strangled with a lasso.

records.l: Ramierez, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Ramierez keeps a fonda or hostelry on a small estate where gambling takes place. Richards and others suspect that Ramierez or people connected with him may have been involved in violence near the fonda, although the text does not establish this.

records.l: Senora Ramierez, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Senora Ramierez is described as a woman with coquettish behavior and considerable physical charms. Colonel Starbottle says that after playful badinage she offered him the use of her daughter's mustang.

records.l: Cota Ramierez, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: The Ramierez daughter is described by Richards as a very pretty, fair-skinned girl of about fourteen, with blue eyes, dark reddish hair in a long braid, and a sing-song voice. She briefly appears at the fonda and is hurried out of the room.

records.l: the Ramierez fonda, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: The Ramierez fonda is a hostelry where gambling occurs and aguardiente is sold. Richards visits it while investigating possible attacks on people leaving with gambling winnings and sees the Ramierez daughter there.

records.l: public road near the fonda, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Colonel Starbottle says he was thrown four or five hundred yards from the Ramierez fonda, on or near the road. Richards waits along the road near a corral and is nearly strangled by an unseen attacker.

records.l: corral near the fonda, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: The corral is about a hundred yards down the road from the fonda, with a half-adobe wall and a palm-stockade top. Richards watches through an opening in it and is seized against the stockade by an unseen assailant.

records.l: Colonel Starbottle's accident, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Colonel Starbottle reports that his horse bolted and buck-jumped, throwing him and causing his injuries. His account is questioned because his neck, nose, and ear reportedly showed signs that could be consistent with a struggle.

records.l: the assault on Richards and Colonel Starbottle, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Some people believe Colonel Starbottle was dragged from his horse and choked rather than merely thrown. The text does not determine whether an attack occurred, though the colonel admits that he experienced a sensation of choking.

records.l: attack on Richards, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Richards is grabbed from behind while watching near the corral, and his coat collar and neck-handkerchief are drawn tightly around his throat. He nearly loses consciousness before his collar button breaks and frees him; he sees no attacker.

records.l: investigation of Starbottle's accident, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Mr. Grey questions Colonel Starbottle directly and learns that the colonel attributes his injuries to a fall from the mustang. Richards independently investigates the Ramierez fonda, but his near-strangulation produces no clear identification of the person responsible.

records.l: Colonel Starbottle's mustang, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: The mustang belonged to the Ramierez family and was offered to Colonel Starbottle by Senora Ramierez as a mount for his ride home. Colonel Starbottle says it bolted and buck-jumped before throwing him.

records.l: lasso, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: The foreman suggests that Colonel Starbottle might have been dragged from his horse and choked with a lasso. Colonel Starbottle reacts uneasily when Mr. Grey mentions this theory.

records.l: black silk neck-handkerchief, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: When Colonel Starbottle was found, his black silk neck-handkerchief was reportedly pulled tight around his throat. The colonel explains the choking sensation by saying that his cravat twisted during the fall and his rolling.

records.l: anti-Mexican prejudice, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: The foreman repeats the local prejudice that Mexicans, whom he calls 'Greasers,' are a bad lot. Mr. Grey recognizes this as provincial prejudice and objects to treating the Mountain Clarion as unbiased by making the Ramierez family its sole target.

records.l: Colonel Starbottle's secret, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: Mr. Grey promises not to publish Colonel Starbottle's secret without his permission. Colonel Starbottle denies that he is concealing the true cause of the accident and asks that none of the discussion about the Ramierez family appear in the paper.

records.l: newspaper reporting, From Sand Hill to Pine, WHAT HAPPENED AT THE FONDA PART I "Well!
records.s: The Mountain Clarion has reported the accident and is urged by Richards to investigate rumors of foul play. Mr. Grey agrees to make inquiries but refuses to publish unverified claims or Colonel Starbottle's private information.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II The next afternoon he went to the fonda.
records.s: Mr. Grey visits Ramierez's fonda to investigate the assault on Richards and Colonel Starbottle, but learns nothing useful about the assailants. He meets Ramierez's daughter, Cota, who returns from riding a distinctive pinto mustang. In a playful contest, Grey mounts the mustang and uses his spurs to stop its attempts to throw him, though the animal is injured. Cota then tricks Grey into the stable, and he leaves without solving the assault.

records.l: Mr. Grey, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II The next afternoon he went to the fonda.
records.s: Mr. Grey visits the fonda to investigate the assault on Richards and Colonel Starbottle. He meets Cota, accepts her challenge involving the mustang, and uses his riding skill and spurs to stop the animal from throwing him. He later escapes Cota's playful but unsettling behavior and returns home without useful information.

records.l: Ramierez, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II The next afternoon he went to the fonda.
records.s: Ramierez, the round-whiskered proprietor of the fonda and tienda, welcomes Mr. Grey with perfunctory urbanity. He warns Grey that Cota's invitation to ride the mustang is a trick and says that the old vaquero is dangerous only to bulls and wild horses.

records.l: Senora Ramierez, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II The next afternoon he went to the fonda.
records.s: Senora Ramierez welcomes Mr. Grey and tells him that Cota has recently returned from four years at the convent in San Jose. She explains that Cota cares chiefly for riding and leads Grey outside to see her daughter and the horse.

records.l: Cota Ramierez, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II The next afternoon he went to the fonda.
records.s: Cota rides her pinto mustang bareback and approaches Mr. Grey on foot after stopping at a distance. She playfully challenges him, traps him briefly in the stable, and apologizes after claiming she feared the horse might have kicked him. She regards Grey as strong because he understands how to handle the mustang.

records.l: the Ramierez fonda, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II The next afternoon he went to the fonda.
records.s: The fonda occupies a former hacienda on the outskirts of the town. Its old patio serves as a stable-yard, one wing is an open veranda, and the opposite wing operates as Ramierez's tienda.

records.l: daughter's mustang, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II The next afternoon he went to the fonda.
records.s: Cota's mustang is a half-broken pinto, or calico horse, mottled in lavender and pink, Arabian in proportions, and similar to Cota in its unusual appearance and expression. When Grey mounts it, the mustang repeatedly leaps in an attempt to throw him, but his spurs force it to stop, leaving scarifying tracks along its sides.

records.l: the assault on Richards and Colonel Starbottle, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II The next afternoon he went to the fonda.
records.s: The assault on Richards and Colonel Starbottle remains unexplained in this unit. Mr. Grey's visit to the fonda is intended in part to discover who attacked them.

records.l: Grey's riding contest with Cota's mustang, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II The next afternoon he went to the fonda.
records.s: Grey accepts Cota's implied riding challenge and mounts her unprepared mustang without taking hold of its mane. He counters the animal's leaps by using his American spurs, eventually dismounting after the mustang stands still and trembles.

records.l: investigation of Starbottle's accident, From Sand Hill to Pine, PART II The next afternoon he went to the fonda.
records.s: Mr. Grey questions Ramierez about suspicious loiterers and possible disturbances at the fonda, but Ramierez knows of none. The search produces no result, and Grey rides home empty of information.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: Mr. Grey learns from Enriquez Saltillo about a Spanish-California legend involving Friar Pedro, a lasso, and a spirit horse that strangles people. Richards then reveals that the mysterious assailants were actually Cota Ramierez's pinto horse, which attacked both Colonel Starbottle and Richards before Richards shot and killed it. Cota is furious with Richards for killing the horse and leaves for San Jose, ending their relationship. Grey abandons his plan to publish the incidents as sensational stories in the Clarion because Richards's involvement is private.

records.l: Mr. Grey, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: Mr. Grey discovers that Richards has developed a sincere passion for Cota Ramierez and becomes concerned about her apparent flirtation with him. He hears Enriquez Saltillo's lasso legend and plans to use it as newspaper material, but abandons the idea after Richards reveals the true identity of the assailant.

records.l: Cota Ramierez, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: Cota visits the composing-room at Richards's invitation and shows simple, childish curiosity about printing while also directing meaningful looks and an audacious kiss toward Mr. Grey. She is furious when Richards kills her pinto horse, leaves for San Jose, and ends her relationship with Richards.

records.l: Richards, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: Richards invites Cota to the composing-room, displays his printing work, and falls sincerely in love with her. He later reveals that he was the unnamed rider attacked by Cota's pinto horse and that he shot and killed it, after which Cota rejected him.

records.l: Enriquez Saltillo, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: Enriquez Saltillo tells Mr. Grey that the mysterious attacks may be connected to an old legend about a Spanish friar condemned to return as a spirit and swing a lasso. He says that the legend is known among his people but does not clearly state whether he believes it.

records.l: Colonel Starbottle, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: Colonel Starbottle was previously attacked near the Ramierez fonda and narrowly escaped being strangled. Richards identifies his attacker as Cota's pinto horse.

records.l: Friar Pedro, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: Friar Pedro is the padre in Enriquez Saltillo's legend who throws a lasso at a fleeing young woman. He is dragged away when the woman proves to be the devil and is condemned to return yearly as a spirit.

records.l: daughter's mustang, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: Cota's pinto horse attacks Colonel Starbottle and Richards by seizing them from behind and gripping their clothing or neckwear in its teeth. Richards shoots it twice in the neck, killing it, and Cota becomes furious with him.

records.l: the Ramierez fonda, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: The Ramierez fonda is associated with Cota, her family, and the attacks on Colonel Starbottle and Richards. Mr. Grey also recalls a strange scuffle outside its stable door.

records.l: Mountain Clarion, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: The Clarion is the newspaper edited by Mr. Grey, whose exchanges Enriquez Saltillo reads in the office. Richards's revelation prevents the Clarion from publishing the real account of the attacks.

records.l: the padres, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: The padres in Enriquez Saltillo's account seek to convert the heathen and save their souls. They use soldiers and lassos to capture those who flee or resist conversion.

records.l: the heathen, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: The heathen in Enriquez Saltillo's legend resist conversion, flee from the padres and soldiers, or backslide after conversion. One young woman escapes the soldiers but is pursued with a lasso by Friar Pedro.

records.l: Colonel Starbottle's accident, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: The mysterious attacks on Colonel Starbottle and Richards initially appear to be the work of an unknown human or supernatural assailant. Richards explains that both attacks were carried out by Cota's pinto horse.

records.l: Richards's second attack, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: During Richards's second attack, Cota's pinto horse seizes him from behind and half chokes him after throwing him from its back. Richards fires two shots under his arm and discovers that the dead horse is still gripping his coat collar and neckerchief in its teeth.

records.l: the assault on Richards and Colonel Starbottle, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: The pinto horse's attack on Starbottle is described as an assault from behind that nearly results in strangulation. Richards identifies it as the same horse that later attacks him.

records.l: the lasso legend, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: The lasso legend recounts how Friar Pedro tried to capture a fleeing young woman, who was actually the devil, and was dragged away with her. The legend says that Friar Pedro must return each year as a spirit and lasso whoever he can.

records.l: the lasso, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: In the legend, the lasso is used by soldiers and Friar Pedro to capture people who flee from conversion. Friar Pedro's lasso catches the devil in the form of a young woman but causes him to be dragged away.

records.l: the Clarion's sensational story, From Sand Hill to Pine, He was still more concerned a week later, on returning unexpectedly one afternoo
records.s: Mr. Grey considers turning the lasso legend and its apparent connection to the attacks into sensational copy for the Clarion. The story is not published because Richards says the actual incident is his private secret and cannot be used.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: Ned Bray of the Eureka Mining Company fetches water from a spring on a brutally hot Sierran foothill. At the spring, Eugenia Neworth falls from the stage road and lands on Bray, who regains consciousness, rescues her from the ledge, and helps her climb back to the road. Bray and Eugenia compare their linked escape to Jack and Jill, while her family searches for and retrieves her. Eugenia thanks Bray despite her relatives’ condescension toward him.

records.l: Edward Bray, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: Ned Bray volunteers to fetch water for the Eureka Mining Company when the tin pail is empty. At the spring, he is knocked unconscious when Eugenia falls onto him, then rescues her from the ledge and escorts her along the rocky trail to the stage road.

records.l: Eugenia Neworth, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: Eugenia Neworth leaves the coach to walk uphill beside the stage road, slips, and falls to the spring below. Bray rescues her, and she returns to the road with his help before thanking him formally despite her family’s dismissive attitude toward him.

records.l: Eureka Mining Company, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: The Eureka Mining Company has five members working on the Sierran foothill. Its members shelter from the heat beneath a pine tree and use dice to decide who must fetch water when their supply runs out.

records.l: Sierran foothill, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: The Sierran foothill is intensely hot, dry, and covered with pine crests, glaring quartz, heated rocks, and steep drops. The Eureka Mining Company works on an exposed ledge there, while the spring lies on the mountainside below the stage road.

records.l: the spring, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: The spring is a cold stream in a niche of the mountainside with a ledge less than four feet wide. Bray reaches it to fill the tin pail, cool himself, and recover after Eugenia falls onto him.

records.l: stage road, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: The stage road curves around the mountain above the spring and is covered with fine, heavy red dust. Eugenia falls from its bank, and Bray later helps her climb back to it.

records.l: rocky trail, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: The rocky trail descends from the mining camp toward the stage road and continues along the mountainside to the spring. Its lower section is narrow and precipitous, with a misstep threatening a fall into the pine trees far below.

records.l: the pail, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: The tin pail is empty at the mining camp, prompting the men to decide who will fetch water. Bray carries it to the spring and fills it, later using it to give Eugenia a drink.

records.l: water, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: Water from the spring cools Bray’s wrists, head, shoulders, shoes, and ankles after his hot journey. He offers it to Eugenia and holds the filled pail to her lips so she can drink.

records.l: bandanna silk handkerchief, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: Bray unties the bandanna silk handkerchief from his shoulders and knots one end to his belt and the other to Eugenia’s leather belt. It links them as they cross the dangerous trail together.

records.l: Jack and Jill, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: Bray compares his water-fetching journey and Eugenia’s fall to Jack and Jill. Eugenia later repeats the comparison, saying it would truly fit because they would both fall if she fell while they were linked.

records.l: the water-fetching journey, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: The water-fetching journey takes Bray from the mining camp down the rocky trail, across the dusty stage road, and along a perilous path to the spring. He returns with Eugenia instead of simply carrying the water back alone.

records.l: Eugenia's accident, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: Eugenia's fall begins when she slips near the bank of the stage road while walking uphill. She lands on Bray at the spring, nearly slides over the ledge, and suffers no serious injury beyond the shock and damage to her dust-cloak.

records.l: Bray's rescue of Eugenia, From Sand Hill to Pine, '" A JACK AND JILL OF THE SIERRAS It was four o'clock in the afternoon, and the hottest hour of the day on that Sierran foothill.
records.s: Bray regains consciousness beneath Eugenia, pulls her body back from the brink, and helps her recover with water. He then links her to himself with his handkerchief and supports her along the trail until they reach the stage road.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, And with it came the dreadful reflection that as yet he had not carried the wate
records.s: Bray realizes that he has forgotten to carry water to his thirsty comrades and hurries down the trail to the spring. At the spring, he lingers because the place reminds him of the girl and searches for something she may have left behind. He fills the pail while reflecting on his appearance, his feelings for the girl, and her earlier remark. Bray struggles back up the trail with the water and leaves the spring and its brief idyll behind.

records.l: Edward Bray, From Sand Hill to Pine, And with it came the dreadful reflection that as yet he had not carried the wate
records.s: Bray realizes that he has neglected to carry water to his expecting and thirsty comrades. He hurries to the spring, lingers while thinking about the girl, fills the pail, and returns up the trail tired but insisting that he is not in love.

records.l: Eugenia Neworth, From Sand Hill to Pine, And with it came the dreadful reflection that as yet he had not carried the wate
records.s: The girl is absent from the spring, and Bray looks for any trace she may have left, such as a bow, ribbon, or hairpin. Bray remembers her reply to his badinage and finds several flattering interpretations of it.

records.l: rocky trail, From Sand Hill to Pine, And with it came the dreadful reflection that as yet he had not carried the wate
records.s: Bray hastens recklessly down the trail to the spring and later makes the difficult climb back up it while carrying the pail.

records.l: the spring, From Sand Hill to Pine, And with it came the dreadful reflection that as yet he had not carried the wate
records.s: The spring has become hallowed to Bray because of the girl's presence there. He notices how deserted it looks without her, sees his reflection in it, fills the pail there, and then leaves it behind.

records.l: water, From Sand Hill to Pine, And with it came the dreadful reflection that as yet he had not carried the wate
records.s: The water is needed by Bray's expecting and thirsty comrades. Bray has forgotten to carry it at first, then returns to the spring and brings it back in the pail.

records.l: the pail, From Sand Hill to Pine, And with it came the dreadful reflection that as yet he had not carried the wate
records.s: Bray slowly fills the pail at the spring and carries it back up the trail. He finds the climb difficult because the pail is insensible and is carried in the hand that once supported the girl.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Edward Bray returns to the Eureka Company camp and learns that Neworth's visit to inspect the claim was abandoned after Eugenia's accident delayed him. The next day Parkhurst discovers gold-bearing quartz near the spring, and the five mining partners quickly locate and begin working a new mining claim there. Parkhurst later gives Bray Eugenia's note, addressed to "Jack," which uses a gill-to-quart pun to indicate quartz and reveals that she remembered him.

records.l: Edward Bray, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Edward Bray feels responsible for ruining the capitalist's visit because his delay and dalliance with Eugenia held up Neworth. He returns to the spring hoping to see Eugenia once more, then becomes deeply agitated when Parkhurst discovers gold there and secretly gives him Eugenia's note.

records.l: Parkhurst, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Parkhurst attributes Neworth's failure to visit the claim to the women accompanying him and later discovers gold-bearing quartz near the spring. He finds Eugenia's note addressed to "Jack," interprets "Jill" as a measure of whiskey, and gives the note and a laurel sprig to Bray after explaining his quartz riddle.

records.l: Eugenia Neworth, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Eugenia falls down a ravine near the spring while visiting the area with Neworth and another woman. She later leaves a note for Parkhurst, signed as a reference to "Jill," expressing respect for his honest, manly calling and hoping he will think of her when he strikes it rich.

records.l: Eugenia's father, Mr. Neworth, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Neworth, a San Francisco capitalist, visits the area from Red Dog to examine the mining claim for possible investment. His visit is interrupted when Eugenia falls, and he proceeds to Sacramento without examining the claim.

records.l: foreman of the Eureka Mining Company, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: The foreman had persuaded Neworth to visit the claim and had engineered the proposed investment affair. He later leads the partners to work the newly discovered ground near the spring.

records.l: the five mining partners, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: The five mining partners are initially disappointed when Neworth fails to examine their claim. After Parkhurst's discovery, they hurry to the spring, stake the ground, work the hillside, and find a major strike.

records.l: Eureka Mining Company, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: The Eureka Company has a burning ledge beside the stage road where the partners work. Its ledge is left behind when the partners move their prospecting efforts to the spring.

records.l: Eureka ledge, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: The Eureka Company claim is the mining property that Neworth intended to inspect for possible investment. The spring is not on this claim, so the partners must formally locate the newly discovered ground.

records.l: Eureka mountain, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: The summit is near the spring and the Eureka Company camp, and Neworth's son and the two women stay there for a day or two after Neworth leaves. The women are scheduled to leave the summit for Sacramento.

records.l: the stage road, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: The stage road runs past the Eureka Company ledge and the spring. It is deserted when Bray goes for water, and later passengers see the newly posted Notice of Location beside it.

records.l: the spring, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: The spring is initially an unremarkable niche in the mountainside. Parkhurst finds a landslide, a crack, and gold-bearing decomposed quartz near it, after which the partners work and stake the surrounding ground.

records.l: the capitalist's visit and investment negotiations, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Neworth's proposed visit is intended to lead to an advance and investment in the Eureka Company claim. Eugenia's accident delays him until he must leave for Sacramento, ending the examination and apparently preventing an immediate renewal of negotiations.

records.l: Eugenia's accident, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Eugenia gets off the coach and wanders near the spring before falling down a ravine. Her fall delays Neworth, and the track made by it later helps Parkhurst identify disturbed ground containing quartz and gold.

records.l: the strike on Eureka mountain, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Parkhurst discovers gold in a pocket of decomposed quartz near the spring after widening a crack with his clasp knife. The partners prospect the area and determine that the discovery is a major strike.

records.l: the mining claim at the spring, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: The mining claim at the spring is located by the partners after Parkhurst's discovery. They post a Notice of Location and begin excavating and testing the ground, although the spring was known to others and the validity of their work is initially uncertain.

records.l: the gold, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Gold is found in a small pocket of decomposed quartz near the spring. Further prospecting reveals enough gold and promise to exceed the partners' most hopeful expectations.

records.l: quartz, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Quartz is found near the spring in decomposed form and throughout the seepage beneath the hillside. Parkhurst connects the word "quartz" to Eugenia's note through the sequence gills, pints, and quarts.

records.l: water, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Water is scarce and valuable at the mining camp, and the partners' water-carrying duties require hard work. The spring's past or present water action appears to have caused erosion and exposed the quartz and gold.

records.l: the Notice of Location, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: The partners pin a Notice of Location to a pine by the road bank beside the spring. Stage passengers see the notice when the coach passes that afternoon.

records.l: Eugenia's note to Parkhurst, From Sand Hill to Pine, By this time the sun had left the burning ledge of the Eureka Company, and the s
records.s: Eugenia's note is addressed on the back to "Jack" and says, "I want you to believe that I, at least, respect and honor your honest, manly calling, and when you strike it rich, as you surely will, I hope you will sometimes think of Jill." Parkhurst mistakes "Jill" for a reference to a gill of whiskey, while Bray recognizes it as Eugenia's remembrance of him and uses the note to explain the quartz discovery.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: Edmund Bray travels to San Francisco to thank Eugenia Neworth for her note and explain why he did not answer it sooner. After Eugenia initially treats him coldly, Bray enters the Neworths' garden by climbing the wall, and they clarify the misunderstandings surrounding her note and its delivery to the spring. Eugenia then directs Bray to call properly on her father, who is interested in the mines on Eureka ledge. Bray continues visiting San Francisco and eventually enters a new partnership with Eugenia, whom he says made the first strike on Eureka mountain.

records.l: Edward Bray, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: Edmund Bray goes to San Francisco intending to seek Eugenia Neworth and thank her for her note. After Eugenia initially passes him coldly, he sends her note back with an explanation, then climbs into the Neworths' garden to speak with her. He later calls properly at the Neworth residence, visits repeatedly, and eventually enters a new partnership with Eugenia.

records.l: Eugenia Neworth, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: Eugenia Neworth wrote the note that Bray found at the spring and arranged for a schoolboy to deliver it and wait until Bray claimed it. She explains that she expected Bray to acknowledge the note and later invites him to call on her properly. She and Bray resolve their misunderstanding, and she becomes his new partner.

records.l: the Neworth family, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: The Neworth family lives in a palatial residence on Rincon Hill in San Francisco, with a garden protected by a high wall. Their earlier discourtesy toward Bray makes him hesitate before approaching the house.

records.l: Eugenia's father, Mr. Neworth, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: Eugenia's father is a well-known investor who regrets not becoming better acquainted with Bray during their brief earlier interview. He is exceedingly interested in the mines on Eureka ledge and is willing to receive Bray when Bray calls at the house.

records.l: San Francisco, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: San Francisco is where Eugenia lives with her family and where Bray goes to seek her. Bray visits the city frequently after their meeting and eventually does not return to his old partners.

records.l: Eureka mountain, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: Eureka mountain is the place associated with Bray's mining activities and with his earlier meeting with Eugenia. Bray later says that Eugenia made the first strike on Eureka mountain.

records.l: Eureka ledge, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: Eureka ledge contains mines in which Eugenia's father is exceedingly interested. Bray's affairs include purchasing machinery for a new claim connected with his mining work.

records.l: the spring, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: The spring is where Eugenia had a schoolboy leave her note for Bray. Bray went there for water, but failed to notice the note while searching around the mountain, and one of his partners found it instead.

records.l: Eugenia's note to Parkhurst, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: Eugenia's note was intended for Bray and was left at the spring by a schoolboy instructed to wait until Bray arrived. Bray did not see it because he was searching elsewhere, and he later returns it to Eugenia with thanks and an explanation for his delayed acknowledgment.

records.l: Bray's mining claim, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: Bray is arranging the purchase of machinery for his new mining claim. His mining affairs provide him with a possible means of gaining access to Eugenia's father.

records.l: Bray and Eugenia's new partnership, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: After Bray makes repeated visits to San Francisco, he enters into a new partnership with Eugenia. He says that she made the first strike on Eureka mountain.

records.l: the strike on Eureka mountain, From Sand Hill to Pine, That night Bray slept but little.
records.s: The strike on Eureka mountain is credited by Bray to Eugenia, who made the first strike. This description marks her as the partner who initiated the new partnership's opportunity.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: After Joshua Bilson’s wife dies, he hires Miss Euphemia Trotter as housekeeper at the Summit House in Buckeye Hill, where her competence and severity make her respected and feared. Trotter, a poor and highly experienced working woman, nurses Chris Calton after he fractures his arm and collar-bone, while Calton becomes interested in the gentler chambermaid Frida Pauline Jansen. Frida’s attention helps Calton’s spirits during his recovery, and he returns to Roanoke Ledge after improving. He sends Trotter a valuable watch and chain in gratitude, while the nature of his gifts to Frida remains undisclosed.

records.l: Mr. Bilson, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: Joshua Bilson, of the Summit House, loses his wife and hires Miss Euphemia Trotter to manage the hotel with him. He stands in awe of Trotter, speaks of her with respect and reverence, and later is found in the card-room with Frida Pauline Jansen, offering an embarrassed and unconvincing explanation.

records.l: the Summit Hotel, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: The Summit House employs Miss Euphemia Trotter as housekeeper and receives Chris Calton as a patient after his injury. Calton convalesces there under medical supervision and Trotter’s care before returning to Roanoke Ledge.

records.l: Buckeye Hill, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: Buckeye Hill expects Joshua Bilson’s housekeeper to become his next wife, but is startled when he selects the serious, middle-aged, highly competent Miss Euphemia Trotter instead. The community respects and fears Trotter’s management of the hotel.

records.l: Miss Trotter, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: Miss Euphemia Trotter is a poor, hardworking woman who has been a teacher, hospital nurse, and reformatory assistant. As housekeeper, she supervises servants, examines bills and stores, and manages the Summit House with precision and authority. She nurses Chris Calton competently, adjusts his bandages, overlooks his interest in Frida Pauline Jansen, and receives a watch and chain from him in gratitude.

records.l: housekeeper employment, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: After his wife’s death, Joshua Bilson takes Miss Euphemia Trotter into the Summit House as housekeeper. Her employment is understood by the community as a practical appointment rather than a step toward marriage, and her work makes her respected, feared, and apparently influential over Bilson.

records.l: Frida Pauline Jansen, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: Frida Pauline Jansen is a pretty Swedish chambermaid at the Summit House. Miss Trotter sees her embracing an unfamiliar young man in the woods, and Frida later attends Chris Calton with gentleness and sympathy, receiving his admiration and apparently undisclosed gifts. She is also seen entering the gentlemen’s card-room, where Joshua Bilson is present.

records.l: Chris Calton, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: Chris Calton, a twenty-six-year-old partner in the Roanoke Ledge, is brought to the Summit House after fracturing his arm and collar-bone. He is emotional and initially despondent, but becomes especially appreciative of Frida Pauline Jansen’s gentleness and beauty. After recovering, he returns to Roanoke Ledge and sends Miss Trotter a watch and chain with a note of gratitude.

records.l: Dr. Duchesne, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: Dr. Duchesne directs Chris Calton’s treatment and asks Miss Euphemia Trotter to ensure that Calton eats properly, avoids excitement and worry, remains hopeful, and keeps his injured parts immobile. He praises Trotter’s nursing ability and believes she is largely responsible for Calton’s improvement, though he mistakenly interprets her look as suggesting that Calton is in love with her.

records.l: Calton's injury, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: Chris Calton fractures his arm and collar-bone in a fall. The injury is not comminuted, and Dr. Duchesne considers his constitution and blood healthy; the prescribed care consists of rest, proper food, limited company, emotional calm, and absolute immobility of the injured parts.

records.l: Calton's recovery, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: Chris Calton initially suffers despondency but later shows improved spirits and then sustained physical improvement. His bandages cause little trouble by the end of his stay, and he leaves the Summit House as a convalescent man to return to Roanoke Ledge.

records.l: medical nursing and convalescence, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: Miss Euphemia Trotter applies her previous hospital experience to Chris Calton’s care, following Dr. Duchesne’s directions and eventually replacing his splints herself when the surgeon fails to appear. Her precise nursing, together with rest and controlled company, supports Calton’s recovery at the Summit House.

records.l: romantic relationships and marriage, From Sand Hill to Pine, Mr. Bilson's Housekeeper
records.s: Buckeye Hill assumes that Bilson’s housekeeper will eventually become his wife, but Miss Euphemia Trotter shows no interest in that role. Frida Pauline Jansen is seen embracing an unidentified young man and later attracts Chris Calton’s admiration; the text also places Frida with Joshua Bilson in the card-room, but does not establish the nature of either relationship.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: Jim Calton visits Miss Trotter to object to his brother Chris's engagement to Frida Jansen, arguing that Frida seeks Chris's wealth and is an unsuitable match. Miss Trotter rejects Jim's attempt to make her interfere, but later agrees to speak with Frida after Chris asks for her help. In the Summit woods, Chris sees Frida with Mr. Bilson and returns changed, releasing Miss Trotter from her promise after discovering her faithlessness. Mr. Bilson then tells Miss Trotter that he and Frida will marry, while Chris leaves without revealing the discovery to his brother.

records.l: Miss Trotter, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: Miss Trotter tells Jim Calton that she has no right to interfere with a guest's matrimonial intentions and refuses to condemn Frida's conduct without evidence that Frida has harmed her reputation. She agrees to speak with Frida at Chris's request, then discovers Frida with Mr. Bilson in the Summit woods. Although Mr. Bilson's marriage announcement will promote her to full control of the hotel, she feels troubled that her material success is connected with Chris's disappointment.

records.l: Chris Calton, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: Chris asks Miss Trotter to help preserve his relationship with Frida and promises not to see Frida until Miss Trotter has spoken with her. He goes to Frida before Miss Trotter can do so, discovers her with Mr. Bilson, and returns pale and changed, releasing Miss Trotter from her promise. He accepts his loss quietly and does not tell Jim what he has learned.

records.l: Jim Calton (Chris's elder brother), From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: Jim visits Miss Trotter to oppose Chris's engagement to Frida, whom he considers an ignorant foreign servant seeking Chris's money. He believes Miss Trotter should control the girls' conduct and asks her to question Frida about what she expects from the marriage. Miss Trotter's reasoning leaves him discomfited, though he admires her clear-sightedness.

records.l: Frida Pauline Jansen, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: Frida is a yellow-haired foreigner employed at the hotel who has become engaged to Chris. In the Summit woods she is seen emerging from the pine grove with Mr. Bilson, displaying conscious, gratified vanity; Chris's discovery indicates that she has been unfaithful to him or was pursuing Mr. Bilson as well.

records.l: Mr. Bilson, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: Mr. Bilson is the proprietor of the hotel and is found privately with Frida in the Summit woods. He tells Miss Trotter that he intends to marry Frida in San Francisco and that their marriage will not diminish Miss Trotter's position, but will promote her to entire control of the establishment. He and Frida plan to go abroad after the wedding.

records.l: the Summit Hotel, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: The hotel employs Frida and places Miss Trotter in charge of ensuring that the girls perform their duties. After Mr. Bilson's marriage to Frida, Miss Trotter is to receive entire control of the establishment while the couple travels abroad.

records.l: Summit woods, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: The Summit woods are the setting for Miss Trotter's walk, her conversation with Chris, and Chris's discovery of Frida with Mr. Bilson. The woods recall Miss Trotter's earlier observations of Frida's flirtations and become the place where Chris learns of Frida's faithlessness.

records.l: Frida and Chris's engagement, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: Jim opposes Frida and Chris's engagement because he considers Frida unsuitable and suspects that she wants Chris's wealth. Chris asks Miss Trotter to help him maintain the engagement, but the engagement effectively collapses after he sees Frida with Mr. Bilson.

records.l: the marriage of Mr. Bilson and Frida, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: Mr. Bilson informs Miss Trotter that he and Frida will marry at once in San Francisco and then travel abroad for a year or two. Their marriage is presented as the outcome of Frida's relationship with Mr. Bilson and the cause of Chris's disappointment.

records.l: Chris's discovery of Frida's faithlessness, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: Chris discovers Frida with Mr. Bilson in the pine grove after going ahead to speak with her. He returns pale, older-looking, and emotionally controlled, refuses to explain what happened, and releases Miss Trotter from her promise to intervene.

records.l: marriage and romantic attachment, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: The unit contrasts Chris's sincere romantic attachment to Frida with Frida's apparent attachment to Mr. Bilson and the practical consequences of marriage. Miss Trotter reflects that Chris has been spared an ill-assorted marriage, while her own interest in him deepens only after his romantic defeat.

records.l: interference in the engagement, From Sand Hill to Pine, II One afternoon Miss Trotter received a message that Mr.
records.s: Jim asks Miss Trotter to interfere in Chris and Frida's engagement, but she argues that she has no authority over their personal intentions. Chris later voluntarily asks her to speak with Frida, though his discovery of Frida with Mr. Bilson makes her intervention unnecessary.

records.l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, III When the news of the marriage reached Buckeye Hill, it did not, however, make much scandal, owing, possibly, to the scant number of the sex who are apt to disseminate it, and to many the name of Miss Jansen was unknown.
records.s: The news of Mr. Bilson’s marriage to Frida causes little scandal at Buckeye Hill, but Miss Trotter’s assumption of control of the Summit Hotel creates a stir. Chris Calton returns to the hotel after an illness and relapse, confesses that he never loved Frida, and declares his love for Miss Trotter. Miss Trotter resigns, leaves the Summit House, and later encounters Baroness X. at a foreign Spa, where she learns that Frida is now Mrs. Chris Calton. Miss Trotter leaves the Spa before Chris can return, and the nature of her relationship with him remains unresolved in the unit.

records.l: Miss Trotter, From Sand Hill to Pine, III When the news of the marriage reached Buckeye Hill, it did not, however, make much scandal, owing, possibly, to the scant number of the sex who are apt to disseminate it, and to many the name of Miss Jansen was unknown.
records.s: Miss Trotter becomes an independent woman of means and assumes superior control of the Summit Hotel while Mr. Bilson is absent. She learns that Chris Calton’s apparent courtship of Frida was a deception intended to provoke her attention, and he confesses his love to her. She later changes her dress and becomes less severe socially, resigns from the hotel, and leaves for a foreign Spa, where she avoids meeting Chris.

records.l: Chris Calton, From Sand Hill to Pine, III When the news of the marriage reached Buckeye Hill, it did not, however, make much scandal, owing, possibly, to the scant number of the sex who are apt to disseminate it, and to many the name of Miss Jansen was unknown.
records.s: Chris Calton returns to the Summit Hotel physically weakened after an illness and relapse. He explains to Miss Trotter that he never loved Frida, fabricated his apparent interest in her to gain Miss Trotter’s attention, and finally tells Miss Trotter that he loves her.

records.l: Jim Calton (Chris's elder brother), From Sand Hill to Pine, III When the news of the marriage reached Buckeye Hill, it did not, however, make much scandal, owing, possibly, to the scant number of the sex who are apt to disseminate it, and to many the name of Miss Jansen was unknown.
records.s: James Calton tells Miss Trotter that he believes her influence changed Chris and suggests that she see Chris while he is ill. He mistakenly implies that Chris may have transferred his affections to her, prompting Miss Trotter’s embarrassment.

records.l: Mr. Bilson, From Sand Hill to Pine, III When the news of the marriage reached Buckeye Hill, it did not, however, make much scandal, owing, possibly, to the scant number of the sex who are apt to disseminate it, and to many the name of Miss Jansen was unknown.
records.s: Mr. Bilson marries Frida and is absent from the Summit Hotel for a year. He later returns to take charge of the hotel after Miss Trotter resigns, and Miss Trotter sends him a letter addressed to Paris before that return.

records.l: Frida Pauline Jansen, From Sand Hill to Pine, III When the news of the marriage reached Buckeye Hill, it did not, however, make much scandal, owing, possibly, to the scant number of the sex who are apt to disseminate it, and to many the name of Miss Jansen was unknown.
records.s: Frida marries Mr. Bilson after Chris Calton’s apparent courtship of her ends. At the foreign Spa she is known as Mrs. Calton, having later married Chris Calton.
